<meta>This page continues the Kabbalistic exploration of language and divine essence, moving from the literal interpretation of Hebrew letters to the mystical concept of "Nothingness" (Ain) as a descriptor for God’s infinite nature.</meta>

# Languages of this Universe.

The representation of the essence of things was intended to be expressed through their proper names, no more and no less than a painting does through the strokes of lines and colors. This process is called resolving things into their primary elements, much as minerals, vegetables, and animals—being mixed and composed substances—are resolved by the actions and effects of fire. From this, one can then form a new mystical sense and intelligence that is hidden beneath the exterior of the speech. Upon this depends nearly all the artistry of the *Steganography* and *Polygraphy* <note>Johannes Trithemius (1462–1516) was a German Benedictine abbot and a pioneer in cryptography (Steganography) and hidden writing (Polygraphy), which he often framed in mystical terms.</note> of Abbot Trithemius, drawn from these Hebrew ciphers. This is seen in the transposition of letters, as in the names *Jehoiachin* and *Jechoniah*, which are the name of the same King, composed of the same letters but transposed. We shall also mention here another example of metathesis <note>Metathesis is the grammatical or mystical rearrangement of letters in a word to reveal deeper meanings.</note>, or the reversal of only two Hebrew letters which, when assembled differently, signify different things, not without great mystery: namely אל *EL* [God], and לא *LA* [No/Not]. It is as if one should understand from this that God is, in our regard, a negative and a privation rather than an affirmative, according to what we have already cited from Psalm 139:

> *As the darkness is, such is His light*, for darkness symbolizes privation. By this means, the most absolute Essence of God—retreating from our senses and apprehension into His infinite obscurity—is also called אין *Ain* [*Not* or *Nothing*], regarding that text from the 17th chapter of Exodus, according to the Hebrew truth: *Is the Lord a Being among us, or is He not a Being?* <note>Original Latin: "Num est Ens Adonai inter nos, an non Ens?" The author uses "Nun" in the text, likely an archaic form or typo for "Num," a Latin question particle.</note> Thus the Kabbalists cite from the 28th chapter of Job, *He Himself* איה <note>Hebrew: "Ayah," meaning "Where."</note> *knows the place thereof*, suggesting that Wisdom is found through privation, specifically from the place called *Ain* [Nothingness].

This aligns with the discussion in Plato’s dialogue *The Sophist*: "Outside of all things there is nothing, except nothingness itself; and yet the One cannot encompass anything except what is, unless by chance it environed nothingness." Furthermore, the *Treatise of Yetzirah* <note>The *Sefer Yetzirah* (Book of Formation) is one of the earliest extant books on Jewish esotericism, describing how the world was created through the Hebrew alphabet and the ten Sephiroth.</note> states that the ten *Sephiroth* <note>The Sephiroth are the ten attributes or emanations in Kabbalah through which the Infinite (Ein Sof) reveals itself.</note>, or divine emanations, proceed from the בלימה *Belimah* <note>Hebrew: "Without anything" or "Nothingness."</note>, which among other things signifies nothingness and privation. This is because the weakness of our spirit causes us to consider those things which we cannot reach or conceive, and which do not appear to us at all, as not existing; concerning which the Apostle says in 1 Corinthians:

> 1. *God has chosen the things that are not, to abolish those that are.* But Plato speaks even more clearly in his 6th Epistle to Hermias, Erastus, and Coriscus: *God is the head of all things, both of those that are, and of the others that must be and are not yet.* Also, this mark of nullity, 0, which is circular and revolves into itself without end or beginning, does nothing on its own; yet, with unity, it constitutes the number 10. From there, it goes on multiplying in the company of others unto infinity, as the great Archimedes demonstrates very well in his treatise *The Sand-Reckoner*. For as Saint Dionysius <note>Pseudo-Dionysius the Areopagite, a Christian mystic who emphasized "apophatic" or negative theology—defining God by what He is not.</note> puts it in his *Mystical Theology*: *God is neither number, nor one, nor unity; and in another place he says, we shall even dare to affirm, by reason, that what is not, participates in the good and the beautiful.*

Thus, this **NON-BEING** relates to God according to our capacity and perspective. Regarding Him, we may say with Simonides to King Hiero <note>Simonides of Ceos was a Greek poet who, when asked by King Hiero of Syracuse to define God, kept asking for more time because the longer he thought, the more obscure the answer became.</note> that the more one thinks of Him, the less one can understand what He is. It is much easier to apprehend that God is not the Heaven, nor the Sun, nor the Earth, nor any other thing that can fall not only under our sight, but even into our imagination and thought, than it is to affirm that He is this or that.

# History of the Origin of...

Wherefore, the more we think we approach Him to gain knowledge of Him, the more He flees and retreats, just as a shadow does from the body from which it proceeds when one thinks to run after it. All efforts, therefore, to reach Him through any reasoning or elevation of our spirits were vain and useless to us, before His <term>logos|The Greek word for "Word" or "Reason," used here to refer to the second person of the Trinity.</term>, or Word, which is perfect reason, came to communicate Himself to us by taking on the garment of our nature in human flesh. For no spiritual thing descending here below, as we have said, operates without a garment.

This is why the sacraments and mysteries, which are entirely spiritual matters of faith, have need of being accompanied by some material sign: as
> the <term>Cabalistes|Followers of Kabbalah, a Jewish mystical tradition that seeks to understand the relationship between the infinite God and the finite universe.</term> say within the *Gates of Justice* by <note>original: "Rabbi Ioseph fils de Carmitol." Likely a reference to Joseph Gikatilla (1248–1305), whose famous work is titled *Sha'are Orah* or "Gates of Light."</note> Rabbi Joseph, son of Carmitol: *The higher things stand in need of the help of the lower* <note>original Latin: "Superos indigere auxilio inferiorum." A fundamental Kabbalistic concept that human actions on earth affect the divine realms.</note>, regarding this: *Drop down dew, ye heavens, from above, and let the clouds rain down the Just One; let the earth open and bring forth a Savior, and let justice spring up together.* <note>Isaiah 45:8.</note>

But since the incarnation of the Word, the Divinity, instead of retreating from us as before, presents Himself on the contrary with arms extended and open to manifest Himself to us and to instill Himself into our Soul. All of this is here deduced for us in imitation of an invisible script, such as one can make with <term>alum|A chemical compound (potassium aluminum sulfate) used historically as a component in "sympathetic" or invisible ink.</term> steeped in water and various other artifices, which being dry becomes white like the paper, so that one would not think anything was marked there; but when moistened with water or heated by fire, the paper then becoming dark, the writing manifests itself. And so it is with the secret mysteries of God, which, in the manner of a very secret cipher, were greatly distanced from our knowledge until they were revealed to us by His Son, who is the true water of healthy wisdom, and the Holy Spirit, the fire of burning charity and love.

There are also other <term>Anagrammes|The practice of rearranging the letters of a word to discover hidden meanings, known in Hebrew as Temurah.</term> commonly in the Holy Hebrew Scripture, such as in חמר *Chamor* [Donkey], and רחם *Rechem* [Compassion or Gentleness] <note>The author notes that these words share the same Hebrew letters (R-CH-M) but in different orders. > Behold, your King will come for you, just and
> savior, humble and gentle, mounted upon a Donkey.

And there are several other Anagrams which I omit to avoid prolixity. Therefore, from the above, we shall learn that from two Hebrew letters the Kabbalists build two words or "Houses," as they say, whether these have meaning or not; from three letters, six words (as many as result from two and three folded into one another <note>The author is describing factorials (3! = 3x2x1 = 6). Above this, these Kabbalists command that we must contemplate what the mouth cannot speak nor the ear hear, both because one would go on to be engulfed in an abyss of the thousands and other numbers comprised in the infinity of the body of all figures.

## Of Anagrams CHAP. 15.

<image-desc>Decorative initial letter L with floral patterns and fruit within a square border.</image-desc>

<margin>cc</margin>
THE ANAGRAM is called by the Greeks <term>Anagrammatismos|Ἀναγραμματισμὸς</term>.
<margin>cc</margin>
It is a movement, transposition, or inversion of let-
<margin>cc</margin>
ters. "Those among us who desire to change their names know
<margin>cc</margin>
this figure," <note>original Latin: "Figuram hanc norunt apud nos qui se transnominare student."</note> as Suetonius says, "and to invert their own name,"
<margin>cc</margin>
as it is commonly called. A name or surname turned about: <term>Anagram-</term>
<margin>cc</margin>
<term>matismos and metagrammatismos involve a transposition of syllables and the</term>
<margin>cc</margin>
<term>removal and addition of letters</term> <note>original Greek: "Ἀναγραμματισμὸς καὶ μεταγραμματισμὸς μετάθεσίν ἔχει συλλαβῶν καὶ ἀποβολὴν καὶ πρόσθεσιν γραμμάτων."</note>. The anagram contains a transposition of syl-
lables and a mixing and addition of consonants or letters. This artifice
<margin>cc</margin>
first came and proceeded from the Hebrews mentioned above,
<margin>cc</margin>
as I have already said, and as Johann Reuchlin (Capnio) confirms
after the ancients in his books on the *Cabalistic Art*. An anagram is composed and arranged from certain names which one separates letter by letter, which are then rejoined and assembled into a new sense or context, under new words other than the first and preceding ones, to make a new assembly and composition that nevertheless possesses meaning and significance. The Greeks have written that in this subtlety of making anagrams among those of their nation and language, the poet Lycophron of Chalcis—one of the seven poets of the Pleiad—greatly excelled all other persons living in his time. THE ANAGRAM is called by the Greeks *Anagrammatismos* <note>original: Ἀναγραμματισμός</note>; it is a displacement, or transposition, or inversion of letters. <margin>cc</margin> *Those among us who study how to rename themselves know this figure,* <margin>cc</margin> as Suetonius says, *and to invert their name is what they commonly call it.* <note>original Latin: "Figuram hanc norunt apud nos qui se transnominare student, vt loquitur Suetonius, & nomen suum inuertere, vulgo id vocant."</note> A name or surname turned about: <margin>cc</margin> *Anagrammatismos and metagrammatismos involve the transposition of syllables and the removal and addition of letters.* <note>original Greek: Ἀναγραμματισμὸς καὶ μεταγραμματισμὸς μετάθεσίν ἔχει συλλαβῶν καὶ ἀποβολὴν καὶ πρόσθεσιν γραμμάτων.</note> <margin>cc</margin> The anagram contains a transposition of syllables and an insertion and addition of consonants or letters. This artifice <margin>cc</margin> originated and proceeded first from the Hebrews mentioned <margin>cc</margin> herein, as I have already said, and as Johannes Reuchlin Capnio <margin>cc</margin> confirms after the ancients in his books on the *Kabbalistic Art*. An anagram is composed and arranged from certain names which one separates letter by letter, which are then afterward joined and assembled into a new sense or context, under new words, different from the first and preceding ones, to make an assembly and composition that nevertheless possesses sense and meaning. The Greeks have written that in this subtlety of making anagrams among those of their nation and language, the poet Lycophron of Chalcis—one of the seven poets of the Pleiad <note>The "Pleiad" was a group of seven Alexandrian poets in the 3rd century BCE.</note>—greatly excelled above all other persons living in his time. Because of this, Ptolemy Philadelphus, King of Egypt, held him in high regard, and for this reason, he nicknamed him in Greek, by way of jesting, *metagrammatizomenos* <note>original: μεταγραμματιζόμενος, meaning "the letter-shifter" or "re-letterer."</note>, as the Greek interpreter of the said Lycophron reports quite particularly: *Lycophron dwelt there then, who was known as much for his poetry as...* <note>original Greek: ἐν δ' οἰκήσει δὲ τότε Λυκόφρων ὃν τοσοũτον διὰ τὴν ποίησιν, ὅσον. This fragment discusses Lycophron's reputation in the court of Ptolemy.</note>

the great antiquity of secret writing and ciphers, which undoubtedly first came from the Hebrews regarding these *Ziruphz* or *Tziruph* <note>original: "Ziruphz." From the Hebrew *Tziruph*, meaning "combinations" or "permutations" of letters used in Kabbalistic practice.</note>. On this subject, those who are curious enough to meditate on it at leisure will undoubtedly find several beautiful and excellent ways of writing in all languages. To avoid wordiness, we shall leave these specifically to their own curious research and mental dexterity; for this is the true root and foundation of all types of ciphers that proceed by way of transpositions and commutations of letters, whether they be single or double. However, this system is not here in its complete "square" form, but only half-complete—namely, the part on the right side moving toward the left, following the Hebrew way of writing. It does not follow the same order and sequence of letters, but rather another manner of pairing specific to the Kabbalists. They devised this for their own use, both for extracting divine names from certain passages of the Hebrew Scriptures and for investigating the internal sense hidden beneath the apparent and external context of the literal text. 

For example, the word מצפץ *Mazpaz* <note>original: "Mazpaz." In the Atbash cipher (where the first letter is swapped with the last, etc.), the letters of the Divine Name YHWH (יהוה) become MZPZ.</note> is attributed to the reign of David, called *Malchut* <term>Malchut: "Kingdom," the tenth and final Sephirot or divine attribute in the Kabbalah, often associated with the physical world and the Moon</term>, and consequently to the Messiah. Although it is not found in the Scriptures, it is nevertheless a cipher and symbol of the ineffable four-letter name יהוה <note>The Tetragrammaton: the sacred four-letter name of God.</note>. It is drawn from the *Ethbas* <note>Atbash: a substitution cipher where Aleph (1st letter) is replaced by Tav (22nd), Beth (2nd) by Shin (21st), and so on.</note>, or the 22nd and final Alphabet of *Ziruphs* and commutations. This can be seen here: where the מ (*Mem*) is put for the י (*Iod*); צ (*Tsadai*) for ה (*He*); פ (*Pe*) for ו (*Vau*); and צ (*Tsadai*) again for ה (*He*). 

This word is composed of *Maz*, which in the fifth and sixth order of Hebrew verb conjugations signifies "to suck or wring out" <note>original: "à succé & esprint"</note>. This is appropriate for *Malchut*, the *Sephirot* or numeration of the Moon, which receives all impressions from above in order to press and wring them out below. It is also composed of *Paz*, which in the first conjugation means as much as "to cry out and sing for joy," as it is written: 

> Lord, you shall open my lips, and my mouth shall announce your praise: Psalm 51. 

And in the second conjugation, it signifies to make an incision, to open, separate, wound, or deliver: *I will kill, and I will make to live: Deuteronomy 32.* <note>original Latin: "Ego occidam , & ego viuere faciam, Deuteron. 32."</note>

Regarding the first point, then, one only needs to reverse the pairings to make the system square and complete. For instance, where there is *Aleph* and *Lamed* joined together at the entry, turn them around and there will be *Lamed* and *Aleph*; and so on for the rest, following what is written in the *Iezirah* <note>The *Sefer Yetzirah* or "Book of Formation," a foundational text of Jewish mysticism.</note>: 

> For which reason God weighed the letters and permuted them: Aleph with all, and all with Aleph; Beth with all, and all with Beth <note>original Latin: "Qua de re appendit litteras Deus, & permutauit eas..."</note>

And toward the end: 

> God made all things one over against another. <note>original Latin: "omnia fecit vnum è regione alterius, Deus."</note>

Saint Jerome and others have believed that the Prophet Jeremiah, in his 25th chapter, followed this artifice when he wrote ששך *Scezac* <note>Sheshach: a famous biblical example of the Atbash cipher.</note> instead of בבל *Babel* <note>Babylon.</note>, for fear that the King of Babylon would be irritated and angered against the Israelites. Regarding this, see what Saint Münster <note>Sebastian Münster, a 16th-century German cartographer and Hebrew scholar.</note> wrote after the Hebrews in his annotations on this Prophet in his Hebrew Bible. Indeed, Jonathan <note>Jonathan ben Uzziel, traditionally credited with the Aramaic translation (Targum) of the Prophets.</note>, in his Chaldean paraphrase—who flourished long before the Incarnation—notably translated it as בבל (*Babel*) where the aforementioned Prophet wrote ששך (*Sheshach*) in Hebrew, which otherwise has no meaning. ...the great antiquity of secret writing and the ciphers that undoubtedly first came from the Hebrews, specifically concerning these <term>Ziruphz</term> <note>Hebrew: *Tzirufim*, meaning combinations or permutations of letters.</note>. On this subject, those who wish to be curious enough to meditate at leisure will undoubtedly find several beautiful and excellent ways of writing in all languages; however, to avoid wordiness, we shall leave these expressly to their own diligent research and mental dexterity. This is because it is the true root and foundation of all types of ciphers that proceed by way of transpositions and commutations of letters, whether they be simple or double. However, it is not shown here in its complete square format, but only halfway—specifically, the part from the right side moving toward the left, following the Hebrew way of writing. This follows neither the same order nor the usual sequence of letters, but rather another manner of pairing specific to the <term>Kabbalists</term>, who devised it for their own use, both for extracting divine names from certain places in Hebrew scripture and for investigating the internal meaning hidden beneath the apparent and external context of the written letter.

For example, the word <term>מצפץ Mazpaz</term> <note>original Hebrew: מצפץ</note>—associated with the reign of David, called <term>Malchut</term> <note>The tenth Sephirah (divine attribute) in the Kabbalistic Tree of Life, representing "Kingdom" or the physical realm.</note>, and consequently with the Messiah—though it is not found in the Scripture, is nonetheless a cipher and symbol of the ineffable four-letter name <term>יהוה</term> <note>The Tetragrammaton, the sacred name of God usually rendered as Yahweh or Jehovah.</note>. It is drawn from the <term>Ethbas</term> <note>The *Atbash* cipher, a system where the first letter of the alphabet is replaced by the last, the second by the second-to-last, and so on.</note> or the 22nd and final alphabet of the *Ziruphz* (permutations and commutations). As one can see here, the <term>מ Mem</term> is placed for the <term>י Yod</term>; the <term>צ Tsade</term> for the <term>ה He</term>; the <term>פ Pe</term> for the <term>ו Vav</term>; and the <term>צ Tsade</term> once again for the <term>ה He</term>. This word is composed of **Maz**, which in the 5th and 6th order of Hebrew verb conjugations means *sucked and expressed*, which suits the *Malchut*—the <term>Sephirot</term> <note>One of the ten emanations in Kabbalah through which the Infinite reveals itself.</note> or numbering of the Moon, which receives all impressions from above to squeeze and press them out below. It is also composed of **Paz**, which in the first conjugation means as much as "to cry out and sing for joy," according to what is written:

> Lord, you shall open my lips, and my mouth shall announce your praise: Psalm 51.

In the second conjugation, it signifies making an incision, opening, separating, wounding, or delivering: <note>original Latin: "Ego occidam, & ego viuere faciam"</note> *I will kill, and I will make alive*, Deuteronomy 32. Regarding the first point, then, one need only reverse the pairings to make it square and complete; just as at the start, where Aleph and Lamed are joined together, turn them around and there will be Lamed and Aleph, and so with the rest following what is written in the <term>Iezirah</term> <note>The *Sefer Yetzirah* or "Book of Formation," an ancient Jewish mystical text.</note>:

> For which reason God weighed the letters and changed them: Aleph with all, and all with Aleph; Beth with all, and all with Beth <note>original Latin: "Qua de re appendit litteras Deus, & permutauit eas : Aleph cum omnibus, & omnes cum Aleph : Beth cum omnibus, & omnes cum Beth"</note>; and toward the end: God made all things, one over against the other. <note>original Latin: "omnia fecit vnum è regione alterius, Deus"</note>

Saint Jerome and others believed that the Prophet Jeremiah, in his 25th chapter, followed this artifice and used <term>ששך Sheshach</term> <note>original Hebrew: ששך</note> instead of <term>בבל Babel</term> <note>original Hebrew: בבל (Babylon)</note> for fear that the King of Babylon would be incensed and enraged against the Israelites. Concerning this, see what <term>Saint Münster</term> <note>Sebastian Münster (1488–1552), a German cartographer and Hebrew scholar who published a Hebrew-Latin Bible.</note>, following the Hebrews, wrote in his annotations on this Prophet in his Hebrew Bible. Indeed, Jonathan, in his Chaldean paraphrase <note>Refers to the *Targum Jonathan*, an ancient Aramaic translation and expansion of the Prophets.</note>—who flourished long before the Incarnation—notably translated *Babel* where the aforementioned Prophet wrote **ששך** in Hebrew, which otherwise has no meaning. These discourses will give us a clear interpretation of the following words taken from Book 3 of *The Kabbalistic Art* by <term>Johann Reuchlin</term> <note>Also known by his Greek name Capnion, a humanist and pioneering Christian scholar of Kabbalah.</note>:

> Perhaps I will show you much more hidden things in this third [book] of the
> Cabala. <note>original Latin: "Multo fortè occultiora, ostendam vobis in hac tertia Cabalæ"</note>

In the part of the Kabbalah called *Themurah* <term>Themurah: A Kabbalistic method of substituting letters for other letters according to specific mathematical or positional rules, often used for cryptography or mystical interpretation</term>, where a mutual substitution of letter for letter occurs, this happens as many times as the alphabets are permuted. They are permuted according to the number of letters, twenty-two times, because we read twenty-two letters in the Hebrew alphabet. It is always permitted to join any two letters together and take one for the other; this combination is called צירוף <gloss>Tziruf</gloss> <note>original: "צירוף" (Tziruf), meaning "combination" or "permutation."</note>. For example, if I were to join the letters of the Latin alphabet A, B, C, D, E, F continuously in pairs, so that A and B are under the first "yoke" <note>original: "sub iugo." This refers to pairing letters together as if they were yoked like oxen.</note>, C and D under the second, and E and F under the third, and I wished to write a letter to someone skilled in this art to urge him to fall before the feet of a prince to petition him, I would write **DBCF**. He would understand this as *Cade* <note>original: "Cade." Latin for "Fall" or "Prostrate yourself." In this cipher, D=C, B=A, C=D, and F=E.</note>, and so it goes for the others. 

This entire mechanism arises from an alphabetical revolution, where letters are swapped for one another according to the pair to which they are "yoked": specifically, *a* for *b* and *b* for *a*; similarly *c* for *d* and *d* for *c*, and likewise *e* for *f* and *f* for *e*. This proceeds even more easily in Hebrew, with nothing standing in the way, because the sounds which the Latins name as vowels are not placed within the order of the Hebrew alphabet <note>The author points out that because Hebrew is primarily a consonantal alphabet (an abjad), the cryptographic swapping of letters is more straightforward than in Latin, where vowels are interspersed among consonants.</note>. 

Therefore, in ancient times, moved by this, our father Abraham said (as read in the *Book of Formation* <note>original: "lib. Iezira." Referring to the Sefer Yetzirah, one of the oldest and most important books of Jewish mysticism.</note>, chapter 12): "Aleph with all, and all with Aleph; likewise Beth with all, and all with Beth," and so on for each letter. This same author later says: the joining of the Hebrew elements must by no means be understood in a crude or unlearned way, for all things are spirit. Thus, it is written in the said *Book of Formation*: "And with that spirit, God engraved twenty-two letters—three mothers, seven doubles, and twelve simples—and each of them is spirit." <note>This refers to the Sefer Yetzirah’s classification of Hebrew letters: "Mothers" (Aleph, Mem, Shin), "Doubles" (letters with two sounds), and "Simples" (the remaining twelve).</note> Consequently, these things have been handed down to us to be contemplated spiritually with great joy, not for contradiction or mockery, but to embrace the mysteries of the Scriptures with pious faith, and so on.

### CHAPTER 17.

From the secret and mystery of the <term>Ziruphs</term> <note>Ziruph, or Tziruf, refers to the Kabbalistic practice of permuting and combining Hebrew letters to reveal hidden meanings or divine names.</note> (or Zirufs) explained above, there proceeds another method which the Kabbalists call <term>Atbash</term> <note>original: "אתבש ATBASZ"; a substitution cipher where the first letter of the Hebrew alphabet (Aleph) is replaced by the last (Tav), the second (Bet) by the second-to-last (Shin), and so on.</note>. This is to say, the Hebrew alphabet reversed, which we might describe as an arrangement or transposition—a "leap" of certain Hebrew letters into others within the alphabet. This is clearly explained, following the ancient Hebrew doctors, by Francesco Giorgio <note>original: "George Venitien"</note> in his *Harmony of the World*, Jean Mercier <note>original: "I. Mercier"</note> in his treatise on Hebrew abbreviations, Theodor Bibliander in his commentary on all languages and letters (in the chapter on secret letters), Guy le Fèvre de la Boderie in his Syro-Chaldean dictionary under the word *Atbash*, and his brother Nicolas in his introduction to the harmony of the aforementioned Francesco Giorgio. This artifice is, for the most part, ingenious, veiled, intricate, and full of many difficulties; nonetheless, it was treated by the great Abbot Trithemius in his *Polygraphia*, and after him by Blaise de Vigenère in his *Treatise on Ciphers*.

Here is an example reported by the Kabbalists regarding the beginning of the Book of Ezekiel, in these words: "being seated in the midst of the captives on the bank of the river Chebar." These Kabbalists interpret this word <term>Chebar</term> <note>original: "כובר Chobar"</note> through this *Atbash* or *Ethbaz*, or transposition of letters, to mean <term>Cherub</term> <note>original: "כרוב Cherub"</note>—that is to say, an influence of the Cherubim, angels of the second rank. For these are the same letters, merely arranged differently. Furthermore, the word "river" relates and fits very well with the word "influence," because they both come from the verb "to flow" <note>original: "fluer"</note>, just as it is the nature of rivers to always strive downward until they swallow themselves into the sea, which is the great receptacle of all. So too is it with the divine influx, which, like intelligence, never ascends, as Zoroaster wrote in these Greek words: "intellect never ascends" <note>original: "νόησις μήποτε ἀναβαίνει"</note>. Thus, God always flows without ceasing through his channels, like a perpetual source of living water, without ever flowing back upward; for where could it rise, given that the throne of His essence is above all things?

Of this descent of the Divinity into inferior things, Rabbi Joseph Gikatilla <note>original: "Rabbi Ioseph Castiglian"</note> speaks thus in the *Gates of Light*, following the ancient Kabbalists:

At the beginning of the creation of the world, the Divine Presence <note>The author uses "cohabitation," a literal translation of the Hebrew *Shekhinah*.</note> descended into lower things. As the Divinity inhabited the regions here below, the heavens and the earth were found united together; they were the sources and the channels that flowed from Him, acting in perfection, drawn from on high to below, God accomplishing everything by the same means, as much above as below.

Thus, the "River Chebar" in this cipher stands in place of the first "bark" or outer covering of the mysteries of the Hebrews; the "influence of the Cherub" to which it is linked is the second layer, which covers the third, wherein lies finally the true sense and intelligence: namely, the light of the <term>Tetragrammaton</term> <note>The four-letter divine name, YHWH.</note> יהוה. Of this it is written in Psalm 36: "In your light shall we see light" <note>original: "In lumine tuo videbimus lumen"</note>; that is to say, through the light of the Son, we shall see that of the Father. It was this light that descended into the understanding of the Prophet, through the second rank...

## On the Gematria of the Hebrews.

### CHAP. 18.

<image-desc>Decorative woodcut initial letter V featuring foliage and a landscape background.</image-desc>
HEre is another admirable mystery of the Hebrews for interpreting and clarifying their Hebrew scriptures, called by them <term>Gematria</term> <note>original: "גמטריא, Ghematria"; a system of assigning numerical value to a word or phrase.</note>, that is, the calculation of numbers, as if it were a numerical dimension of earthly characters in turn; which nevertheless depends on that Arithmetic which, because of its hidden simplicity, cannot be grasped by any senses. Wherefore it was called <term>Geometry</term> rather than <term>Arithmetic</term>, although both are worth one and the same in this art. By this reasoning, says <term>Kimhi</term> <note>David Kimhi, a medieval biblical commentator and grammarian.</note> on Zechariah 3, "Branch" <note>original: "צמח Germen"</note> is equivalent to "Consoler" <note>original: "מנחם consolator"</note>, which is a name of the Messiah, since the letters of both names result in the number 148. So in the <term>Tikkunei HaZohar</term> <note>original: "Tikum Hazoar"; a classic work of Kabbalistic literature.</note>, that "Throne" <note>original: "הכסא thronus"</note> by way of <term>Antonomasia</term> <note>The substitution of a title or epithet for a proper name.</note> is equivalent to <term>Elohim</term> <note>original: "אלהים"; one of the divine names for God.</note>, because the letters of both names taken separately total 86. Some Hebrew doctors and others have written that this Hebrew word, Gematria—which is an equivalence of Hebrew numbers, measures, and proportions—originates and proceeds from <note>original: "ἀπὸ τῆς γεωμετρίας"; Greek for "from geometry."</note>, as reported very well by Elias Levita in his *Tishbi*, Guy le Fèvre de la Boderie in his Syro-Chaldean dictionary, and his brother Nicolas in his introduction to the *Harmony of the World* by Francesco Giorgio <note>original: "George Venitien"</note> in the interpretation of this word. Although in fact, this mystery does not retain its property at all: for it relates rather to number, and takes place when one word is substituted and extended for another by equality and calculation. The Kabbalists still construct devices of occult and secret writing by way of this Gematria; these devices are established on numbers and points on one hand, and the lengths of lines on the other, which they afterwards disguise in many and various forms and manners. The <term>Ghilgul</term> <note>original: "גלגול GHILGVL"; literally "cycling" or "rolling."</note>, which is a numerical quantity, is a part and rule of it; for which reason Rabbi Joseph of Salem <note>Likely referring to Joseph Gikatilla, author of "Ginnat Egoz".</note> has titled (as I have already remarked before) a discourse of his on these devices and secrets <term>Ghinat</term> <note>original: "גנת Ghinat"; meaning "Garden."</note>, that is to say, <term>Gematria</term>, <term>Notarikon</term>, and <term>Temurah</term>, according to the report of Johannes Reuchlin <note>original: "I. Reuclin Capnion"</note> in Book 3 of *The Art of the Kabbalah*, Jean Mercier in his little book on Hebrew abbreviations, and Guy le Fèvre de la Boderie in his Syro-Chaldean dictionary.

# Languages of this Universe.

### [Page 169]

Kabbalists <note>The original OCR reads "balistes," likely a transcription error for "Caballistes."</note> celebrate the letters of the word **Malach** <note>original: "מלח Malach"; Hebrew for "salt."</note>, which signifies salt, for the calculation of their numerical values amounts to 78. For *Mem* is worth 40; *Lamed*, 30; and *Heth*, 8. Now, in whatever manner you divide this 78, there will always result some number representing a Mystery of the divine names. For example, half of it is thirty-nine, which is the same as the letters of **Chuzu** <note>original: "כוזו Chuzu"; a Kabbalistic cipher for the name of God (YHVH) often written on the "sheath" or case of a Mezuzah.</note>, the "sheath" as they interpret it, of the Great Name; namely, *Caph* twenty, *Vav* six, *Zain* seven, and *Vav* again six. If divided into three parts, each will amount to twenty-six, which is the number of the **Tetragrammaton** <note>original: "יהוה"; the four-letter sacred name of God (Yahweh/Jehovah).</note>. In six parts, they will be thirteen, which is equivalent to the measure of piety <note>The number 13 corresponds to the Hebrew words "Echad" (Unity) and "Ahava" (Love).</note>. In thirteen parts, they will be six, the value of the letter *Vav*, representing the life from above; and six is the first perfect number <note>In mathematics, a perfect number equals the sum of its divisors (1+2+3=6).</note>. In twenty-six parts, it will be the number of the most holy and sacred Trinity: three. In thirty-nine parts, it is two, the value of the letter *Beth*, the symbol of the **Word** <note>The "Verbe" or Logos.</note>, or the second person and the house of the Ideas of the Archetype. Finally, the seventy-eight denote as many units, each representing the unity of a single God. It is exactly the same with the word **Lechem** <note>original: "לחם Lechem"; Hebrew for "bread."</note>, meaning bread, which is an anagram of the preceding word; therefore the letters also yield seventy-eight: *Lamed* thirty, *Heth* eight, and *Mem* forty.

But **Iain** <note>original: "יין Iain"; Hebrew for "wine."</note>, or Wine, is worth only seventy, a number proceeding from the multiplication of ten by seven, which concerns the soul, which has its seat in the blood—into which wine is very easily converted. By this means, the Divinity has always taken great delight in these two substances of bread and wine, both for the mystery they denote of His Church (composed of many souls united in a common agreement of belief, in imitation of how bread is made of many grains of wheat kneaded together, and wine is pressed from many clusters of grapes), and because of the incorruptibility they share more than any others, arising from the quintessence of the "water of life" <note>likely referring to alcohol or spirits</note> which resides there in great abundance. Thus they are coupled in the first book of Esdras, chapter six, with salt and oil, as the four most useful and necessary things that Nature produces.

To be brief, <term>Gematria</term> <note>original: "Ghematrie"; a Kabbalistic method of interpreting words by their numerical values.</note> is a circular revolution and a square and cubic multiplication containing many artifices that depend principally on formal Arithmetic and Geometry, employed in the profound meditations of the Hebrew Kabbalah. The aforementioned **Johannes Reuchlin** <note>original: "I. Reuclin"; a famous German humanist and scholar of Hebrew (1455–1522).</note>, in the place cited above, says these words:

> The Kabbalistic art <margin>cc</margin> <note>original: "Ars Cabalistica"</note> consists of three principal things. First, the computation of numbers, <margin>cc</margin> which is called Geometry <note>original: "Geometria"</note>, as if it were a numerical dimension of earthly characters in turn, <margin>cc</margin> which nevertheless depends on that Arithmetic because of its <margin>cc</margin> abstract simplicity, untouchable by any senses, and therefore not even <margin>cc</margin> subject to the crude skill of a novice. It is therefore called the first part, <margin>cc</margin> Geometry rather than Arithmetic, although both in truth have the same <margin>cc</margin> value in this art. Next, syllables are sometimes changed, just as a <margin>cc</margin> word is changed, or a term is simply inverted. Second, a letter is <margin>cc</margin> placed for a whole word, and it is called **Notariakon** <margin>cc</margin> <note>original: "Notariacum"; a system of shorthand or using letters as acronyms.</note> from the marks of Notaries, since there every letter is noted at the top <margin>cc</margin> so that it becomes a sign of some whole word. Third, this art <margin>cc</margin> consists in the mutation of letters, when one is <margin>cc</margin> ingeniously placed for another, and it is called commutation <note>The Hebrew system of Temurah.</note>, by which it happened that Rabbi <margin>cc</margin> Joseph the Minor of Jerusalem <note>original: "Rabbi Ioseph Minor Salemitanus"</note> named the books he wrote on this art "The Garden." <margin>cc</margin>

” <note>original Latin: "propter ternas huius dictionis literas, quarū singulæ singulas portiones artis Cabalisticę designāt..."</note> ...because of the three letters of this word <note>original: גנת (GNT), though the OCR reads גנח (GNH)</note>, of which each signifies one portion of the Kabbalistic art. For *Gimel* signifies **Gematria**; *Nun*, **Notariacon**; *Tav*, **Temurah**. Thus, the parts of the whole art are these: **Gematria**, which is Arithmetic; **Notariacon**, which is a kind of shorthand or acronym system; and **Temurah**, which is the exchange or permutation of letters, etc. Briefly, from what has been deduced above, we learn that the mystery or artifice of the aforementioned Kabbalists, called **Gematria**, is a word undoubtedly corrupted from that of **Geometry**, as I have already said. By this term, they also encompass **Arithmetic**, without which Geometry cannot exist—nor can measurements and figures exist without numbers. Arithmetic, however, can exist on its own, being simpler and more formal, whereas Geometry is more material and coarse, just as figures are more material than numbers. Indeed, just as speech and writing cannot exist without some premeditation of thought, yet thought can well exist without speech or writing. 

They might also, perhaps, have been moved to give these two sciences, joined together, the name of the second—namely, **Geometry** (which is a more modern term)—rather than the first, **Arithmetic**, because Plato magnifies it so much in the seventh book of the *Republic*, where he calls it the knowledge of that which always is. <note>original Greek: "τῷ γὰρ ἀεὶ ὄντος, ἡ γεωμετρική, γνῶσίς ἐστιν"</note> And in another place, according to the citation by Plutarch in the second question of the eighth book of the *Symposiacs* <note>A series of philosophical table-talks by Plutarch.</note>, he posits that God practices it continually. Upon this, he discourses that **Lycurgus** <note>The legendary lawgiver of Sparta.</note> banished **Arithmetical** proportion from **Lacedaemon** <note>Sparta.</note> in order to introduce **Geometrical** proportion. By the former, he denoted the tumultuous confusion of the Common People, which consists in number and consequently concerns a raw equality in which everyone is the master, "like rats in straw." By **Geometry**, he denoted reason, because it lies in the difference of lines being longer or shorter; this signifies the authority that the great, the good, the honorable, the wise, and the foresighted must have over the ignorant and brutal Common Populace—the majority of whom are vicious, debauched, reckless, and hasty, seeking nothing but an equality than which there is nothing more unjust or pernicious in a state. 

By this means, God, in all things—so far as they permit and it is possible to do—removes such equality from the world; he observes in its place merit according to **Geometrical** proportion, and dignity, determining the whole according to reason. Plato, therefore, through "the great and the small," describes not only matter (as Aristotle wishes to attribute to him), but forms as well, together with all things composed of these two, according to the degrees of their essence and perfection. This is neither more nor less than what **Pythagoras** did before him with even and odd numbers, and **Empedocles** with the "Dense" and the "Rare" <note>The original French "Espoix" likely refers to the "Thick" or "Dense."</note> which he established among his Principles. 

In this imitation, the **Kabbalists** have built systems of occult writing by way of the aforementioned **Gematria**, established on numbers of points on one hand and lengths on the other. They then disguise these in various ways. As **B. de Vigenère** <note>Blaise de Vigenère, a 16th-century diplomat and cryptographer.</note> has already remarked on this subject in his treatise on ciphers: in order to avoid a too lengthy extension of these lines, he contented himself with deducing eight differences, each of which serves reciprocally for two letters, which are distinguished by certain small marks and secret notes difficult to perceive, for fear of engendering some suspicion of the ruse. # On the Notariacum or Notariacon of the Hebrews.
# CHAPTER 19.

<image-desc>Large ornamental drop cap 'L' with floral and vine-like patterns.</image-desc> THE **NOTARIACON** of the Hebrews is another marvelous mystery used to interpret and clarify their Hebrew scriptures and their secrets. It is called thus, נוטריקון <note>original Hebrew: *Notarikon*</note>, a word composed of the roots *Notar* and *Teikon*, meaning to preserve a diction or figure. This is because, in the manner of notaries and legal practitioners, it is formed from certain assembled Hebrew letters, each of which—without being joined into syllables—represents and takes the place of an entire word. Sometimes, through a "Laconism" <note>a style of brief, pithy speech named after the Spartans of Laconia</note> or in the manner of an oracle, a single voice or an entire word carries as much weight as a whole clause, expression, or sentence. 

This is clearly taught by Elias Levita in his *Tishbi* <note>a dictionary of Talmudic and Midrashic Hebrew</note> in the interpretation of this word; J. Reuchlin (Capnion) in Book 3 of *The Kabbalistic Art*; J. Mercier in his booklet on Hebrew abbreviations; Sixtus of Siena in Book 3 of the *Notariac Exposition*, method 7, in his *Holy Library*; Father Louis in Book 10, Chapters 12 and 13, of *The Divine Hebrew Secrets*; Guy Lefèvre de la Boderie in his Syro-Chaldean dictionary; and his brother Nicolas in his introduction to *The Harmony of the World* by George the Venetian. 

This method of abbreviation, taken from the first letters of Hebrew words and phrases (of which they form signs and figures), is called by the Hebrews ראשי תיבות <note>original Hebrew: *Rashe Tevot*, literally "heads of words"</note>, or the "beginning of dictions." It is represented among the Hebrews by the two letters ת' <note>an abbreviation mark</note>. These Hebrews say: "The word *Ginat* [Garden], as a 'Head of Words' (*Rashe Tevot*), signifies by these three letters the three parts of the Kabbalah which we call **Gematria**, **Notariacon**, and **Themurah**." <note>original Latin: "Ginat, in Rasce Theuoth, his tribus litteris tres Cabalæ partes significat, quas appellamus Ghematria Notariacon, & Themurah..."</note> This follows a certain Rabbi Joseph of Salamanca <note>Likely referring to Joseph Gikatilla, a 13th-century Kabbalist</note>, who composed his books under the name *Ginat Egoz* <note>Hebrew for "Garden of Nuts," a reference to the Song of Solomon 6:11</note>. From this, many others have attached excellent and pleasant titles to their own books. 

**Gematria** and the other method of abbreviation taken from the *last* letters of the said Hebrew words and phrases is called סוף תיבות <note>original Hebrew: *Sof Tevot*, literally "ends of words"</note>, or the "finality of dictions or vocables." It is figured in Hebrew by two other letters סת, as confirmed by the aforementioned J. Reuchlin (Capnion), J. Mercier, Guy Lefèvre de la Boderie, and his brother Nicolas in the places previously cited. There are still other types of **Notariacon** among the Hebrews: the first being when every Hebrew letter of a word denotes, individually, as many words as there are letters. The second, when the first [letter] is removed...

But this artifice, which is practiced with all the Hebrew letters of a complete word, is called by the general name **Notariacon** <term>a Kabbalistic method of shorthand or acronyms where letters represent whole words or phrases</term>. According to the opinion of some modern theologians, this is what the beloved disciple of Jesus Christ <note>Saint John</note> calls in his Revelation—when mentioning the Beast—the *Mark* <note>original Greek: $\chi\alpha\rho\alpha\gamma\mu\alpha$, *charagma*</note>.

Now, as for a single word standing for an entire period and perfect sentence, we find among infinite examples cited by Rabbi Judah Marinus, Samuel Nagid, and other Hebrew Rabbis and doctors—whom Abraham Aben Ezra <note>a celebrated 12th-century scholar and commentator</note> alleges in the *Book of the Mystery of the Law*—a very excellent one in the Chaldean language <note>Aramaic</note>, in the 5th chapter of the Prophet Daniel. This concerns the three or four words said to have been written by the Angel’s hand against the partition or wall in this manner: *Numbered, numbered, weighed, and the Persians* (or *divisions*) <note>original Hebrew/Aramaic: מנא מנא תקל ופרסין, *Mene mene Thequel Ufarsin*</note>. These were words that the Babylonian Sages and Astrologues did not know how to explain, but Daniel interpreted them in this fashion: *Numbered* <note>original: מנא, *Mene*, Latin: *id est numerato*</note>: God has numbered your kingdom and brought it to its end; *Weighed* <note>original: תקל, *Thequel*, Latin: *pondera*</note>: you have been placed in the balance and found light and wanting; *Divided* <note>original: פרס, *Peres*</note>: your kingdom is divided and given to the Persians and Medes.

Therefore, it is not a matter of idle invention that the Hebrews have asserted that each character of their language represents an entire utterance and word, as well as a complete and perfect clause according to the types of **Notariacon** deduced above, in the guise and form of the Egyptian Hieroglyphics, of which we shall speak more fully hereafter in the chapter on the Egyptians and the Egyptian language.

Some modern authors suggest that the Romans tacitly practiced these types of **Notariacon** from the Hebrews in their Latin writing and language. There are infinite inscriptions and formulas of this kind made entirely of capital letters, each representing a complete word: such as **S.C.** for *a decree of the senate* <note>Latin: *senatusconsultum*</note>; **S.P.Q.R.** for *The Senate and the Roman People* <note>Latin: *Senatus populusque Romanus*</note>; **D.T.** for *Only* <note>Latin: *Duntaxt*</note>; **D.M.** for *To the Divine Shades* <note>Latin: *Diis Manibus*, a common funerary dedication to the spirits of the dead</note> on all their tombs; **H.M.H.N.S.** for *This monument does not pass to the heirs* <note>Latin: *Hoc monumentum hæredes non sequitur*</note>; **Q.R.C.F.** for *when the King fled the assembly* <note>Latin: *quando Rex comitio fugit*</note> or *when it is lawful for the King to attend the assembly* <note>Latin: *quádo Rex comitiauit fas*</note>; **A.A.A.F.F.** for *For the casting and striking of gold, silver, and bronze* <note>Latin: *Auro, Argento, aere, flando, feriundo*</note>; and infinite others that can be seen in ancient books, marbles, bronzes, medals, and cameos. Marcus Tullius Cicero composed a book on this in his time, which he dedicated to his son; then a certain Valerius Probus wrote a treatise *On Roman Notations* <note>Latin: *Romanorum notis*</note>, which Paul the Deacon greatly expanded. However, this art must have been quite meager given the simple artifice involved, according to the testimony of Suetonius Tranquillus in the *Life of Julius Caesar*, chapter 56. He mentions that this Emperor used to employ certain transpositions of letters in his secret dispatches, substituting one for another, all in a sequence without any distinction between words. Here are his words:

And in the Life of Augustus, chapter 88: <margin>“</margin> *Whenever he wrote by cipher, he put B for A, C for B, and followed the same logic for the subsequent letters. For X, however, he used a double A, AA.* <note>original Latin: "Quoties autem per notam scribit..." This describes a Caesar cipher</note> The historian Dio, in the life of the <margin>“</margin> aforementioned Augustus, reports that Maecenas, his great friend, was the first <margin>“</margin> among the Latins to invent these "Notes" <note>shorthand symbols</note>. Today, one can see in several places a large volume entitled *On Ciceronian Notes* <note>original: "De Notis Ciceronianis"</note>, the artifice of which is more like a cipher than the previous example. This is because they are all characters formed at will to serve as abbreviations; these were more suitable for the clerks who record the pleas of lawyers—just as they used to do for ancient orators and their harangues—than for any other purpose. This was due to the promptness and speed of speech, which passes suddenly like a well-feathered arrow. Indeed, each of these characters or "Notes" signified at least one word, or even several for the most part, as the poet Ausonius testifies:

> Where a great abundance of speech
> Is handled with individual points,
> So that a single voice is completed.
> <note>original Latin: "Qua multa fandi Copia / Punctis per acta singulis, / Vt vna vox absoluatur."</note>

Some attribute this work—even Eusebius does—to a freedman of Cicero named Tyro. But it was later enriched and increased by Perennius Pylargyrus and Aquila, another freedman of the aforementioned Maecenas. Still a few years later, Seneca arranged them into alphabetical order, reaching the number of five thousand. Saint Cyprian also added to them and adapted the whole system for Christian use in the form of a dictionary, as the Abbot Trithemius explains at length in the *Clavicula* <note>Little Key</note> of his *Polygraphy* <term>a 16th-century treatise on cryptography and shorthand by Johannes Trithemius</term>. A. Glauburg, in his commentary on the said Trithemius, cites P. Crinitus, Angelo Decembrio, P. Appianus, Bartholomaeus Amantius, and other modern authors who have treated this matter. After them, one may see T. Bibliander in his commentary on the common reasoning of all languages and letters, in the chapter on "notes and secret writing" <note>original: "de notis & arcana scriptura"</note>.

But this is a deep sea of confusion and a true hell for the memory, being an infinitely laborious and, despite all that, useless thing. This is because anyone can create their own personal and particular abbreviations, which are impressed—indeed, almost innate—within the depths of their own memory. Such personal marks are more prompt and run more lightly under the pen, as we see with the clerks of the Sovereign Courts, whose speed of hand not only accompanies but even outpaces the lightest and most free tongues of the lawyers. This is also seen in all the scribbles and minutes of Notaries, Attorneys, and the writs of bailiffs.

To return to the aforementioned **Notariacon** <term>shorthand acronyms</term> of the Hebrews: it does not deviate from their customary letters, though it is of various sorts. Specifically, when a syllable or a letter is put for an entire word, or one word for an entire clause (as we have already said above), and conversely, a complete clause for a single term, or a term for a single letter. As one can see in the *Polygraphy* of the aforementioned Trithemius, it is in truth a quite fine and ingenious invention, were it not for the long-winded and tedious meaning produced by these synonyms joined together in a row, and the little substance they ultimately express. A single letter is used for a word, as in the four-letter Name <term>יהוה</term> <note>the Tetragrammaton, the name of God</note>, in which the first letter **Iod** <term>the Hebrew letter Yod (י)</term> represents...

This is why this most holy name was "ineffable" <note>unpronounceable</note> to them, as it is said in Exodus 6: *And my name the Tetragrammaton יהוה, I did not make known <margin>,,</margin> to them.* <note>original Latin: "Et nomen meum Tetragrammaton... non indicaui eis"</note> Sometimes these single and singular letters, which represent <margin>,,</margin> an entire word, are drawn from the end or the middle of a phrase and marked above with a sign or title to discern them, as was mentioned above. There is, furthermore, another branch of this <term>Notariacon</term> <note>a system of shorthand or acronyms where words are formed from the initial or final letters of other words</note> when all the letters of a word denote just as many words, as in the 3rd Psalm: *many rise up against me*. This is the true <term>Notariacon</term>.

The aforementioned Hebrews have yet another secret of writing depending on this: when one removes the first letter of a word, or adds one to it, whereby the meaning of it changes. This might be seen in the Latin *Claudo* [I close] and *laudo* [I praise], *tango* [I touch] and *ango* [I distress]; and likewise in the middle of a word, *Surgo* [I rise] and *Sugo* [I suck]; or in French *Paris* and *Païs* [Country]. ...of a man, the alphabets by spaces in this scattered dust, according to the understanding of your thoughts: and at that very instant this man was reduced to dust, and vanished from their sight. From then on, the Prophet affirmed he had knowledge of the faculty and virtue of these alphabets, and of their revolving literal permutations <note>This refers to *Gematria* or *Temurah*, Kabbalistic methods of rearranging letters to find hidden meanings</note>, by way of the accomplishments of which he had already learned the manner in the *Book of Yetzirah* <note>The *Sefer Yetzirah* (Book of Formation) is one of the oldest Jewish mystical texts, describing how God created the world using the 22 letters of the Hebrew alphabet</note>. But this Rabbi remains silent on the fact that all of this was intended to denote nothing other than that God was to become man, and die as a man: the God of truth, namely, who is the Messiah, *because Christ is the truth* <note>original Latin: "quoniam Christus est veritas"</note>, in Saint John chapter 5, and in Psalm 85, *truth has sprung out of the earth* <note>original Latin: "veritas de terra orta est"</note>. 

Furthermore, this word אמת <note>Emet, meaning "Truth"</note> is not devoid of mysteries: for it is composed of three letters which are the beginning, the middle, and the end of the alphabet <note>Aleph is the 1st letter, Mem is the middle/13th, and Thau is the 22nd/last letter of the Hebrew alphabet</note>. Moreover, they represent the following: *Aleph* [א], which is worth one, represents the simplicity of numbers, which is attributed to God and to the intelligible world; *Mem* [מ], which is worth 40, represents the tens in the celestial world; and *Thau* [ת], which is worth 400, represents the hundreds in the elementary world. 

And there is still to consider the firm and solid "squareness" that truth must possess: which squareness is perceived as much in the shape of these characters, which are all square, as in their value in calculations. This is because *Aleph* also signifies a thousand <note>The word for the letter Aleph is spelled the same as *Eleph*, meaning 1,000</note>, which is the end of all numbers and the Cube of ten; *Mem* is 40, which is the same ten multiplied by the four that constitute it (because 1, 2, 3, and 4 make ten); and the *Thau* is 400, the square of ten (which is 100) multiplied by that same four, or four tens times ten (for 10 times 40 are 400). Thus, both the shapes and the numbers of these three letters אמת (*Emet*, "Truth") are always solid, however one might take them. Those of falsehood, שקר (*Sheker*), on the contrary, are weak and wavering—following the proverb, *That a lie has short heels* <note>A common Renaissance proverb meaning lies are easily tripped up or overturned</note>, as if presupposing that it is easy to overthrow. Their numbers, moreover, are all in the hundreds, which denotes the thickness of matter, in perpetual change and alteration: for ש (*Schin*) is worth 300, ק (*Coph*) 100, and ר (*Res*) 200.

AS FOR removing a letter from the middle of a word, Rabbi Simon <note>Likely Simeon bar Yochai, the traditional author of the Zohar</note> in the Talmud of the Jews, having been asked why, in this passage of Holy Scripture in Job 38: *THE LIGHT SHALL BE TAKEN AWAY FROM THE WICKED*, they eclipsed the letter ע (*Ain*) out of מרשעים (*Mersaim*), which means "impious" or "wicked," so that there remained מרשים (*Meresim*), by a syncopation <note>The shortening of a word by omitting a sound or letter</note>, which no longer means "impious" but "indigent" and "suffering." 

He responded that it is because whoever, in this temporal life, becomes negligent in the contemplation of the beauty of the sensible world, will by that same means be destitute in the knowledge of intelligible things—of which this physical world is like a portrait—and consequently falls into misery regarding the world to come. Truly, he who does not observe and pay heed to what is exposed here below to our senses (though it be fleeting and corruptible) will no longer be able to penetrate the perception of the invisible and permanent which is up there. Just as one cannot recognize the interior thought of a man except through speech or writing, and similar signs and outward marks—which is what the Apostle meant in Romans 1, already cited: *That the invisible things of God are made manifest and perceptible to the creature of the world through those things that have been made by Him.* Many such other great mysteries are discovered in the prophets by the diverse placements and sequences of letters, and by their additions and subtractions...

It is a most certain and indubitable thing that the more one seeks wonders, mysteries, and secrets in this Hebrew language, the more one encounters them; and the more one finds there, the more one recognizes its excellence and why it is admired. ## Of the ten Sephirot of the Hebrews, or divine measures and numerations, which the Kabbalists call the garments of Divinity.
### C H A P. XX.

<image-desc>Decorative woodcut initial L depicting a landscape with a stag or unicorn resting under a tree, framed by ornate floral and scrollwork patterns.</image-desc>The Hebrews have at all times held in high regard the ten <term>Sephirot</term><note>The ten attributes or emanations in Kabbalah through which the Infinite reveals itself</note>, that is to say, divine measures and numerations, otherwise named by their Kabbalists "garments of Divinity," as we have remarked before. To each of these Sephirot, these Hebrews and Kabbalists attribute one of the divine names. The first of these refers to the divine essence <note>original: "אהיה"</note> **Ehieh** <note>Hebrew for "I Am"</note>, and particularly represents the **FATHER**. It consoles and flows through the order of the Seraphim into the first mobile heaven, and from there to all things to which it gives being. It is called <term>Keter</term><note>Hebrew for "Crown"</note> or Crown, and is denoted by the letter <note>original: "ש"</note> **Shin**, which has the shape of a crown with three points and is a symbol of the **TRINITY**. But in another way, the crown, which is perfectly round, is also marked by that "non-value" in counting ciphers called **zero**, 0, when it stands alone and by itself; but when accompanied by a 1, it makes 10 (ten). Thus, the numerical signs are not at all devoid of mysteries contained beneath their shapes. Furthermore, although the Greeks try to represent the name **EHIEH** by <note>original: "ὤν"</note> *The Being* and the Latins by *Ens* (**EXISTING**), it can hardly be well expressed in any language other than Hebrew by a single word, nor translated except by a circumlocution of words. For being made of four letters, it belongs only to God, whose essence it signifies, insofar as that essence resides within Him without explaining itself or moving outward. Therefore, it is attributed to the Father and denotes all three tenses in eternity: a plurality of persons with a unity of nature. In Exodus 3, when Moses asks God what His name is, He answered him, "I am who I was, who I am, who I will be" <note>This is a literal translation of the French text's interpretation of the Hebrew *Ehyeh asher Ehyeh*</note>; which cannot be attributed to creatures,

The <term>Talmudists</term><note>Jewish scholars of the Talmud</note> interpret it as the Eternity of God, because the future tense presupposes the present and the past, which are the three distinctions of time, reduced in the divinity solely to the present; for He is exempt from the boundaries and circumscriptions of the other two, all things being present to Him: *a thousand years are as one day* <note>original Latin: *mille anni dies unus*</note>, Psalm 90 and in the second Epistle of Saint Peter. Regarding this, <term>Nahmanides</term><note>Moses ben Nahman (1194–1270), a leading medieval Jewish scholar and Kabbalist</note> said, not poorly or unlearnedly: *That God is this existence and subsistence which has not passed nor shall pass, etc.* For He is always without having had a beginning, and shall just as little have an end, inasmuch as He surpasses all respect of time, and He alone can say: *He who is, and who was, and who is to come* <note>original Greek: *ὁ ὢν, καὶ ὁ ἦν, καὶ ὁ ἐρχόμενος (ho ōn, kai ho ēn, kai ho erchomenos)*</note>, in the first chapter of Revelation. 

The letters of this name, <term>Ehyeh</term><note>אהיה</note>, also show this with a very great mystery: of which the second letter, *He* <note>ה</note>, and the third, *Yod* <note>י</note>, denote the third person of the past tense of this verb—which is the first person for the Greeks, the Latins, and us—namely <term>Hayithi</term><note>היה, actually *Hayithi* (הייתי) means "I was"</note>. This word reminds me, and not without purpose, of that verse so common in everyone's mouth: *names often suit their things* <note>original Latin: *conveniunt rebus nomina saepe suis*</note>; so it is that in the past, ill-omened and unlucky names were changed into others of better omen. For instance, the name *Malevente* <note>literally "Badly come"</note> was changed to *Benevento* <note>literally "Well come"</note> in Book 9 of Livy; *Segesta*—which alludes to *seges*, meaning harvest—was used instead of *Egesta*, meaning indigence and penury; *Epidamnus* was changed to *Dyrrachium* in Festus; and other similar examples. 

I say then, that at the first discovery of the West Indies by the Spaniards under the Genoese Christopher Columbus, the first place where they settled was the island called by the savages *Haithi*. The Spaniards changed its name to *Hispaniola* <note>the island comprising modern Haiti and the Dominican Republic</note>. But it was quite the opposite of "populating" it: for as even Peter Martyr, Gonzalo de Oviedo, and other of their own historians testify, having found more than fifteen or sixteen thousand souls upon their arrival, they treated them so "humanely" that in less than two years they consumed and reduced that great number of people to nothing. Thus, with good reason, this poor miserable island, one of the most beautiful and richest in the world, could well say "I was," according to the meaning of the Hebrew word *Hayithi* <note>הייתי, "I have been" or "I was"</note>...

Furthermore, these three letters <term>Iod</term>, <term>He</term>, and <term>Vau</term> <note>original: "י, ה, ו"</note> are "circular" in the numbers they represent, whether by a straight line, a square, or a cube; for they always end in themselves. For example, the <term>Iod</term> is worth ten, and that is the extended line; if you multiply it by itself, it will produce one hundred, which is its square, a number of ten tens; and this hundred again by itself makes a thousand, or a hundred tens, which is the cube of ten: and so on from ten to ten unto infinity. Likewise, multiply the five by itself (represented by <term>He</term>), and it makes 25; and five times 25 gives 125. The <term>Vau</term>, which is worth six, does the very same, for 6 times 6 makes 36, and six times 36 makes 216. By this, one can perceive that the numbers denoted by these three letters—ten for <term>Iod</term>, five for <term>He</term>, and six for <term>Vau</term>—always meet again at the end of their products <note>In mathematics, these are known as "automorphic numbers," where the last digit of the power is the same as the number itself.</note>; which is not so for others that always depart from themselves, just as twice 2 makes four (which is no longer 2), nor twice 4 makes eight (neither 2 nor 4); twice three makes 6, and three times three 9, and so on for the rest. There are still other things to consider regarding the number six, which we will discuss hereafter. This letter, combined with the <term>Iod</term> <note>The letter י, which has a numerical value of 10.</note> which is worth ten, makes **Yah** <note>original: "Iah" (יה), a shortened form of the divine name.</note>. Now, that the name of **Elohim**—which is the plural of <term>אלה</term> (God), to denote the plurality of persons—represents in particular the **Holy Spirit**, we have many testimonies from the **Kabbalists** <note>Scholars of Jewish mysticism.</note>, who interpret it as a Spirit of a fiery nature: in the 1st of Genesis, *the Spirit of God was moved over the waters* <note>original Latin: "Spiritus Elohim ferebatur super aquas"</note>: which waters he fostered by his heat: in accordance with **Trismegistus** <note>Hermes Trismegistus, the legendary Hellenistic figure to whom the Hermetic writings are attributed.</note> from the beginning of his *Pymander*: *but from the vitals of moist nature a pure and light fire flew forth* <note>original Latin: "ex humidæ autem naturæ visceribus syncerus ac leuis ignis euolans"</note> etc. For water represents the Word and Wisdom: *the water of saving wisdom shall give him to drink* <note>original Latin: "aqua sapientiæ salutaris potabit illum"</note>, in Ecclesiasticus 15. And again: *he has set before you water and fire* <note>original Latin: "apposuit tibi aquam & ignem"</note>: that is to say, mercy and justice. 

And in fact, God has a double tribunal: one of severity and rigor, at the left hand in the north, designated by **Elohim**, principally with the adjective <term>גבור</term> (**Gibor**), "strong and robust"; and the other of clemency at the right hand, and in the south, following this from the 3rd of Genesis, *he walked gently toward the south* <note>original Latin: "ambulabat leuiter ad meridiem"; a mystical interpretation of the "cool of the day" in Gen 3:8.</note>, not wishing to punish our first parents to the utmost; and in the 1st of the Canticles: *where you pasture, where you rest at noon* <note>original Latin: "vbi pascas, vb cubes in meridie"; Song of Solomon 1:7.</note>. This is what the name <term>יה</term> (**Yah**) carries: which, being drawn from the first two letters of the great name יהוה, if you subtract them from <term>אלהים</term> (**Elohim**), there will remain <term>אלם</term> (**Elem**), "mute" or "silent" <note>The author is using a linguistic cipher: Elohim (A-L-H-I-M) minus the letters Y-H (He and Yod) leaves the letters A-L-M, which spells "mute" in Hebrew.</note>. As if that were meant to infer that if you separate the name of mercy from the justice designated by *Elohim*, it must remain mute. 

But it seems rather to be the opposite: for when a Prince allows himself, through the importunity of prayers or otherwise, to pardon a wrongdoer or moderate the just punishment he has deserved, that is to close the mouths of his Judges, and to gag them so that they dare not proceed as they ought; whereas, on the contrary, there is nothing that can make them speak louder than a universal denial and refusal of all these manners of abusive graces, pardons, remissions, and abolitions, obtained illegitimately—true seeds and nurseries of all malversions and crimes. We must therefore seek the understanding of this mystery from another place: and presuppose that just as the future, which is the third tense, includes the two...

the other two, namely the present and the past, although in the Divinity all is but one: *What is it that was? The very same that shall be. What is it that was done? And in the first place, this word **El** <term>אל</term>, that is to say, "God," which are the first two letters of the said **Elohim**, represents the *Father*, the land of the living, and the law of nature: tempered, moreover, with clemency and severity. *I am the Lord thy God visiting the iniquity of the Fathers upon the Children unto the third and fourth generation of them that hate me, and showing mercy unto thousands of them that keep my Commandments.* <note>A paraphrase of Exodus 20:5-6.</note>

And the five characters together—by the addition of the final **Mem** <term>ם</term> which is entirely closed—denote the Holy Spirit, the fire, and the written law, which was entirely of servitude and rigor, as is the name itself, *In his right hand a fiery law* <note>original Latin: "In dextera illius ignea lex"</note>, in Deuteronomy 33. This closed letter *Mem*, within the *Jezirah* <note>Refers to the *Sefer Yetzirah* or "Book of Formation," a foundational text of Jewish mysticism.</note>, is taken as a symbol of silence.

This refers to Paul's allegory of Hagar and Sarah.</note>)—this must be understood mystically and not literally: because there are more than ten days' journey from one to the other. Not only does Saint Augustine testify to this in the 14th book of the *Trinity*, but **Elchana** <note>Likely referring to Elkanah ben Jeroham, a figure often cited in later Kabbalistic commentaries.</note> himself, a very famous Hebrew doctor, acknowledges it: *that the law pre-existed in the word of God before it was given* <note>original Latin: "quod lex præexistebat in verbo Dei antequam daretur"</note>. 

Or, if we wish to take it from the opposite side, the law was as if pregnant with the Gospel, which it brought forth at a certain period of time, at which, through the incarnation of the Word, the great wonders of God were manifested, following Psalm 88: *Shall thy wonders be known in the dark?* <note>original Latin: "Nũquid cognoſcẽtur in tenebris mirabilia tua?"</note> And in Psalm 119: *Open my eyes, and I will consider the wonders of thy law.* <note>original Latin: "Reuela oculos meos, & cõſiderabo mirabilia de lege tua."</note> 

If, therefore, from the word *Elohim* you come to subtract these two letters **Iah** <term>יה</term>—that is to say, the law of grace—from the natural law and the Mosaic law, they must remain entirely mute and gagged, as having been perfected and accomplished in and by the Christian law, toward which all religions must tend. 

Furthermore, let the Holy Spirit, following the attribution of his name **Elohim**, be taken for the exact severity of rigor, according to what the Kabbalists posit, who call the hard and harsh judgment **Din** <term>דין</term>, by which the world, as they say, is maintained; that is to say, that without this, which holds the wicked and perverse in check, everything would go up in flames and be turned upside down. The Savior himself seems to show this tacitly in Saint Mark 3 and Saint Luke 12, when he says: *Every one that saith a word against the Son of man, it shall be forgiven him: but unto him that shall blaspheme against the Holy Spirit, it shall not—*

...to the actions and effects of the stars and celestial bodies, or rather the intelligences that assist them, by means of appropriate and suitable materials: with words, characters, fumigations, and prayers, as if one were imprinting the figure of a seal or signet into wax, or some other similar substance. All of this is accompanied by what the Hebrews call *Kavanah* <term>Cavanah</term> <note>Hebrew: *Kavanah*, meaning "intention" or "direction." In Jewish mysticism, it refers to the intense mental focus and sincerity required during prayer or ritual.</note>, a strong and elevated intention, without which nothing can be properly done; for, approaching very near to ecstasy or the ravishment of the spirit, it holds the same place in these marvelous operations as the soul does in our body, which it vivifies. Furthermore, there are no occult faculties or virtues separated like seeds—some in heaven, others on earth—such as the mold of the matter one wishes to cast, or like our interior concepts in relation to the words or letters that express them, that the mage cannot unite together and bring into action. Nevertheless, whatever miraculous work one might produce, whether by the way of magic or the Kabbalah <term>Cabale</term> <note>Also spelled Kabbalah; a system of Jewish mysticism exploring the nature of the divine.</note>, or in any other sort, one must refer the entire principal effect to the will and power of God. For just as man naturally produces his likeness, which is his work—as the creation of the world is that of the sovereign Creator—in the same way, the mage produces his own by artifice. But as natural things are more perfect than those of art, which only imitates nature according to Aristotle in the second book of the *Physics* <term>Phyſiques</term>, so are divine things to be more esteemed and are incomparably more accomplished than those of nature. This was even testified by the enchanters of Pharaoh in the 8th chapter of Exodus: when Aaron, extending his rod, brought forth gnats from the dust; for not being able to do the same by their charms, they were constrained to admit, *the finger of God is here* <note>original Latin: "digitus Dei hic est"</note>. Thus, all the words, all the sacred names, characters, figures, signs, and formal numbers—which have more power than any material quality—along with their perfumes, lights, and other such external things that support them, have no virtue or efficacy in magic or Kabbalah except insofar as they conform to the voice and the hand of the sovereign God, that is to say, to the word and scripture. From this it follows that strange words which signify nothing to us—which nevertheless Zoroaster and Orpheus forbid us to alter or change for others, especially the Hebrew ones, which are the primitive source of all others—can do more than meaningful and intelligible words. For although there are many words that do not seem made for pleasure or by chance, yet signify nothing in any language whatsoever, they might nevertheless be just like a writing in cipher; while those who do not understand the secret can draw no sense from it, others who know the artifice know very well how to discern what it means. The same could be true of characters and words which, being unknown to us, do not fail to have some significance to the spirits to whom they are addressed. This has been treated by us incidentally regarding magic, because it is the science of the celestial world, which comprises within itself the ten heavens or Spheres <term>Spheres</term> <note>In the Ptolemaic/medieval worldview, the universe was composed of concentric spheres with Earth at the center.</note>, which are the instruments and means through which the divinity acts in us: namely, nine mobile spheres, and the tenth firm and stable, called by some the Empyrean heaven <term>ciel empriree</term> <note>The highest heaven, believed to be the dwelling place of God and the blessed.</note>, and in the scripture the heaven of heaven: *Behold, the heaven is the Lord your God's* <note>original Latin: "en domini Dei tui coelum est"</note>, and *the heaven of heavens in Deuteronomy 10* <note>original Latin: "coelum coeli au Deuteron. 10."</note>, and in the plural again the heavens of heavens, which is not without mystery in the 3rd book of Kings 8: *If indeed the heaven, and the heaven of heavens...* <note>original Latin: "Si enim coelum, & coeli coelo-"</note>
