...cannot contain Thee <note>The Latin fragment *rum te capere non possunt* likely completes the phrase *Caeli caelorum te capere non possunt*, meaning "The heavens of heavens cannot contain Thee" (1 Kings 8:27).</note>, and by reason of its firm stability, the land of the living: *When I shall set glory in the land of the living* <note>original Latin: *Cùm dedero gloriam in terra viuentium*</note> Ezekiel 26. In which is planted the tree of life and the throne of God, seated and placed on this sea of glass resembling crystal, mentioned in Revelation 4 and 15. And whoever would wish to report here the rare and marvelous things of this magic, it would never be finished; whoever wishes to see the particulars should read, after the ancients: Gaspar Peucer in his books on the principal types of divinations; Giambattista della Porta in his books on natural and supernatural magic; Johann Weyer in his books on the *Deceptions of Demons* <note>original title: *De Praestigiis Daemonum*</note>; Girolamo Cardano in his books on the subtlety and variety of things; Jean Bodin in his book on Sorcerers and the *Theater of Nature*; and Benedictus Pererius in his books on magic. 

And to return to the aforementioned numerations and measurements of the ten <term>Sephirot</term> <note>In Kabbalah, these are the ten attributes or emanations through which the Infinite (Ein Sof) reveals itself and creates the universe.</note>, ten being the end of all numbers, and consequently the measure of all measures, one appropriates the ten categories or <term>predicaments</term> of <term>dialectic</term> <note>A term for logic. The "ten categories" refer to Aristotle's classification of all possible kinds of being or predicates.</note>, which comprise all the circumstances of things: namely essence or substance, quality, quantity, relation: *when* (denoting time) or *where* (place), situation or posture: state, the agent, and the patient. 

Then there are five <term>predicables</term> <note>Logical terms derived from Porphyry that classify the relationship between a subject and its predicate: genus, species, difference, property, and accident.</note>: the genus, the species, the difference, the property, and the accident, which two groups together make fifteen. This is the same value denoted by the two letters of the name יה <term>Jah</term> <note>A shortened, poetic form of the Hebrew name for God.</note>, of which the *Yod* (which is worth ten) represents the ten predicaments, and the *He* (five) represents the five predicables, because all things were made by the virtue of this holy name. 

Furthermore, to these aforementioned ten <term>Sephirot</term> and to the ten celestial spheres correspond the ten commandments of the Law, according to Abraham Aben Ezra <note>A significant medieval Spanish rabbi, scholar, and philosopher.</note> in his Commentary on them. Of these, the first shows the most simple unity of the FATHER, who is like the base and foundation of all: *I am the Lord your God who brought you out of Egypt from the house of servitude: You shall have no other God but me*. This relates to the tenth immobile sphere, as it sustains the throne of God: *Heaven is my throne, and the earth is my footstool* <note>original Latin: *Cælum sedes mea est, & terra scabellum pedum meorum*</note>, in Isaiah 66. From there He moves the first mover <note>The *Primum Mobile*, the outermost moving sphere in the Ptolemaic model of the universe.</note>, and consequently all the rest: *All things rejoice when the Father moves them* <note>original Latin: *Gaudent omnes mouente Patre*</note>, says Saint Dionysius in his *Celestial Hierarchy*, speaking of the intelligences, which, being moved, move the spheres and the celestial bodies over which they preside. 

Thus, Hermes <note>Referring to Hermes Trismegistus, the legendary Hellenistic figure associated with the Hermetic writings.</note> defines God as a circle whose center is everywhere and whose circumference is nowhere. This is quite clearly represented by the two digits of the number 10, where the first (the 1) is like an indivisible point or the center which is everywhere—for there is no number where unity cannot be found, since they all start from it and are nothing other than a heap of units strung together—and the *0* or zero, which is round in the manner of a circumference, is said to be in no place because by itself it does nothing. In this way, it relates to the <term>Ein Sof</term> <note>original: *Ensoph*. In Kabbalah, this refers to God prior to self-manifestation; the Infinite or Boundless.</note>, the non-finite or infinite.

*The second commandment: You shall not make any representation or likeness of anything that is in the heavens above, or below on the earth, nor in the water, to worship them*, corresponds to the 9th Sphere and the first mover, which moves and carries with it all the other underlying spheres in 24 hours; and also to the Son, who is the first movement of all things, proceeding from the immobile Father. On this subject, Boethius says:

> Creator of the lands and of the heavens, who commands time
> To proceed from eternity: and remaining stable, Thou givest all things to be moved.
> <note>original Latin: *Terrarúmque cælíque Sator, qui tempus ab æuo / Ire iubes: stabilísque manens das cuncta moueri.*</note>

### History of the Origin of the...

...Which Son has banished and extirpated all the idolatries of the world, wherever his Gospel is proclaimed. **The third commandment: You shall not take the name of the Lord your God in vain: for the Lord will not hold him guiltless who takes his name in vain.** <note>Exodus 20:7</note> This corresponds to the eighth sphere where all the fixed stars are located, the Zodiac with the 12 signs, and the 48 principal stars depicted as one sees them in Hyginus <note>Gaius Julius Hyginus (c. 64 BC – AD 17), a Roman author whose *De Astronomica* described the constellations.</note> and several other astrologers. And one must not think it a matter of mere whim that these celestial images are formed from several stars in the manner they are represented; for many excellent men of old—Chaldeans, Indians, and Egyptians—observed them to be such by means of certain instruments suited to that purpose. This they were able to do and discern more clearly and distinctly than we can, because of the great plains of those regions and the continual serenity of the sky that reigns there. 

Furthermore, because the principal celestial virtues consist in this eighth sphere, and since the Holy Spirit is the dispenser of all virtues, it is attributed to Him for this reason, being the third in order, just as He is the third person of the **TRINITY**. Additionally, to take the name of God in vain and to abuse it is like a sin particularly against the **HOLY SPIRIT**, just as perjury is a sin against one's own conscience, which symbolizes for him that which is not forgiven in this world or the next: *You shall not swear falsely by my name, nor shall you profane the name of your God* <note>original Latin: *Non peierabis in nomine meo, nec pollues nomen Dei tui.* Leviticus 19:12.</note>. **The fourth: Remember to sanctify the Sabbath day.** This corresponds to the Sphere of Saturn, which is an unfortunate, malicious, and harmful planet. For this reason, Moses judged that nothing should be undertaken or done on that day, but rather one should remain entirely at rest and devote oneself to divine service; because Saturn presides over the first hour of Saturday, which begins in the evening at nightfall, just as Mars does over the last, which is also pernicious on its part. This does not occur on any of the other days. For this reason, the *Zohar* <note>original: *Zoar*; the foundational work in the literature of Jewish Kabbalah.</note> and other Kabbalists allege that evil spirits have more power to harm on all fourth and seventh nights, during which these two planets preside, than at any other time of the week. 

**The fifth: Honor your Father and your Mother, so that your days may be long upon the land.** This corresponds to the Sphere of Jupiter, which is benevolent and represents peace, love, piety, and mercy—as does also the sphere or numeration <term>Chesed</term> <note>The fourth Sephirah in Kabbalah, representing Mercy or Loving-kindness.</note> and the divine name *El*, which is attributed to it. **The sixth: You shall not kill.** This corresponds to Mars, who presides over wars, murders, bloodshed, pillaging, and other such violence. **The seventh: You shall not commit adultery.** This corresponds to Venus, following the opinion of the <term>Brahmins</term> and <term>Gymnosophists</term> <note>Ancient Indian philosophers known to the Greeks for their asceticism and wisdom.</note> along with other philosophers of India, who place her above the Sun, though the more common opinion places her below. And because she corresponds to the numeration <term>Netzach</term> <note>original: *Nefach*; the seventh Sephirah, meaning Victory or Endurance.</note>, or Victory, this admonishes us that we must strive to conquer our illicit lusts. **The eighth: You shall not steal.** This corresponds to the Sun, which ravishes, withdraws, and steals from all the stars their clarity and light, which it extinguishes and obscures. **The ninth: You shall not bear false witness against your neighbor.** This corresponds to Mercury, to whom the tongue is attributed, so much so that in their sacrifices the Pagans offered him this part of the victims; he is, moreover, the patron of all trickery, deceit, deception, and fraud. **And the tenth: You shall not covet your neighbor's wife, nor his house, his servant, his ox, nor anything else of his substance.** This corresponds to the Moon, the lowest sphere...

-># Languages of this Universe.<-

...the lowest of all the celestial bodies, just as greed is the most infinite and abject passion of our soul. These ten **Sephirot** or measures <note>The Sephirot are the ten attributes or emanations in Kabbalah through which the Infinite (Ein Sof) reveals itself.</note> are furthermore called by the Kabbalists by the name **Belimah** <note>original Hebrew: בלימה</note>, that is to say, "without any addition," just as simple numbers are the very basis and first origin of all apprehension and demonstration. For just as Characters <note>referring to written symbols or magical sigils</note>, being more composite and material, are suited to **Magic**—which is an intermediate operation between celestial and terrestrial things, and which **Chemistry** takes as its subject in its arts, using fire as its instrument—so too the heat of the sky, the sun, and the stars which imprint themselves here below is the instrument of nature: *for once heat is removed, no motion at all occurs* <note>original Latin: "sublato enim calore nullus omnino fit motus"</note>, says the philosopher Alphidius <note>Alphidius was a legendary figure in medieval alchemy, often cited in Western hermetic texts.</note>. Numbers are likewise more suited to the **Kabbalah**, as they are an access and passage from celestial things to intelligible things; as for letters, they hold a middle place between numbers and figures. In this regard, this word *Belimah* <note>original Hebrew: בלימה</note> also signifies taciturnity and silence, to show that divine things can be reached sooner and more conveniently by a profound meditation of thought gathered within oneself, than by a certain chirping of sophists; and yet the **Pythagorean philosophy**, more spiritual than any other among the gentiles, was founded upon this. 

But to say something more of the **Sephirot** that is closer to and more in conformity with Scripture, and even with numbers: they are represented by the three letters called "mothers" in the *Yetzirah* <note>The *Sefer Yetzirah* or "Book of Formation," one of the oldest books of Jewish mysticism.</note>, which symbolize the three elements; and by the seven "doubles," which denote the seven planets, for whom the twelve remaining "simple" letters—representing the twelve signs of the zodiac—serve as dwellings, to complete the number of twenty-two. This follows the example that every circle contains in its circumference twenty-two sevenths of its diameter <note>A reference to the approximation of Pi (22/7).</note>. In this manner, just as from the various aspects of the seven planets in these twelve signs (where they play as if at a game of bars) all bodies come to be produced in the four elements where they spread out, so too from the Characters of writing that symbolize them are formed the names of all things composed of them. 

All these considerations tend toward no other goal than to draw us closer to the **Divinity**, and Divinity closer to us, through the intellect which it has pleased Him to bestow upon us. This intellect joins us to Him by means of His emanations, which the Kabbalists call vehicles and garments; for according to their traditions, *no spiritual thing descending below operates without some veil or covering* <note>original French: "nulle chose spirituelle descendant en bas, n'opere sans quelq. voile ou couuerture"</note>. Experience shows us that we cannot endure the dazzling rays of the sun by looking at them directly and uncovered as well as we can when they are refracted by the interposition of some crepe or cloth, which somewhat deadens and blunts their overly penetrating light. In this same way, **Moses** showed himself to the children of **Israel** upon returning from his conference with God, who had imprinted such a sparkling clarity upon his face that they could not bear it. These numerations are again compared by them to an overturned tree with its roots upward; and indeed man, who is fashioned in the likeness of God, is even said by the great **Aristotle** to be a tree turned upside down. This conforms to the aforementioned traditions: *Man is planted in the garden of pleasure by the roots of his hair: of which it is said in Canticles 7: "The hair of your head is like royal purple bound in channels"* <note>original Latin: "Plantatus est homo in horto voluptatis per radices capillorũ: de quibus dicitur in Canticis 7. Comæ capitis tui sicut purpura regis iuncta canalibus." A reference to Song of Solomon 7:5.</note>; namely, these influxes from above.

## History of the Origin of the

...proceeding from the living source of divine existence, whose root, which is **EHIEH** <note>original: "EHIEH," a Hebrew name for God meaning "I Am" or "I Will Be"</note>, is attached to the intelligible world, the true land of the living, as it is written: *"He will pluck up your root from the land of the living"* <note>original Latin: "Radicem tuam euellet de terra viuentium," from Psalm 52</note>. And the trunk is the sacred and most holy **Tetragrammaton** <note>The "four-letter" name of God, יהוה, often rendered as Yahweh or Jehovah</note>, the ineffable origin of all things, along with its primary branches, which are the divine names mentioned above. These, like branches that sprout further shoots, suckers, and offshoots to serve as grafts, produce many surnames and sub-surnames. In this way, the entire Law comes to be like a graft upon the single Tetragrammaton, **Jehovah**, in the same manner that a complete clause in a piece of writing consists of words, words of syllables, syllables of letters, and all letters of the **Yod** <note>The Hebrew letter י, the smallest in the alphabet and the first letter of the Tetragrammaton, often seen by mystics as the atom from which all other letters are formed</note>, which is the beginning of the ineffable name, to which it is even equivalent. 

For it is also used to represent the entire word, held anciently in such respect and honor by the Israelites that only the High Priest alone wore it engraved on a golden plate, called by the Hebrews the **Tzitz Zahab** <note>original: ציץ זהב, meaning "Golden Plate" or "Golden Flower"</note>, upon the front of his miter. Only he was permitted to express it by its characters, and even then, only once a year, on the tenth day of the Moon of the month of **Tizri** <note>The Hebrew month of Tishrei</note>, which corresponds to our September, called **Yom Kippur** <note>original: *Iom Hachepurim*, the Day of Atonement</note>, the Day of Forgiveness, on which was celebrated the great propitiation and general absolution of all the Jewish people. He would utter it deep within the Sanctuary by himself, following a secret tradition of the **Kabbalah** revealed by God to Moses, and from him to Aaron, in a way quite different from how the sequence and arrangement of its characters sound. 

And as **Rabbi Joseph** <note>Likely Rabbi Joseph Gikatilla, a famous 13th-century Kabbalist and author of the *Sha'are Orah* (Gates of Light)</note> testifies in his *Gates of Light*, the ancient Jews considered it an infallible article of faith that whoever uttered it by its own letters, without a very urgent necessity, would have no part in the world to come. This is because it is communicable only to the Creator alone, and there is nothing in it that is common between God and His creatures—unlike names such as **Tzadik** (Righteous), **Dayan** (Judge), **Hannun** (Gracious and Merciful), and other similar ones. This name represents the being of God, which is incomprehensible to all creatures, and His substance, with His intrinsic properties and His very essence, through a manifest and most perfect showing, without any ambiguity, mixture, or any regard or relation to the outside world. 

All other names are derived from divine operations, except for this one, which for this reason is called the Great Name: *"What will you do for your great name?"* <note>original Latin: "Quid facies magno nomini tuo?" from Joshua 7</note>. It does not signify through effects, but rather through a pure existence, for which it is most redoubtable and awe-inspiring, according to the 98th Psalm: *"Let them praise your great name, for it is terrible and holy"* <note>original Latin: "Confiteantur nomini tuo magno, quoniam terribile & sanctum est"</note>; and in the second letter to Timothy, chapter 2: *"Let everyone who calls on the name of the Lord depart from iniquity"* <note>original Latin: "Discedat ab iniquitate omnis qui inuocat nomen Domini"</note>. 

Thus it is and was, but it is not read according to the order and sequence of its characters; for it is expressly forbidden in Exodus 20 to take the name of God in vain, which the Rabbis interpret as uttering it from the lips rashly and without cause. Even the Gentiles, conforming in this to Hebrew traditions, acknowledge that one must not importune the divinity out of season or abuse His grace and goodness rashly and at every turn. This is why the Church has appointed for us certain days and hours for prayers, more particularly at one time than another, according to Psalm 55.

Furthermore, to express it by its characters is understood as it being ineffable <note>Too sacred or great to be spoken</note>, for they are all vowels, so that one could not easily discern what its pronunciation should be, given that the points and accents <note>The Hebrew vowel markings (niqqud) which were added later to clarify pronunciation</note> which could clarify all that were not yet added. Some pronounce it *Jahue*, which sounds almost like "God" joined with human nature, because *Jah* signifies God, specifically of mercy; the *Vav* thereafter is a connective particle; and the second *He*, which is at the end, denotes the human nature of **Christ**. Others utter and transcribe it as *Jova*, but improperly, because one should rather say *Jehovah*; others *Jeve*. But wherever it is encountered in the Scripture, they used to read it as **Adonai** <note>Hebrew for "Lord"</note>, as that word is an access and entry to reach the ineffable name. And thus, in the ten **Sephirot** <note>The ten attributes or emanations in Kabbalah through which the Infinite reveals itself</note>, *Adonai* is placed as the first at the bottom, like the first step to climb up to **Ehieh** <note>The divine name "I Am," associated with the highest Sephirot</note>, and the tenth in descending.

# Languages of this Universe. 199

...most secret and profound mysteries of divinity, to the **intelligible world** <note>The realm of pure thought and divine forms, as opposed to the physical world</note>, upon which depend—like two clear streams proceeding from a living, eternal source—everything that the human spirit can achieve in the knowledge of the admirable effects of nature and art in the **sensible world** <note>The physical world perceived through the senses</note>. For there is such an analogy and relationship between God and His works that they cannot be well understood except reciprocally, one through the other. Nature invites us to apply our understanding there, especially since from this relationship arises one of the most secret and ingenious methods of secret writing or ciphers. These consist of characters that are all equal, without any difference in form, quantity, or color: such as a sky all scattered with stars, a tree clothed in its leaves, a sea agitated by waves, or points and lines that are all similar. In short, everything that nature produces that is perceptible to our eyes, or that we can imagine in our thoughts—as we have clearly shown above—indicates that this entire universe seems like a book in which the wonders of the Creator are written, incessantly announcing His praises to those, at least, who know how to read it.

For it is a cipher, and a very hidden one for the most part, for those who contemplate the celestial bodies in no other way than they would a great number of burning lamps in a Jewish synagogue or a Mahometan mosque—or else, according to the philosopher **Xenophanes** <note>A pre-Socratic Greek philosopher (c. 570–475 BC) who famously suggested that stars were actually clouds of fire or glowing coals</note>, like so many large coals lit at night and extinguished by day, without looking further into their order, placement, and disposition.

We leave aside the intelligences <note>Angelic or spiritual beings believed to govern the planets</note> that invisibly assist them, and I restrict myself to what can be perceived by the senses, upon which all efficacy in this case depends. This is what the <term>Gematria</term> <note>A Kabbalistic method of interpreting Hebrew scriptures by correlating words with numerical values</note> of the Hebrews discovers for us; it is the source of all secret ways of writing and ciphers which must be taken into account. It introduces us through true <term>Arithmetic</term> and <term>Geometry</term>—which <term>Pythagoras</term> <note>The Greek mathematician and philosopher who saw numbers as the fundamental reality of the universe</note> calls the harmonies and proportions, and considers the principles of all things—into infinite revelations of secrets from the three non-vulgar sciences attributed, as has already been said, to the three worlds.

For just as in a beautiful palace, where there was first on the lowest floor a great quantity of exquisite utensils and furniture, such as wooden household goods, linens, tapestries, and other such conveniences for human life; then above, inside some secret wardrobe, many sideboards of gold and silver plate, vessels, and cups; and at the very top, a cabinet of precious stones: to see what is inside these three rooms, which are locked with strong padlocks and ironwork, one would need to have the keys. The same is true of the three worlds, of which the three <term>occult sciences</term> <note>Specifically referring here to the esoteric branches of mathematics and divine philosophy</note> are the true keys, which alone can unlock for us the secret treasures within. As it is said in <term>Isaiah</term> 29:
> The vision of all these things will be to you like the words of a sealed book, which, when presented to one who knows letters to read it, he will answer that he cannot, because it is closed; and the ignorant person will say the same.

But in the very same way that from the same turf or clod of earth are produced good, healthy herbs for the human body along with poisonous and harmful ones; and from the same dew imprinted on the flowers, the bee sucks and prepares its graceful liquor of honey, while the spider, quite to the contrary, draws a mortal, pestilential poison; so from the same text of **Holy Scripture**, the faithful and obedient son of the Church...

Catholic Church draws the true meaning proper for its salvation—and the stubborn heretic, a false and erroneous understanding which leads it to perdition—so too, there have never been lacking in any place, nor in any profession or doctrine, minds strayed from the right path. These individuals have perverted all this beautiful knowledge into vain abuses, illicit curiosities, and impious superstitions: some under the cover and name of **Kabbalah** <note>A tradition of Jewish mysticism focused on the esoteric interpretation of Scripture</note>; others under the title and quality of **Magic**—a science formerly so honored that Plato, in the *Charmides*, calls it the true medicine of the soul (by which the soul acquires a perfect tranquility and the body a healthy state). In the *First Alcibiades*, he notes that it was accustomed to be taught to the children of the great kings of Persia by their theologians and philosophers called ***Mages*** <note>The priestly caste of ancient Persia, from which the word "magic" originates</note>, in order to teach them to form their empire and rule upon the pattern and model of the order and governance of the universe.

And others, finally, have decried the entire third science, called **Chemistry** or **Alchemy**, under the lures and false baits of a mountain of riches born in an instant through imaginary metallic transmutations. Those good men who so carefully employed their study in this field never aspired to such things. Rather, they sought through it remedies more sovereign than common ones to counter the accidents to which the **frailty of the flesh** <note>The physical weaknesses and illnesses of the human body</note> subjects us. They also wished to smelt metals by this same means—the most beautiful, permanent, and admirable substance that nature produces. For besides the diversity of ornaments coming from them, with which a person may be adorned and dressed; besides so many conveniences that human life receives from them in agriculture, navigation, and in all sorts of arts and trades (which without them would remain lacking); and finally, the medicines made from them, both for external and internal use—their wonder in all this is that they can be metamorphosed in infinite ways without losing their specific form. They always restore themselves to their original state (unless by a very ingenious artifice and very long preparations), even though they may have been reduced to impalpable powder, lime, salt, water, oil, glass, enamel, and similar alterations.

Their intention was as stated above, and not a vain and frivolous greed: to discover through this elementary science the hidden progress of nature. Nature, according to **Empedocles** and **Anaxagoras** <note>Pre-Socratic Greek philosophers who theorized about the elements of the universe</note>, is nothing other than the mixing and separation of elements, with which this chemistry or alchemy occupies itself. For this reason, it is called **Spagyric** <term>Spagyric: A term for alchemy meaning to "separate and re-combine" (from the Greek words *spao* and *ageiro*)</term>, as it separates and rejoins substances. In the revelation of these beautiful secrets, the glory of Him who is the first author of them is manifested, taking His delight therein, just as we His creatures do in the investigation of their hidden and latent causes, along with their properties and effects. This is one of the most favorable nourishments for the soul; for it serves us as a ladder to mount up high, and an elevation of our thought out of the sensuality of this human husk. This husk seeks only, by a troublesome counterweight, to pull the soul down and keep it submerged in its idle pleasures and beastly lusts, with the help of that false and treacherous deceiver, our inveterate adversary and cursed **ancient serpent**. He is named by the Kabbalists ***Hazael***, father of ***Tumah and Lilit*** <note>In this context, personifications of impurity and filth in mystical traditions</note>—pollution and filth—who, as the **Zohar** <note>The foundational work of Jewish Kabbalah</note> says, is the final end of all flesh where he predominates, and in the blood, as they are of the earth. **Pythagoras** held that to the **binary** <note>The number two, which in Pythagorean philosophy represents duality, division, and the material world, as opposed to the "monad" or unity of God</note>—that is, the number two, which he takes for the devil and the evil principle—belongs all the matter of this visible world, which he also names the binary. This is further confirmed by the fact that the Savior calls the common enemy the **prince of the world**. But the elect—**who were born, not of blood, nor of the will of the flesh, nor of the will of man, but of God** <note>original: "Qui non ex sanguinibus, neque ex voluntate carnis, neque ex voluntate viri, sed ex Deo nati sunt"</note>, as in Saint John 1—always hold themselves to the good, without wandering off the straight path. Whereas others, at the suggestion of the evil one—who is constantly listening and on the lookout to spy for characters suited to the weeds he always keeps ready to sow there—pervert good into evil (or he perverts it through them), truth into lies, and that which truly exists into smoke and frivolous, deceptive illusions.

This is not to say, however, that it should be so decried; no more than a beautiful gold vase enriched with precious stones, which, for having been employed in some infamous and filthy service, it would be too great a simplicity to wish to reject for that reason, given that it is only an external contamination which does not penetrate into its substance, which is incorruptible by nature. Is the scripture less commendable for this?

The second is taken from the 13th of Exodus: **And the Lord speaking to Moses**, until the end of verse 10: **You shall keep these ordinances**. The third from the 11th of the same: **Now when the Lord shall have introduced you**, until the end of verse 16. And the fourth from the eleventh of Deuteronomy, beginning at verse 13: **If therefore you obey**, until the end of verse 21: **As long as the heavens extend over the earth**. 

They write these with great ceremonies on **virgin parchment** <note>Parchment made from the skin of an unborn or newborn animal, considered more pure</note>, and when they kill a calf to make it, they use these words: "I sacrifice this calf here, with the intention of employing its skin to make Tephillin." Regarding the **Zairagia** <note>The *Za'iraja* was a complex divination device used by medieval Arab practitioners, involving concentric circles and letters to answer questions.</note>, we have here reduced its practice to another method; namely, by arranging the single spherical figure—which they usually form into four or five circles enveloped one within the other—into as many separate tables. This is done to make the whole system more intelligible and to shift the use of these idle divinations toward that of **Gematria** <note>A Kabbalistic method of interpreting Hebrew scriptures by calculating the numerical value of words.</note>, which concerns itself only with the true deciphering of the secret mysteries of scripture and prophetic predictions. For upon this depends true rational **Arithmancy** <note>Divination or philosophy based on the significance of numbers.</note> and formal **Geomancy** <note>The original text uses "Germantie," likely a variant or error for Geomancy, which the author links here to physical "measures" and geometric forms.</note>. The former symbolizes the intelligible world because of the subtlety of numbers, which are more essential, distant, and abstracted from matter than mere measurements; they act as the reasons, relations, and regards to which the species of the Sensible World are referred. This is much like what **Aristotle** intends to infer in the text previously cited from the 12th book of the *Metaphysics*: *Species are as numbers* <note>original: "Species ſe habent ſicut numeri"</note>. And **Geomancy**, established upon measurements as forms introduced into matter, corresponds to the sensible world that participates in matter—being more refined and formed in the heavens, and more coarse and material on the earth. All of this follows the example of the **Sephirot** <note>The ten attributes or emanations in Kabbalah through which the Infinite reveals itself.</note>, where numbers correspond to the three superior levels, and measurements correspond to the seven inferior levels.

Upon these two dependencies of **Gematria**—namely Arithmancy and the intelligible world—depend the interior conceptions of our thought; and upon **Geomancy** depends the writing that expresses them. For from the plurality of points that consist of numbers (not including that accidental projection of points scattered by chance, for that is pure nonsense without foundation from which nothing solid can be drawn), are produced lines, both straight and curved, from which letters are then formed. From letters coupled into syllables and words, a sense is procreated, which manifests and casts outward everything that the understanding can apprehend within. This sense is analogous to the spirit that vivifies the parts of a body, which are designated by the said letters, just as the body is represented by the word woven from them. This captures the natural property of each thing it signifies—at least in the **Hebrew** language, in which it is held that **Adam** imposed the true and significant names upon all things that were created.

And just as in the corruption of an individual, the form that used to be there is erased and another succeeds in its place; likewise, in a context of writing, if the letters are transposed and cast out of their previous order, position, and arrangement, the meaning that was there before is altered and changed. For in very few ways could you turn or assemble the **Hebrew** characters without a meaning always being found therein. And because letters consist of numbers and measures (which **Gematria** encompasses), and because words are formed from them—carrying within themselves the true essence and **quiddity** <note>term: quiddity (the inherent nature or "what-ness" of a thing)</note> of the thing they represent—and since this entire Universe is governed by an **intellect** spread and mixed into all its smallest parts, to which both the past and the future are present: one takes the letters of the proposed question as a foundation in this rule of the **Zairagia**. It is not, therefore, our intention to teach anything here regarding what is divinely licit or illicit through the way of <term>Gematria</term> <note>A system of assigning numerical values to letters to find hidden meanings in words.</note>. In this system, one proceeds in this manner: first, they draw a Circle for you, which they divide into four by two diameters crossing at right angles. Below that are placed the three Mother letters, <term>Aleph</term>, <term>Mem</term>, and <term>Shin</term>, which denote the three Elements: Earth, Water, and Fire. For the Hebrews admit no more than these, rejecting Air from this count, as it serves only as a kind of glue or bond for these elements and likewise fills the vacuum that nature so abhors. In place of Air, they establish here a small circle, acting as a zero (0) in cipher, which serves the calculation for pauses and distinguishing the tens. They then add the four seasons of the year and the four parts of the world, along with the four winds that come from them:

And the four Angels who preside over them in the seventh chapter of the Apocalypse. And insofar as the THREE is a symbol of the divinity and of the intelligible world <note>The realm of pure ideas and divine intellect that exists above the physical universe.</note>, and in us of the <term>Neshamah <note>original: "Nessamah"</note></term> or Intellect which corresponds to it; and the FOUR represents the Elementary realm and the body: and since every middle point participates in one and the other of its two extremes; upon which one must note what the Apostle calls the mediator composed of divinity and humanity, the "celestial Man," in the first [letter] to the Corinthians, chapter 15; they add the three to the aforementioned Quaternary to make Seven. This number represents heaven because of the equal number of planets which are its primary instruments; and upon which depend nearly all the varieties and alterations down here, both in the production of things and in the fortune of persons—at least according to <term>Trismegistus <note>Hermes Trismegistus: A legendary Hellenistic figure combining the Greek god Hermes and the Egyptian god Thoth, credited with the Hermetic writings.</note></term> in the first chapter of his <term>Poimandres <note>original: "Pymandre"</note></term>: "He consequently fashioned seven governors, who by their revolutions and Spheres envelop the sensible world; the arrangement of which is called fatal destiny." <meta>This page continues the discussion of numerology, moving from the sacred number seven to the number twelve. It explores how these mathematical patterns form a bridge between the divine realm and the physical universe, specifically through the Zodiac and sacred geometry.</meta>

### Languages of this Universe.

These two numbers, three and four, which when joined together make 7, if you multiply them by one another, will produce 12—exactly the number of signs in the Zodiac; from this, one can see the great affinity that the planets have with them. It is just as with the relationship of 7 to 12, or 6 to 8 (for 2 and 4 make 6, and 2 times 4 gives 8). These signs serve as dwellings for the planets, much like the 64 black and white squares on the back of a checkerboard <note>The author compares the astronomical grid to a game board, suggesting that the movements of the planets are like pieces in a cosmic game of chess.</note> are used for the various placements of pieces in a game of chess, and their different arrangements and "aspects" <note>In astrology, an "aspect" is the angle planets make to each other, believed to influence their power.</note> toward one another. There is nothing more suitable to represent the celestial bodies than this, just as there are the many encounters of letters—both in general writing and specifically in "square ciphers" <note>original: "chiffres carrez." This likely refers to magic squares or cryptographic grids where letters and numbers are arranged in a square for hidden meanings.</note> which contain several meanings beneath a single character. For the "gazes" and habits of the planets within the signs, when added to the four elements from which all bodies are produced, symbolize the characters of writing that constitute words.

These 12 signs, moreover, which Plato calls the "gates of Heaven," of which Capricorn is called the Ascendant because the Sun begins to rise again within it; and the crayfish <note>original: "l'escreuice." This refers to the sign of Cancer, which in older texts was often depicted as a crayfish rather than a crab.</note> the descendant, because having arrived there, it begins to decline again; these denote the 12 gates of the Holy Celestial City described in Revelation 21. To these are attributed as many Angels who assist there, divided three by three as guards for each of the four regions of Heaven: East, West, South, and North, in the exact same manner that astrologers distribute them. To each of these signs is attributed one of the twelve "simple" letters—called so because they are always pronounced in the same way—just as the signs, for their part, always remain within the same property and virtue <note>This refers to a concept from the *Sefer Yetzirah* (a Jewish mystical text), which assigns the 12 "simple" Hebrew letters to the 12 signs of the Zodiac.</note>. 

All of this can be seen in the following table, where the significance of said letters is placed alongside the 12 months, which correspond to the 12 signs. And this is the third Circle: through which it is demonstrated to us that Heaven—to which this number of 12 is so well suited—is a passage and intermediary between divine things (designated by the number three) and earthly things (represented by the number four, as they consist of the four elements). Thus, our Savior, who participates in both of these two natures <note>Refers to the Christian doctrine of Christ being both fully divine and fully human.</note>, held this number of twelve in high regard, as one can see in many places in the Gospel—and again in Revelation regarding the aforementioned Holy City, which is entirely divided by 12. Likewise, Plato did the same for his worldly city in the 5th and 6th books of *The Laws*, so closely aligned with the other that it would not be possible to do more; from which is clearly seen the great sympathy and connection <note>original: "colligance"</note> that exists between superior things and inferior ones.

...the moon in the 12 signs of the Zodiac, which it traverses in 28 days; for meanwhile, as the Sun moves away by one degree, the moon goes to catch up with it on the 29th day. And from this the fourth Circle is formed; applying to it the intelligences that preside there with the corresponding Hebrew letters and the significance of the said houses. So that when this figure of the *Zairja* <note>original: "Zairagia." The Zairja was a complex mechanical device used by medieval Arab and later European occultists to generate answers to questions through a combination of astrology, numerology, and alphabet manipulation.</note> is completed, it consists of four circles, to represent the four Elements—the principles of all things both above and below—following the Emerald Tablet of Hermes:
> That which is above is like that which is below, and vice-versa, to perform the miracles of the one thing. <note>original: "Quod est superius est sicut quod est inferius, & è conuerso, ad perpetranda miracula rei unius." This is the most famous maxim of Hermeticism, expressing the idea that the laws of the macrocosm (the universe) are mirrored in the microcosm (the human or the earth).</note>
And the Kabbalists on this same point: 
> The house of the sanctuary which is below is arranged according to the house of the sanctuary which is above. <note>original: "Domus sanctuarij quæ est inferius, disponitur iuxta domum sanctuarij quæ est superius." This reflects the Jewish mystical belief that the earthly Temple is a reflection of a celestial prototype.</note>
Of these four Circles, in imitation of the four Elements, there is one that remains firm and immobile, just as the Earth does, serving as the base and foundation for the Universe, which turns all around it: 
> He set the Earth on its foundations; it shall not be moved for ever and ever; Psalm 104. <note>original: "Fundauit Terram super stabilitatem suam, non inclinabitur in seculum seculi." The author uses this biblical verse to support a geocentric view where the Earth remains stationary while the heavens rotate.</note>
And the other three circles move following the example of the three mobile elements—Water, Air, and Fire—for the encounters of what one seeks, just as the Planets do.

Furthermore, it is somewhat complicated by matter, but possesses a very strong bodily constitution: and of these, the sages say that through their means, people for a long time received answers concerning many things of which they desired to know the truth.

Know furthermore that each of them can, whenever it pleases, take a body in any of the four elements; although their life depends on fire, and their dwelling consists in fire, along with all their actions and maintenance. The Sage says regarding these six kinds of animals that their invocation and appearance, consideration, binding, and deliverance, is sometimes good and lawful, and sometimes evil and entirely repreputable, according to the various ends for which it is applied. 

You therefore, who are a lover of **Wisdom** <note>The author uses "Sapience," referring to divine or esoteric wisdom.</note>, and curious to know the works and wonders of the Creator, do not fall into scruple or doubt that there is a difference or division between the body and the spirit regarding these six kinds of animals, for they are but one, being made and joined together inseparably forever. Furthermore, the conjunction of the spirit and the soul, from which life proceeds, is called **Wind** <note>The word used is "Vent," corresponding to the Hebrew "Ruach," which means both wind and spirit.</note> in Job, chapter 7: *Remember that my life is but a breath* <note>original Latin: "Memento quod ventus est vita mea"</note>. Thus, the **living Wind** is what we call the spirit and the soul, and it is said to be "living" when this assembly occurs without corruption. But when such a conjunction of these two occurs—namely, of the soul and the spirit—and a corruptible body intervenes with them, then the spirit and the soul, which were one, become separable from the body.

## On the Hebrew mystery of the words Urim & Thummim.

### C H A P. XXI.

<image-desc>A large decorative floral initial 'L' set in a square border, beginning the first paragraph.</image-desc>

The Hebrews were accustomed to utter the word Adonai <note>Hebrew: "My Lord"</note>, one of the Hebrew names of God, wherever the four-lettered יהוה <note>The Tetragrammaton: YHWH</note> Jehovah—the ineffable—was found. This was because it was not permissible for everyone to know how it should be pronounced, nor which vowels represented its characters; nor whether certain letters should be doubled or spoken simply. Thus, Rabbi Abina, in the book of sanctifications in the Talmud, commenting on these words from Exodus 3: *I am who I am, I was, and I shall be, this is my name eternally*, and *my memorial from generation to generation* <note>original: "Ie suis qui suis, fus & seray, c'est mon nom eternellement, & ma remembrance au siecle des siecles"</note>, states that it must not be read as it is written, *Jehovah*, but rather *Adonai*, which means Lord. Furthermore, in the book of the Sanhedrin <note>A Jewish judicial assembly and the name of a Talmudic tractate</note>, Rabbi Abba Saul affirms that whoever pronounces it openly, according to the sound of its letters, shall have no part in the world to come. Indeed, in the 24th chapter of Leviticus, it is said that an Israelite, for having blasphemed the name of God by expressing it distinctly as *Jehovah* and not *Adonai* according to custom—which was a most abominable thing to the Jews—was stoned. For this reason, this holy name, which very often in Scripture is called by a certain substitution השם *Haschem* <note>HaShem: "The Name"</note>, is called the ineffable name. This is not so much due to the impossibility of its pronunciation, but for the mysteries it carries regarding the pure essence and substance of God: Three in one most simple and absolute unity, and one in a Trinity of persons. This is a thing entirely incomprehensible to the human mind, except through faith and belief alone. By this ineffable means, we follow even what Hermes Trismegistus witnesses in the *Poimandres*: *That the name of God cannot be uttered by a human mouth*; and what the oracle of Delphic Apollo also confesses: *That his name cannot be expressed by any diction or word*. For all the letters of this Holy Name, which are only three (as we have said, the letter *He* being doubled), are comprised within the substantive verb "to be" <note>original: "Ie suis"</note>, and from them consist the three tenses: the past, the present, and the future. This denotes the immutable and permanent stability of the divine essence. Nevertheless, Moses the Egyptian <note>The philosopher Maimonides</note>, regarding the passage cited above, notes that the priests and the elders of the Council of the Hebrews would give a lesson on it to their children and disciples only once a week. This was to show them both how it should be pronounced and its significance, as well as the deep secrets and mysteries that depended upon it. But after it was suppressed in the sanctuary due to the depravity of the Israelites—for from the time of Simeon the Just <note>A High Priest in the Second Temple period</note>, shortly before the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ (who was the last of the Great Synagogue, and who blessed the people using this ineffable Tetragrammaton)—this blessing began to be performed by the name of twelve letters, and consequently by that of forty-two. Even then, these were not communicated except to those who were gentle and humble of heart, of a holy and reformed life. It was expressly forbidden to divulge them too freely; rather, they were to keep them secret in their hearts, for fear of profaning them and reducing them to contempt on one hand, and on the other, to avoid inciting the people to idolatry, until finally this myste-

God's familiar discourse. This remained in power during the time of the second tem-

sense was drawn. As when David, in the second book and chapter of Kings <note>Known as 2 Samuel in modern Bibles</note>, consults with

# History of the Origin of the

Jews, the tractate <term>Masechet Yoma</term> <note>original: "Massectah Iomah"; the section of the Talmud dealing with the Day of Atonement</note>, the treatise on the days, chapter 6. In the first place, it was not permissible for anyone except the King and the President of the Consistory <note>the Sanhedrin, or high religious court</note> to interrogate or inquire of God by this way of the <term>Urim and Thummim</term>, and even then only in matters of great importance: such as for undertaking a war, or if the Consistory—that is to say, the Court that administered justice—could not properly decide a cause or reach a resolved opinion. In these cases, the King, or the Judge who was inquiring, turned his face toward the Priest he was questioning; meanwhile, the Priest kept his own face fixed straight toward the Urim and Thummim, with the <term>Shem HaMephorash</term> <note>The "Explicit Name" of God</note> beneath it, being within the aforementioned ornament on the chest of the High Priest. Furthermore, the voice of the one who interrogated had to be soft and quiet, and not loud or haughty, but only enough to be barely heard by the Priest in distinct words. One must not ask two things at once, but only a single one, unless by chance necessity pressed for more. For even if two were proposed, the response nevertheless was given for only one, and then the letters from which the answer was to be formed—by the power of the great name of <term>Jehovah</term>—would begin to brighten and rise up above the others. Thus, the Priest, having a good means of noticing them, gathered in his mind what he saw represented there. But if he were incapable or unworthy, the letters would not illuminate or rise at all, and he would draw no response to his demand. Some have written that these Urim and Thummim were not specifically the letters of the name <term>Shem HaMephorash</term> nor any stones added to the twelve in the ornament, but rather those twelve stones alone, which would glow almost like fire if the Divinity admitted the request; otherwise, they remained in their natural state. In fact, <term>Ur</term> signifies fire; and as for <term>Thummim</term>, which comes from <term>Thom</term> <note>original Hebrew: תם</note>, meaning integrity or perfection, this denoted that these gemstones, as true and exquisite paragons of their kind, without any blemish or defect, together yielded a brilliant luster, intermingled with various colors such as one sees in opals or in the rainbow, from which the Priest, inspired by a divine fervor <note>original: "Enthusiasme"</note>, came to understand and conjecture what the Divinity foretold. But there was, in addition, the <term>Ephod</term>, which the Seventy-Two <note>The translators of the Septuagint</note> have translated as <term>epomis</term> <note>Greek: ἐπωμὶς; meaning "shoulder-piece"</note>, and Aquila <note>A 2nd-century translator of the Hebrew Bible into Greek</note> as <term>epirrhamma</term> <note>Greek: ἐπίῤῥαμμα; meaning "covering" or "garment"</note>; we would call it a <term>camail</term> <note>a short shoulder cape</note>, provided it had no hood, or a scapular that reached only to within half a foot of the belt. This Ephod, moreover, was woven of gold and three types of purple (Exodus 28 and 39), having on each shoulder-piece a large clasp and binding where was encased a <term>Soham</term> <note>original: "Sohá"; the Hebrew Shoham stone</note>, which some take for an Emerald—Josephus, in book 3 of the *Antiquities*, chapter 12, takes it for a Sardonyx—and those with the most evidence take it for an Onyx. On each of these were engraved the names of the six Tribes—namely, the six eldest sons of Jacob on the right shoulder, and the other six younger sons on the left. From these, oracles were perceptibly taken, as it is written in the First book of Kings 30 <note>1 Samuel 30 in modern bibles</note>, where David, to know from God if he should pursue those of Amalek, had the Priest Abiathar apply the Ephod to him, by means of which Ephod he obtained a response for two things all at once. But the effects of the Urim and Thummim, as well as the Ephod and the <term>Hoschen</term> <note>The Breastplate of Judgment</note>, according to the aforementioned Josephus in the place cited above, had ceased about two hundred years before he began to write, some seven-score years before the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ.

Others push it back more than 400 years, because five things were lacking in the second temple that used to be in the first, as is contained in the <term>tractate Yoma</term> <note>original: "traicté Ioma"; the Talmudic volume concerning the Day of Atonement</note> chapter 1; and in the commentaries of <term>Rabbi Kimhi</term> <note>David Kimhi (c. 1160–1235), a preeminent medieval Jewish biblical commentator and grammarian</note> on Psalm 84 and Haggai. These were: the Ark of the Covenant, with the mercy seat and the Cherubim; the fire which burned continually upon the bronze altar, where sacrifices were burned in the open air without ever being extinguished by rain, snow, wind, or other atmospheric conditions—this fire having been sent from heaven onto a burnt offering in the time of Moses and Aaron, as seen in Leviticus 9. It maintained itself without fading until the building of the first temple by Solomon. At that time, it was renewed again from heaven and lasted until the time of King Manasseh and the Babylonian captivity, when the Priests hid it in the depths of a well; upon the return, their successors, thinking to draw it out, found in its place a thick water which, when poured over the sacrifices, caught fire, as is recorded in 2 Maccabees, chapter 1. The third thing was the presence of God, called in Exodus chapter 40 the <term>Shekhinah</term> <note>original: שכינה; the dwelling or settled presence of the Divine</note>, which manifested around the Ark. Then <term>Nebuah</term> <note>original: נבואה; Prophecy</note> or Prophecy; and finally the Oracle of the <term>Urim and Thummim</term>. Furthermore, inside the Ark were contained the tables of the Decalogue <note>The Ten Commandments</note>, the rod of Aaron still adorned with its leaves, flowers, and almonds, the vessel filled with Manna, the vial of holy oil for anointing the Kings and Prophets of Israel, and the chest of the Philistines' offering mentioned in 1 Kings chapter 6. Additionally, there were the fragments that remained of the first two tables that Moses broke in Exodus 32, which were engraved clear through from one side to the other so that they could be read from both sides—as <term>Rabbi Solomon</term> <note>Rashi (1040–1105), the most influential medieval commentator on the Torah and Talmud</note> confirms—but differently. Their ancient traditions speak of it thus: <term>The closed Mem and the Samekh in the tablets stood by a miracle</term> <note>original: "Mem Setumah, Vesamech, Beluchth Beniaiaion hauu"; a reference to the Talmudic teaching (Shabbat 104a) that because the letters were carved all the way through the stone, the centers of the circular letters ם (final Mem) and ס (Samekh) had to be miraculously suspended in mid-air</note>, meaning that the closed or final Mem ם, and the Samekh ס, were a source of great wonder because they were closed all the way around. Consequently, it was necessary for them to be as if suspended in the air without holding onto anything. This manner of the Oracle of Urim and Thummim, where it was necessary to rearrange the letters until some meaning was obtained, was not far removed from that of the Pythian Apollo in Delphi and many other pagan oracles, where one had to organize the confusion of their entanglements and muddled responses into distinct and declarative words. Therefore, by all the points deduced above, we learn that the Hebrews hold that <term>Urim</term> <note>original: האורים</note> signifies the truth and perfection of things, as they take from subsequent passages of the Bible. Some interpret this word as "Doctrine," or more properly "illustrations of truth" and all sorts of perfections, as <term>George the Venetian</term> <note>Francesco Giorgio (1465–1540), also known as Zorzi, a Franciscan friar and Christian Kabbalist</note> does in several places in his *Harmony of the World*, deriving this word from <term>Or</term> <note>original: אור</note>, which signifies light. In this, <term>Münster</term> <note>Sebastian Münster (1488–1552), a German cartographer and Hebrew scholar</note> and <term>Pagninus</term> <note>Santes Pagnino (1470–1541), a Dominican philologist and Hebraist</note> agree in their Hebrew Dictionaries on this word, which along with that of <term>Thummim</term> <note>original: התמים</note> mentioned in Exodus 28, Leviticus 8, and Deuteronomy 33—stemming from <term>Thom</term> <note>original: תם</note> which signifies integrity or perfection—are pure Hebrew words translated by the Seventy-Two Interpreters <note>The Septuagint, the earliest Greek translation of the Hebrew Bible</note> as "declaration of truth" or "illuminations and perfections." The <term>Chaldean Paraphrast</term> <note>The Targum, an Aramaic translation/paraphrase of the Hebrew Bible</note> left them without translation, because the Hebrews were accustomed to hiding and concealing their secrets in significant words. Some of the Hebrews have called these words <term>Ruach HaKodesh</term> <note>original: רוח הקדש; the Holy Spirit</note>...

# History of the Origin of [Languages]

The Holy Spirit, according to Pierre Costau in his *Type of the Messiah* <note>original: "P. Costus en son Type du Messihah"; Pierre Costau was a 16th-century scholar who wrote on emblems and biblical types</note>, and to put it briefly, this **Urim and Thummim** was a certain tablet in which twelve precious stones were encased, with the names of the twelve children of Jacob engraved upon them. This tablet, named <term>Hoshen</term> <note>original: "חשן" (Hoshen); the Priestly Breastplate</note>, hung by two small chains upon the chest of the High Priest, as can be seen in Exodus chapter twenty-eight and Leviticus chapter eight. It contained several unique features and mysteries described by Rabbis Solomon <note>likely Rashi, the preeminent medieval commentator</note> and Nehemias, among others, stating that this **Urim and Thummim** was a work of the Eternal just as much as the tables of the Decalogue <note>The Ten Commandments</note>, both having been given together by God to Moses on Mount Sinai, as I have noted previously.

This **Urim and Thummim** was used in this manner: if the matter requested of God through the High Priest was to succeed, the stones of the **Hoshen**, upon the inquiry being made, would give off a vivid light, or the same priest, inspired by God, would say what would happen. This can be seen in the places cited above, in Numbers 27, Ezra 2, and Nehemiah 7; and more clearly in Josephus <note>Flavius Josephus, the first-century Romano-Jewish historian</note> Book 3, Chapter 9; Book 6, Chapters 7 and 15; and Book 8, Chapter 2. The Greeks called this **Hoshen** the <term>Oracle</term> <note>original: "λόγιον" (logion)</note>, meaning a divine utterance; the Latins called it the *pectorale* <note>breastplate</note> or *rationale*. Some Talmudists interpret **Urim** as the sacred names by the power of which the hidden letters on the said tablet became elucidated, and **Thummim** as those which made the said letters visible and apparent.

The Kings of Israel were accustomed to asking counsel of God through this **Urim and Thummim** in all their actions of consequence; if no answer was drawn from it, it was a sign of the ire and wrath of God. For this reason, Saul, having been forsaken by the Eternal, found no answer either by Prophet, or by dream, or by **Urim and Thummim**, as is contained in the 1st book of Kings, chapter 28 <note>In modern Bibles, this is 1 Samuel 28</note>. Then this Saul said that a sorceress should be found for him who had a diabolical spirit to know the outcome of the battle, in which he died. On the contrary, David always had an answer by **Urim and Thummim**, by the vision of some Prophet, or by dream, as is contained in the 2nd book of Kings, chapters 2 and 5 <note>In modern Bibles, 2 Samuel</note>. It is a very certain thing that in former times among the Hebrews, God declared His will and deliberation by three principal means: namely, by **Urim and Thummim**, vision, and dream.

We even read in the Hebrew doctors that although the Oracle of the **Urim and Thummim** ceased after the return from Babylon, the Jews nevertheless confess that a certain divine voice was always heard in the temple, which Yehoshua son of Levi, Joseph Albo, and others have called in their Hebrew language <term>Bath Kol</term> <note>original: "בת קול" (Bath Kol); literally "daughter of a voice"</note>, which the Greeks call <term>Echo</term> <note>original: "Ηχω"</note>. This was the resonance of a voice which, coming to form and strike within certain cavities suited for it, was accustomed to emerge from there with the air it struck. Regarding this, Elias Levita in his *Thesbite* <note>Elijah Levita (1469–1549), a Hebrew grammarian and scholar; *The Tishbi* is his dictionary of Rabbinic Hebrew</note> says these words:

> "And they say **Bath Kol** is not a true or solid voice, but the daughter of a voice: the use of which was former after prophecy had ceased. Moreover, those who are skilled in the Kabbalistic art <note>The tradition of Jewish mysticism</note> say that it is the voice of a certain divine power, which is called **Bath Kol**, and perhaps it is so. The Commentator of the Hebrew book titled **Pirke Avot** <note>Ethics of the Fathers, a collection of ethical teachings from the Mishnaic period</note> says **Bath Kol**, if you interpret it literally, sounds like the daughter of a voice; thus they formerly called the voice which sounded from heaven, and which, as the Hebrews say, was one degree among the degrees of the Holy Spirit. It was, however, the common voice of the temple..."

...the time of the second temple, after prophecy had already ceased, as had the **Urim and Thummim**. For five things were lacking in the second temple which were present in the first temple, namely: the Ark, the Mercy Seat <note>original Latin: "Propitiatorium"</note>, the Cherubim, the Perpetual Fire, the presence of the Divinity <note>the Shekhinah</note>, the Holy Spirit, and the **Urim and Thummim**. Furthermore, in the New Testament we read more than once that the <term>Bath Kol</term> <note>original: "Bath Kol"; literally "Daughter of a Voice," understood as a divine echo or heavenly voice</note> came from heaven and bore witness to Christ, as in Matthew 3, when he was baptized by John in the Jordan, and behold, a voice from heaven said: "This is my beloved son, in whom I am well pleased." Similarly, in Matthew 17, when he was transformed on the mountain before his disciples. Likewise, in John 12, a voice came from heaven, saying: "I have both glorified it and will glorify it again," etc. And who does not see the mystery here? Namely, that God, by this voice which they called the *Bath Kol*, wished to prepare the world and accustom it to that true heavenly voice, which is Christ our Savior, in whom God the Father wished to be heard henceforth, according to that very command: "Hear him."

Guy Le Fèvre de la Boderie <note>a 16th-century French Orientalist and poet</note>, in his Syro-Chaldaic dictionary, speaks of this at length in the interpretation of this word. And so that we leave nothing noteworthy in this place without explaining it, we shall say that there were ten preeminences and dignities in the first temple, as written in the book of the *Sanhedrin* <note>a tractate of the Talmud concerning law and courts</note> chapter *Ellu en Haggolin* under the assertion of Rabbi Samuel, and others mentioned in the Hebrew book <term>Pirke Avot</term> <note>original: "Pirke Abath"; Ethics of the Fathers</note> cited above. These are as follows:

1. Never did a woman miscarry because of the smell of the meat being sacrificed in the sanctuary.
2. This meat never smelled foul, being sanctified.
3. No fly was ever seen in the house of slaughtering.
4. No nocturnal accident of evil illusion <note>referring to ritual impurity</note> ever befell the High Priest on the Day of Atonement <note>Yom Kippur</note>.
5. The rains never extinguished the fire burning the burnt offerings.
6. The wind never scattered the pillar of smoke mentioned in Exodus chapters 13 and 33.
7. No defect was ever found in the <term>Omer</term> <note>a unit of dry measure</note> of Manna mentioned in Exodus chapter 16, nor in the two loaves, nor in the showbread.
8. Though the people were crowded while standing, they had ample space when kneeling to worship.
9. No snake or scorpion ever did harm in Jerusalem.
10. No one ever said to his companion, "the place is too narrow for me to stay here in Jerusalem."

This is confirmed by Porchetus <note>Salvagus Porchetus, author of *Victoria adversus impios Hebraeos*</note> in part 1, chapter 2 of his *Victory Against the Jews*, and in the subsequent chapter 7. Sebastian Münster <note>a German cartographer and Hebrew scholar</note> also discusses it in his dispute on the Messiah, following the <term>Gloss</term> <note>commentary</note> of Rabbi Solomon <note>Rashi</note> on the word *Veccaba*, based on the deficiency of the letter <term>He</term> <note>ה; the fifth letter of the Hebrew alphabet</note>, and Pierre Costau in his *Type of the Messiah*. Previously, Samuel of Morocco, a Jew by birth, had treated these things in his book on the coming of the Messiah, having drawn them from the Babylonian Talmud in the *Shevu'ot* <note>original: "Scebagnat Tomin"</note>, meaning "seven days," and from the book *Yoma* (or "of the days") in the chapter *Tereph Vekalpi*, and from the Hebrew book titled *Mishnayot* in the treatise on measurements. Whoever wishes to see more on this may read the Talmud in the treatise *Yoma* chapter 6; the *Midrash* on the Song of Songs chapter 8; Nahmanides <note>original: "R. Gerūdense"</note> in his commentaries on Exodus 25 and 28; Porchetus part 1, chapters 2 and 7; Philo in book 3 of the *Life of Moses* and his book on *Monarchy*; Pietro Galatino in book 4, chapters 5, 9, and 17 of his *Secrets of the Catholic Faith*; Sebastian Münster in his commentaries on the Hebrew Bible, Exodus chapter 28; Jean Cheradame in his *Alphabet of the Holy Language*; Sixtus of Siena in book 2 of his *Holy Library*; and Benito Arias Montano in his *Noah*, or the *Fabric of the Temple*, citing David Kimhi <note>original: "Camhius"</note> and Josephus, and in his *Aaron*, or description of the sacred vestments.

For the "Spirit of the Great Synagogue," as the Hebrews say, which somewhat supplied the lack of Prophecy, failed with Simeon surnamed "the Just" <note>This refers to the righteous man who met the infant Jesus in the Temple; while the text cites Luke chapter 1, the account is found in Luke 2:25.</note>. A certain modern personage, mentioning these **Urim**, **Thummim**, and **Ephod**, has said the following:
> "Just as God was bringing forth the Church in the family of Abraham during this time, so Satan was bringing forth his own synagogue among the Gentiles. For around these days, two oracles seem to have been revealed by two doves flying from Egypt: that of Ammon in Libya, and that of Dodona in Greece. Herodotus writes in his second book that these are therefore the oldest of all. From this, the name 'Ammon' seems derived from Ham (or Cham), the son of Noah, and the name 'Dodanim' is found in Genesis 10. This was done so they might correspond to the two types of Hebrew oracles: one, the **Urim** and **Thummim** in the **Ephod**, which was mute <note>meaning it communicated through light or stones rather than speech</note>, just like the oracle of Ammon; the other, vocal like that of Dodona, coming from the living voice of either God or a prophet." <note>original Latin: "Vti Deus parturiebat hac tempestate Ecclesiam... è viua vel Dei vel Vatis voce."</note>

...in many ways it <note>The Second Temple</note> was inferior. For it lacked five things which previously provided a marvelous sense of majesty and holiness, as noted in the treatise *Yoma* <note>original: *Ioma*</note> chapter 1, and by *Kimhi* <note>David Kimhi, a medieval biblical commentator</note> on *Psalm 84* and *Haggai*. 

First, the divine presence <note>The Shekhinah</note>, which gave responses and oracles from the mercy seat <note>The golden lid of the Ark of the Covenant</note>. Second, the Spirit, or holy inspiration, which once seized the Prophets; for from Malachi until John the Baptist, no Prophets appeared. Third, the sacred fire, whose keeping Moses so anxiously commanded in *Leviticus 6*; it never appeared after it was submerged in a pit by the priests so that it would not fall into the hands of the ungodly, as told in *2 Maccabees 1*. Fourth, the <term>Urim and Thummim<gloss>Sacred stones used by the High Priest for divination and discerning the will of God.</gloss></term>, which were stones in the High Priest’s breastplate. By looking at them, the priests understood hidden things and announced them to the people whenever the stones glowed more than usual. For if they kept their natural appearance and color, it was understood that nothing should be changed. Thus, the former oracle <note>the First Temple</note> was vocal, while this one <note>the Second Temple</note> was silent, as it consisted of movement and signs. Fifth, the Ark and its cover, the mercy seat, and the two Cherubim attached to the Ark, where God was said to dwell because of the abundance of His presence which He granted there to the High Priests. By the name "Ark," I mean both: the one built by Moses to hold the sacred monuments and relics, and the one built by Solomon. In its place <note>in the Second Temple</note>, they then set a stone protruding three fingers from the ground, which held the censer, according to *Rabbi Jacob* in the *Talmud*, part 1, page 106. 

Yet God had not abandoned His people for all that; for to lead them to Christ, oracles were often given through the <term>Bat Kol<gloss>literally "daughter of a voice"; a heavenly echo or divine voice heard by humans.</gloss></term> <note>original: *Batkol*</note>—that is, a thin voice sent from heaven into the ears of the gathered multitude—and other signs continued among the people, which are recounted by the Talmudists in the treatise *Avot* <note>original: *Auoth*</note>. Such was the voice in the Gospel which descended from the Father to glorify the Son, as in *2 Peter 1*.

## *Of the gifts of prophecy, visions, and dreams of the Hebrews.*
### CHAPTER 22.

<image-desc>Decorative square woodcut initial 'I' featuring ornate floral scrolls and leaf patterns.</image-desc>In the preceding chapter, we spoke in passing of divine visions and dreams without explaining them in detail, reserving a fuller treatment for this chapter. To enter into the matter, we shall say that we must turn to the Hebrew prophets to find the true sources of all philosophy and occult sciences. This is because they read (according to Saint Augustine in the first book of *On Free Choice of the Will*) in the "book of life." By this means, Eusebius, in his *Preparation for the Gospel*, not only prefers them to the Greek philosophers, but even prefers the simple Hebrew theologians. In comparison to the Hebrews, he says, the others—though there are some truly excellent and even admirable ones among them for their superficial subtlety of understanding—nevertheless appear to have very little solid foundation. 

The visions of the Hebrew prophets, however, were placed and established upon such a foundation, looking without any obstacle or hindrance, as in a very certain mirror, at the first exemplar and original of all created things in their real and true existence. In contrast, the reasonings of the naturalists <note>Historical term for those who study the physical world or nature</note> depend on the bodily senses, which are for the most part uncertain and deceptive. This is what moved Democritus <note>An ancient Greek philosopher</note> to bring into play a certain deep well, where he said truth was hidden...

For just as the land of the living is in the intelligible world <note>The "intelligible world" refers to the spiritual realm of pure thought and divine forms, as opposed to the physical "sensible world."</note>, likewise there are the living waters which should be understood from these two passages of Leviticus 14 and 15: *In living waters* <note>original: "In aquis viventibus"</note>; as the Savior demonstrates well enough throughout the 4th chapter of Saint John. For this reason it is said in Isaiah 49, as one of the blessings of the people of God, *he shall lead them to the fountains of waters* <note>original: "ad fontes aquarum potabit eos"</note>. The Prophets, therefore, are the true source from which one must draw all that can be known and understood, not only for the simple salvation of our souls within the intelligible world, where the seat of divinity is established, but also regarding the sensible world, concerning the secrets of nature both in heaven and in the four elements. 

For the spirit of the Prophets, being Ravished <note>Caught up in a state of divine ecstasy.</note> and transported out of their bodies even before the throne of God—which the Apostle <note>Saint Paul</note> calls the third heaven, otherwise the third world, or the intelligible realm—they see there quite openly and without any veil the Ideas and first examples <note>The "exemplars" or original blueprints of creation.</note> of all things. These are more perfect in God, from whom they proceed, than they are in themselves, upon which they have been as if stamped or imprinted; and therefore their report of them is more certain than our conjectures made through the natural discourse of reason. Reason often errs because it depends on the animal sense <note>The basic physical senses shared with animals.</note>, with which the Apostle agrees in 1 Corinthians 2: *the spiritual man judges all things* <note>original: "spiritualis homo omnia iudicat"</note>, and not the corporeal man. 

And this is done either by a vision while awake—truly apparent and a familiar conversation face to face, such as that of Moses with God—or while totally asleep and in a dream. Orpheus, in his hymn, says this is what discovers the projects of the blessed Gods to humans during sleep, and without speaking, tacitly announces future things to them. Homer calls it the Angel or messenger of the great God Jupiter. With this agrees what is written in the Zohar: that to wicked souls during the sleep of the body, many visions of evil and hideous figures present themselves; but to those well-disposed, God even speaks sometimes, as in Numbers 12: *I will appear to him in a vision, or I will speak to him through a dream* <note>original: "In visione apparebo ei, vel per somnium loquar ad illum"</note>.

And also while slumbering, which is a middle state between sleeping and waking, which the Hebrews call <term>תדרמה<gloss>Tardemah: A deep sleep or supernatural trance.</gloss></term>, and the Greeks <term>ὄναρ<gloss>Onar: A dream seen in the state of light sleep or a vision.</gloss></term>; for that which appears while sleeping they name <term>ἐνύπνιον<gloss>Enypnion: A standard dream occurring during deep sleep.</gloss></term>. Saint Jerome often translated this as *slumber* <note>original: "Sopor"</note>, as in Genesis 15: *a deep sleep fell upon Abraham* <note>original: "Sopor irruit super Abraham"</note>, and in chapters 4 and 33 of Job: *in the horror of a night vision, when deep sleep usually seizes men, fear took hold of me* <note>original: "in horrore visionis nocturnæ quando sopor solet occupare homines, pauor tenuit me"</note>. 

But there is another kind of these ecstasies and raptures which lies in a vision in the spirit, when the external bodily senses are so numbed in a man that he no longer attends to anything but God alone, so that even if one did him many injuries to his body, he would hardly feel it. *I was in the spirit on the Lord's day* <note>original: "fui in spiritu in dominica die"</note>, in Apocalypse 1 <note>The Book of Revelation</note>.
