# History of the Origin of the [Languages] <note>The header is incomplete in the original; it likely reads "History of the Origin of the Languages of the World."</note>

The ancient Egyptians did not use distinct letters and writing in the same way we do, but rather only certain signs that represented an entire concept. This is shown in two examples: the **Vulture**, which signified nature—since it was believed that among these birds no males are found, but only females, who at a certain season of the year are impregnated by the Wind—and the **Honeybee**, which denoted the King. This represented the two qualities a King should possess: one of kindness and sweetness, represented by the honey, and the other of severity and vigor, represented by the sting.

Theodor Bibliander <note>A 16th-century Swiss scholar and linguist.</note>, in his commentary on the common logic of all languages and letters, writes:
<note>original: "Porrò quod Volaterranus negat Hieroglyphica nulli adhuc comperta..."</note>
"Furthermore, as for Volaterranus’s <note>Raffaello Maffei (1451–1522), a humanist scholar.</note> denial that Hieroglyphs have been understood by anyone yet, it conflicts, in my judgment, with published books in which reputable authors record what the sacred letters of the Egyptians were, and what their use was. Moreover, Diodorus in Book 4 of his *Historical Library* <note>original: "de fabulosis gestis"</note> testifies that the Egyptians received their letter forms from the Ethiopians—specifically those used by the common people. Since that language was completely destroyed in Egypt, first by the Greeks, then by the Romans, and later by the Saracens and Arabs, and since few words survive in literary monuments, it is not easy to judge or pronounce anything for certain regarding the language of the Egyptians. However, from what has come to our knowledge—based on the origin of the People of <term>Mizraim</term> <note>The Hebrew name for Egypt and its biblical progenitor.</note>, which was shared with the Ethiopians and the followers of Nimrod in Babylon, and based on their proximity to the Idumeans and Israelites and the commerce between these peoples—it can be gathered that it was no less related to the Hebrew dialect than the Ethiopic, Chaldean, or Phoenician languages. Even if it were as remote as Latin or Scythian, it could still be compared in its individual parts with Hebrew, and therefore fit into the same standard of art and science."

Of these Hieroglyphs, plenty of remains can still be seen on large and small obelisks, bases, sphinxes, and other marbles brought from Egypt to Rome, of which Pliny makes ample mention in the 36th book, chapter 9, of his *Natural History*. Ammianus Marcellinus, in the place cited previously, provides an explanation in the Greek language and letters of the largest obelisk, under the name of the aforementioned <term>Rameses</term>.

Regarding the common speech or language, and the writing, we have nothing certain. Because of this, these two Alphabets attributed to the Egyptians have made the most curious scholars of antiquity feel uncertain and suspicious. Additionally, the first seems to hold something of that "Leaping Latin" <note>original: "Capreolatin d'Apulee." This refers to a flourishing, ornate script style associated with the writer Apuleius.</note> of Apuleius, and the names of the letters conform to it, as you see following. They are twenty-four in number, just as there are in the Greek alphabet; nevertheless, Plutarch, in his treatise on *Isis and Osiris*, lists twenty-five, according to the square of five, which was the number of years a certain sacred animal lived. Here are the two Egyptian Alphabets represented in figures by Theseus Ambrosius <note>An Italian humanist known for his work on Oriental languages.</note> in his appendix on the Chaldean, Syriac, and Armenian languages.

# History of the Origin of...

...leaving each to abound in his own sense, possessed by a vain and light inconstancy. But these people agree unanimously among themselves regarding the eternity of the world and the perishing of the soul along with the body, persuading themselves that what came from nothing must also return to nothing. Whereupon one among them, thinking by this to express what he might have been before his procreation and birth, what he was during his life, and what he would become after his death, had a dry tree depicted in the middle of a meadow; at the roots of which, on one side, he placed these two verses, which signify these **Latin** words translated from the **Japanese** <note>original: "Giapanois"</note> words:

> "Tell me, who made you, withered tree?"
> "I, whose beginning is nothing, and end is nothing."
> <note>original Latin: "Cedo, quis nam te fecit arbor arida? / Ego, cuius principium nihil est, & finis nihil."</note>

And on the other side, these other two:

> "My heart, which has neither being nor non-being,"
> "Neither goes, nor returns, nor is held anywhere."
> <note>original Latin: "Meum cor, quod neque esse, neque non esse habet / Neque it, neque redit, nec retinetur uspiam."</note>

So it is that their entire belief agrees on this: that the being of all creatures—whether animals, both rational and irrational, or plants and minerals—depends on a **Nothing**. Furthermore, they establish three souls in man, which are introduced into the body and leave it one after another in order. And although they propose many deities to the people to be adored under various names, they admit nothing in their secret teachings except what is perceptible to the senses: namely the spacious and vast **Universe**, where everything is comprised and enclosed, even time, with its course, sequence, and duration, to which they limit no boundary, neither of the "before" nor the "after," the past nor the future. **Orpheus** calls it **Jupiter** in his hymns, saying:

> "Jupiter is what you see,"
> "Everything you perceive moving"
> "In the heaven, on the earth, and in the wave,"
> "And in short, this round machine."
> <note>original French: "Iuppiter est ce que tu vois / Tout ce que mouuoir apperçois / Au ciel, en la terre & en l'onde, / Et brief ceste machine ronde." This reflects the Pantheistic idea that God and the physical universe are one.</note>

And for the rest, just as the earth, which is but an indivisible point in regard to the "prime mover," remains suspended in the middle of the said **Universe**, the universe itself—however immense it may be, even taking it from the convexity of the empyrean sky—remains equally enveloped on all sides, like a little ball, in that void or nothingness which the **Stoics** call the **Infinite**; the **Cabalists** call **En Soph** <note>original: "En Soph" — the Hebrew term *Ein Sof*, referring to God as the Infinite prior to self-manifestation.</note>; the **Prophets** in many places call "the darkness"; and **Orpheus** and **Hesiod** call "the night." In this regard, I remember having once read a passage in **Rabbi Moses the Egyptian** <note>The scholar Maimonides (1138–1204), author of "The Guide for the Perplexed."</note> book 3, chapter 46 of his *Guide*, stating that the nation of the **Zabians** <note>The Sabians, an ancient community often discussed in Islamic and Jewish scholarship as star-worshippers.</note>—a word quite similar and conforming to that of the **Japanese** <note>original: "Zaponiens"</note>—not knowing that there was a creator, estimated that the **Eternal Being** <note>original Latin: "Ens eternel"</note>, to whom privation never applies, was this sky with its stars. And because certain powers and virtues are derived from there onto images and certain trees, they conceived an opinion that these trees and images announced future things, both useful and harmful. These hieroglyphic letters of **China** and **Cathay**, then, are very difficult to learn to read and to form, because they consist of various figures of beasts, birds, trees, herbs; and in short...

# Languages of this Universe

...the sum of everything that nature produces, which serves them as notes—some standing alone and by themselves, others joined and coupled together in groups to form a character. These represent more than one word, much like how **Centaures**, **Chimeras**, **Sphinxes**, and similar monstrosities are composed of diverse natures. Thus, these <term>Bonzes</term> <note>A term used by early European travelers to refer to Buddhist monks in East Asia.</note>, however bright their minds may be, consume the better part of their lives before they can become masters of them. This is according to the account of the Jesuit **Luis Frois**, written from **Bungo** (one of the kingdoms of **Japan**) <note>original: "Gyapan"</note> in the month of June in the year 1577, in these exact words:

"Cicatora, in his great youth, is endowed with such a vivacity of spirit that in these letters of **China**—which are certain characters that the Bonzes spend their entire lives learning—there is no man in all these kingdoms, however expert and well-versed he may be, who knows how to form those characters better than he, nor how to create more varieties of them."

This shows us that based on the general notes of this hieroglyphic writing, by disguising and coupling them in various ways, entirely new composite characters can be formed—just as in the <term>Ciceronian notes</term> <note>Refers to Tironian notes, a system of shorthand credited to Cicero's scribe, Tiro.</note>, and in our mottoes and name-ciphers. This is evidenced by what follows a little further on in the same letter:

"Cicatora changed his name to that of **Simon**, which, written in Chinese characters, signifies and represents: *one who is taught by the master.* By this, we are certain that this writing works like a cipher with multiple meanings."

Today, some marks or relics of these hieroglyphs still remain among us French in those **Rebus** called "of Picardy" <note>A type of heraldic or visual pun popular in Northern France.</note>. **Blaise de Vigenère**, in his treatise on ciphers, writes that there are ciphers of certain languages forged for pleasure, as well as of writing—such as the jargon of beggars <note>original: "Gueux"</note> and **Bohemians** <note>A historical term for Romani people.</note>, and other similar ones. This individual asserts having once seen and read a large dictionary of these printed in **Venice**, so ample and complete that there was nothing whatsoever that could not be said or written there far more distinctly than in the **Genevan** language, **Breton**, or **Basque**, or perhaps even in **Scots**. See **Giambattista della Porta**, the Neapolitan, in his volume titled *On Secret Literacy* <note>original Latin: "De furtituis litterarum notis," a foundational work on cryptography published in 1563.</note>.

The aforementioned Lord de Vigenère, in his previously cited treatise on ciphers, held that the use of occult and secret ways of writing—commonly called ciphers—has existed for a very long time, almost alongside writing itself, if not before. It is true that they are not distinct in letters, syllables, and words to specifically compose a clause, but rather certain marks and notes, each containing within itself <unclear>some</unclear> entire meaning. They are very much like our mottoes, which they closely resemble, representing some mystery of divinity or secret of nature. Ludovico Marmolio reports that it is even named "Bersack" today by some Africans. The mountain that was once surrounded by this city, in which the Byrsa citadel stood, is today called *Rocca de Mastinaces* by Christians and *Almenara* by Africans. The author Lampridius states that Emperor Commodus ridiculously named it "Alexandria Commodiana Togata." "For here were her arms, here was her chariot," as the poet says <note>A reference to Virgil’s *Aeneid*, describing the goddess Juno’s devotion to Carthage.</note>. I do not agree with the opinion of Isidore, nor of Servius in his commentary on the 4th book of the *Aeneid*, where he teaches that this city was also once called Tyre; for contrary to Virgil's intent, he makes Carthage and Tyre out to be the same. St. Augustine, in *On the Unity of the Church*, nonetheless thinks that Carthage was designated under the name of Tyre by the prophet Ezekiel. But this is more an improper usage than a proper name. According to Balsamon, it was called Justiniana by the Emperor Justinian because he restored it to the Roman Empire. Hermolaus and others testify, based on Suidas and Eustathius, that it is called Tarshish <note>original: Tharsis</note> in the Holy Bible. Drusius has in his *Sacred Observations*, book 7, chapter 8. New Carthage <note>Modern Cartagena</note> in Tarraconensian Spain is a maritime city of the Contestani; a diligent description of it by Ptolemy and others exists in Polybius, book 10. Authors such as Pliny, Antoninus, and Appian give it the surname Spartaria <note>original: σπαρταρίαν, referring to the esparto grass of the region</note>. The same Appian thinks it was previously called Saguntum, but was later destroyed by Hannibal and made a Carthaginian colony. That it was called Carthage Spartagena, but that this Carthage and Saguntum are two different towns, is **known to the bleary-eyed and the barbers** <note>A Latin idiom (lippis et tonsoribus) meaning "obvious to everyone" or "common street knowledge."</note>, as they say. But this must be forgiven in a Greek man and a foreigner to whom Spain was less known, much like one who writes that the Ebro River <note>original: Iberum fluuium</note> flows into the Northern Ocean, when it actually exits into the Mediterranean. Stephanus writes that this Carthage is also called Caenepolis, like the Libyan one. The same Polybius in book 3, and Polyaenus in book 8 on Scipio, calls it Phoenissa. Today it is named **Cartagena**. "Old Carthage" is a city of the Elarcaones in Tarraconensian Spain according to Ptolemy. Pliny gives it the surname "of the Punic people." Cicero also mentions this in *On the Agrarian Law*. The Bishop of Girona writes that it is today called Villa Franca. Varretus and Bentherus write that it is Cantavilla. A. Augustinus reads it as *Canta veia* in his *Dialogue 8 on Ancient Coins*; so also does Juan Mariana in his *History of Spain*. Stephanus and Plutarch’s *Lucullus* (who says this was the work of Hannibal) also place a Carthage in Armenia; see **Carchedon**.

## Concerning the Punic and Carthaginian Language.

### CHAPTER XLIII.

The most ancient historians assert that some time after the universal flood, the coast of Africa (or Barbary) and Spain was populated by the Phoenicians, whom they say were for a long time the lords and masters of the sea. They state that the republic of Carthage, so renowned and far-reaching, was one of the colonies of Tyre, the capital of Phoenicia and a neighbor to Judea. Tyre sent half of its people there, which is why it was called in the Hebrew language <term>Kartagaa</term> <note>original Hebrew script: בדתאגאא</note>, meaning a superb and magnificent city. Others say "Carthago" comes from the word *Charta*, which in the Syriac language means a "city," and *Go*, meaning "middle," as if one were to say <term>Media urbs</term> <note>Latin: "Middle city"</note>, or half-city. <note>Modern linguists generally agree that Carthage (Qart-ḥadašt) actually means "New City."</note> The first people who settled there entered through that species of isthmus called the Catabathmus <note>Greek: *Katabathmos*, meaning "the descent"</note>, which joins Palestine with Egypt. This could still be seen in the time of the historian Procopius <note>A 6th-century Byzantine scholar</note> by a column in the city of Tangier <note>original: Tingit</note> in Africa, based on the testimony of the inhabitants of Canaan who fled before the face of Joshua. This is confirmed by Suidas, a Greek author, in his explanation of the word <term>Canaan</term> <note>original: χάνααν</note>. For this reason, Saint Augustine held in several of his works that the Punic and Carthaginian language was nothing other than a dialect of the Hebrew or Canaanite language, as Otto Heurnius well noted in his work on the Chaldean language, citing Salvian, Book 7, *On the Judgment and Providence of God*. The words of the aforementioned Procopius in his *History of the Vandals* are as follows:

> All the country from Sidon to Egypt was once called Phoenicia, and those who have written the history of the Phoenicians recount that a single King once ruled there. In those surroundings lived the Girgashites, Jebusites, and others, who, when they saw this great army of Joshua coming toward them, passed into Egypt. But shortly after, as the land could not support them all, they passed into Africa, where they built several cities and populated the land as far as the Pillars of Hercules <note>The Strait of Gibraltar</note>, and their language is half-Phoenician. In Numidia, they also built, among others, the city of Tangier, which is very strongly situated, where two columns of white stone are seen near the great fountain. In the Phoenician language, these words are engraved: *we are those who fled before that great brigand Joshua, son of Nun*. To this purpose, Gilbert Génébrard in Book 1 of his *Chronographia* writes: <note>original: Chananæorum alij migrarunt in Ægyptum, deinde in Africam...</note> Other Canaanites migrated to Egypt, then to Africa, in which they built many cities as far as the Pillars of Hercules, among others Tangier in Numidia, where two columns of white stone were erected with this inscription in Phoenician characters and language: *we are those who fled before the robber Joshua, son of Nun*. See Procopius, Book 2 of the *Vandal War*, and Epiphanius in some places. Because of this affinity, it could happen that the Sidonian Dido migrated with half the city and founded Carthage; for this name is Canaanite or Syriac <note>original: קדתא גו</note> meaning "middle city." Even in the time of Plautus <note>A Roman playwright</note>, the African language was a dialect of Phoenician and Syriac, as is clear from his play, the *Poenulus*.

These aforementioned Phoenicians seem to have asserted in centuries past that they were the first who taught the Africans and the Greeks their letters, which—

### History of the Origin of...

...and communicated it to posterity, this same author in the place cited above has made such a judgment regarding the characters of the letters, and the Punic, Carthaginian, and Arabic languages.

> I suspect it is so clear that the forms of Punic, Carthaginian, or Arabic letters are various and different, that there is no need for proof. Indeed, I have more than thirty chapters of books, both small and large, and two volumes which, when unfolded, extend to nearly five cubits <note>A cubit is an ancient unit of length, roughly 18 to 22 inches; here, it describes scrolls nearly 7.5 to 9 feet long</note> in length. The figures of the letters are so diverse and distinct that there is no small difficulty in reading them. Just as we see even in our own Latin, in which there is sometimes such a difference that one must rely entirely on guesswork to read them. For someone who has been accustomed only to various Italian letter-shapes will not be able to read without difficulty the writing of the Germans, French, or Spaniards, or even the English, or even the characters used by many merchants, although they are all Latin. So it is also in Punic and Arabic: and what we have said about the diversity of letters, the same is easily to be thought regarding grammatical rules. Since the Tartars, or Persians, and Turks teach grammar in one way, and the Punic, Numidian <note>Ancient North Africans</note>, and Baetic <note>People from southern Spain</note> peoples in another. This can be seen by those who read the books of that Monk (who, in the Kingdom of Granada—which was captured by the kings of Spain—immediately wrote Arabic grammatical rules) compared to those which Postellus <note>Guillaume Postel, a 16th-century French linguist and polymath</note> recently published in his introduction, about which we believe we have said something in the previous section on the formation of letters. We know from the words of Priscian <note>A famous Latin grammarian from around 500 AD</note> that they have only two genders, namely masculine and feminine, and are entirely ignorant of the neuter, when he says: *And especially since the language of the Phoenicians <note>original: "Pænorum"</note>, which is similar to Chaldean or Hebrew and Syrian, does not have a neuter gender.* That same Spanish monk later affirmed this in his introduction to Arabic reading. They have three numbers in declining nouns: singular, dual, and plural. And their masculine nouns end in l, or in v, and in all consonants, but not in the five vowels; feminine nouns are those that do not end as stated above. They have masculine nouns in the manner of the Chaldeans, Hebrews, Syrians, and Indians, with only one ending in the singular and one in the plural. In the dual, however, they retain a peculiar ending, as can be seen in this example for the reader: *Raiul* <note>original: "Raiul" - likely the Arabic "Rajul"</note>, that is, man in the nominative singular; in the dual *Raiulai*, two men, and this kind of addition is general in all duals. Sometimes, however, the syllable *en* is added, and we say *Raiulen*, two men, which is common to both feminine and masculine nouns. In feminine nouns, before *Ay* or *En*, the letter *t* is inserted, which is specific and (so to speak) formative of feminine nouns in the dual and plural. For example: *Duffæ*, that is, Door; *Dufferay*, two doors; *Xamaa* <note>likely Arabic "Jamal"</note>, Camel; *Xamaatai*, two camels; *Mara* <note>Arabic "Imra’a"</note>, wife or woman; *Maraten* or *Maratay*, two wives or women. In the plural, feminine nouns for birds, herbs, fruits, animals, and other seeds, as well as materials and metals, are inflected by shortening <term>apheresis|The removal of a letter or syllable from the beginning of a word, though here used more broadly for stem changes</term> from the nominative singular, by adding the last letter, as *Dabora*, *Dabar*; *Diziła*, Hen; *Dizij*, Hens. And just as these are declined by shortening the word, so verbals and participles are inflected with the addition of *in*, as *Hhabiz*, Baker <note>likely related to "Khubz" or bread</note>; *Hhabizin*, Bakers; *Raiul*, Man, then by shortening,

<margin>cc</margin>likewise, and by a transposition of letters <note>original: "metathesim"</note>, in the plural it becomes *Rigil*, or even *Regil*, meaning "many 
<margin>cc</margin>men." Since among the Arabs, just as among other various languages, 
<margin>cc</margin>there are two types of nouns, namely primitive <note>root words</note> and derivative. It should be 
<margin>cc</margin>known that if a primitive noun ends in a single sound, that sound in the 
<margin>cc</margin>derivative noun is changed into an "I." For instead of *Baza* or *Bazta*, we say *Bazti*, 
<margin>cc</margin>meaning "a thing of Baza." *Roda* becomes *Rodi*; *Gebel* <note>Arabic 'jabal', meaning mountain</note> becomes *Gebeli*. An exception 
<margin>cc</margin>is *Garnata* <note>Granada</note>, used as the name of the City, because we do not say *Garnati*, but *Garnataxi*; 
<margin>cc</margin>and *Alcala* is not *Alcali*, but *Alcalai*. If indeed the primitive noun ends in two vowels, the 
<margin>cc</margin>last one is dropped to form the derivative noun, such as *Valentia* <note>Valencia</note> becoming *Valenti*. 
<margin>cc</margin>If the primitive noun ends in a consonant, then by adding an "I" at the end, the derivative 
<margin>cc</margin>noun is formed, as in *Gebel* becoming *Gebeli*. In this, however, it must be noted that if the 
<margin>cc</margin>primitive noun has the accent on the first syllable, then in the derivative noun the accent 
<margin>cc</margin>is pulled back to the last syllable, as is clear in the stated name. For *Gebel* has a sharp 
<margin>cc</margin>accent <note>acute accent</note> on the first syllable, and *Gebeli* has a heavy accent <note>grave accent</note> on the last. 
<margin>cc</margin>But if the accent of the primitive noun was in the middle of the word, then it is 
<margin>cc</margin>mostly preserved in that same place in the derivative. 
<margin>cc</margin>The cases of nouns among the Punic <note>referring here to North Africans or Moors</note> and Arabs are six, no differently than 
<margin>cc</margin>among the Latins: namely the Nominative, Genitive, Dative, Accusative, Vocative, and Ablative. 
<margin>cc</margin>Among them, the Nominative is called *Mubtade* <note>the subject</note>; the Genitive, *Mudaph* <note>the possessive</note>; 
<margin>cc</margin>the Dative, *Maxror* <note>the indirect object/prepositional</note>; the Accusative, *Maphuul* <note>the direct object</note>; the Vocative, *Munede* <note>the called</note>; and the Ablative, *Darph* <note>the adverbial/circumstantial</note>. 
<margin>cc</margin>It should also be known, as we believe we have already said above, that the Arabs 
<margin>cc</margin>have only one ending for nouns in the singular, and another in the plural. 
<margin>cc</margin>Therefore, we can only distinguish the cases of nouns either from the 
<margin>cc</margin>power of the phrasing <note>context</note> or by the addition of articles. This is also common 
<margin>cc</margin>to the Chaldeans, Hebrews, Syrians, and Indians, and to almost all who 
<margin>cc</margin>decline their native nouns in their own language, about which George 
<margin>cc</margin>Reisch <note>a 15th-century Carthusian monk</note> wrote extensively in his *Philosophical Pearl* <note>original: "Margarita Philosophica," a famous early encyclopedia</note>. 
<margin>cc</margin>The articles of the Punic language are: for the Nominative case, *A*, *Al*; for the Genitive, 
<margin>cc</margin>*A*, *Al*, *Mi*, *a*, *Mital*; for the Dative, *La*, *Lal*, *Li*, *Lil*; for the Accusative, *A*, *Al*, as in 
<margin>cc</margin>the direct case; for the Vocative, *A*, *Ya*; for the Ablative, *Ba*, *Bal*, *Fa*, *Fal*, *Fi*, *Fil*, *Maa*, *Maal*, *Min*, *Minal*.

Epiphanius says: <term>Saracens, who are also Ishmaelites, practice circumcision</term> <note>original: "Σαρακηνοὶ, οἱ καὶ Ισμαηλῖται, περιτομὴν ἔχουσι"</note>. Their dwelling and residence was anciently in Arabia Petraea <note>Stony Arabia</note> where Mount Sinai is, upon which the law was given by God to Moses, who, with the children of Israel upon leaving Egypt, remained there for 38 years, roaming side to side in the surroundings without advancing more than a day's journey, as remarked by Rabbi Rambam <note>Maimonides, the famous medieval Jewish philosopher</note>, son of Maimon, in Book 3, Chapter 51 of his *Moreh Nevukhim* <note>The Guide for the Perplexed</note>. This country took its name from its capital city, Petra, situated on the torrent of Arnon, where King Aretas formerly established his rule some 1600 years ago; the other kings, his successors, were later called by his name, just as those of Egypt were called after the first Ptolemy, son of Lagus.

This being presupposed, we shall learn that after the prophet Muhammad—who held dominion in this place—had died, the pontiffs <note>The author uses "pontiffs" to refer to the Caliphs</note> who succeeded him, departing from there, made great incursions and conquests. It is said that under these Pontiffs there were also as many brave warriors and men of letters and understanding as could ever be found in all the rest of the other nations. But the Saracens, whom people commonly take for Muhammadans, have always been the most notorious bandits <note>original: "bandouilliers"</note> and thieves of all others, without having any firm or settled dwelling, thus flitting incessantly across the straits and deserts of the mountains of Assyria, Mesopotamia, Syria, and Egypt, to rob all sorts of people coming and going. Formerly, this people devoted themselves to agriculture and tillage, as well as the tending of livestock, but the majority cared for nothing but arms; this was why the *Greek* Emperors called them into their service, and why *Heraclius* <note>Byzantine Emperor, r. 610–641 AD</note>, while marching against the *Persians*, hired them. But seeing themselves despised after the victory was won and gained, and finding that they were defrauded of the promise made to them, they were inflamed with wrath and fury. From there, in the course of time, under *Ali* <note>original: "Hali"; the cousin and son-in-law of the Prophet Muhammad</note>, one of the disciples of *Muhammad* <note>original: "Mahomet"</note> the Prophet, they became lords of *Antioch* and then of *Jerusalem*. Thus grew the greatness, power, and renown of these barbarians, and so terrifying was their effort that there was no longer any people or nation to offer them resistance. 

But behold, as these *Arab Saracens* were at the height of their glory and everything trembled before them, the *Turks*—a nation descended from the *Scythians* <note>A group of ancient nomadic warriors from Central Eurasia</note>, a barbarian and cruel people—were driven from their lands by their neighbors. Passing through the *Caspian Gates* once established by *Alexander* <note>Alexander the Great</note>, they rushed into *Asia Minor* through the *Colchian* country. Then, leaving that route, they overran *Armenia*, the *Persians*, and the *Medes*, putting everything under their power. These *Arab Saracens*, who would have been greatly distressed to be suddenly deprived of their conquests, went against these *Turks*; but seeing themselves unequal in strength, and the enemy being more vigorous, they came to an agreement: the *Turks* would be admitted into the government with them, provided they received the faith of *Muhammadanism* <note>Islam</note>, which was granted. And so this bond of a single opinion or religion, which joined these two great and powerful nations together, was the reason why for a long time among the less learned, the *Turks* were taken for *Saracens* and *Arabs*, and the latter for the former, without any distinction between such different things. Whereas today, the name of *Turk* alone being in force, there is no longer any memory of the name *Saracen*, and even less of their power, as is confirmed by *Sabellicus*, *Enneades* 8 <note>Marcantonio Sabellico, a Venetian historian</note>; *Biondo*, *Decades* 1, Book 9 and *Decades* 2, Book 1 <note>Flavio Biondo, a Renaissance humanist historian</note>; and by *Hayton the Armenian*, Chapter 15 of his histories <note>A 13th-century historian of the Mongol Empire and the Near East</note>; with whom one should also see *André Thevet*, Book 6, Chapters 1 and 2 of his *Cosmography*. 

It would be far too long and tedious a task to traverse all the affairs and conquests of these *Saracens* and *Arabs*, who for five or six hundred years ruled the greater part of *Asia* and *Africa*, and even a large portion of *Europe*—at the very least all the *Spains* <note>original: "les Heſpagnes"; referring to the various kingdoms of the Iberian Peninsula</note>, from which the Kings of *France* have driven them on several occasions—holding occupied, not even a hundred years ago, still the kingdom of *Granada* and *Andalusia*. Thus it is a most certain and assured thing that at present this language has great currency and popularity throughout this universe, occupying entirely two parts of it, it being divided into three parts; namely, throughout the Levant and the South, even to the Molucca Islands, and as far as Nubia and Ethiopia commanded by the *Padishah* of Prester John <note>original: "Padeſcha Preſtegiani"; "Padishah" is a royal title, here applied to the mythical Christian monarch of the East</note>, in short, in all of Asia except among the Indians and those of Narsinga <note>The Vijayanagara Empire in Southern India</note>, and through a third of our Europe because of the religion and the disciplines, according to G. # History of the Origin of

four points in the shape of a diamond or a cross; and this language is so similar to the Hebrew and Chaldean <note>Chaldean usually refers to Aramaic in this period</note> languages, that if someone moderately versed in the knowledge of these Hebrew and Chaldean languages wished to employ themselves for two years in understanding this said Arabic <note>original: "Arabesque"</note> language—though it is very difficult to learn for those ignorant of Hebrew and Chaldean—they would perfectly learn the greater and more substantial part of it. In fact, the late G. Postel <note>Guillaume Postel (1510–1581), mentioned on the previous page</note>, who was highly learned in the Hebrew language, wrote in his *Alphabet of Twelve Different Languages* that while he was in Constantinople, the Turks who taught him this Arabic language called him a "Demon," because he understood it as soon as it was shown and taught to him—unlike others who ordinarily spend five or six years before perfectly knowing the grammar. This is confirmed by Theodore Bibliander <note>Theodor Bibliander (1506–1564), a Swiss linguist and reformer who published the first printed Latin translation of the Quran</note> in his commentary on the common reasoning of all languages and letters.

The Arabs, Turks, and Persians do not permit any man of their Law to handle the books of their religion, named in the Arabic language *Almashaf* <note>The Mushaf, a physical copy of the Quran</note>, and in Persian *Lereteb*, except for the principal priests, or their deputies whom they call *Elcadię* <note>Qadis, or judges</note>, *alakeith* <note>likely al-Khatib, a preacher</note>, or indeed the great Sultan who is their sovereign King. Thus, whatever book it may be, it is not placed in the hands of the common people, both because it is a rare thing—printing being unknown in those parts—and because they feel a great moral scruple and conscience, as if such books would be profaned and exposed to the sight of everyone. They would think they had fallen into the indignation of God and the disfavor of Muhammad, Ali <note>The cousin and son-in-law of Muhammad, central to Shia Islam</note>, and their other Prophets, if such a fault had happened to them; and they would believe that all was lost if any cooks, masons, or servants took the boldness to handle the sacred books which the great God gave to his holy Prophets and revealed to their ancient fathers.

A certain modern author in his commentaries on the Quran <note>original: "Alcoran"</note> has written the following words regarding the Arabic language:

> „ [Arabic] has the greatest kinship to Hebrew. Whence these Arabs, who 
> „ are here called Ishmaelites or Saracens, just like the Jews, draw their 
> „ letters in writing from the right to the left, and not from the 
> „ left to the right as we do. Alif, Lam, Mim <note>original Latin: "Eliph, Lem, Mim"</note>—A, 
> „ L, M—they place these Arabic letters at the beginning of the book, which they 
> „ call the seal of the book. The reason is, they say, that from this kind of character, since 
> „ Alif <note>original: "Eliph"</note> is first both in the order of letters and in the name of God among them. Through Lam 
> „ indeed, the Majesty of God is designated, and through Mim, his Empire, to intimate that God 
> „ is almighty, whose messenger this is, as well as his precepts. <note>This refers to the *Muqattaʿat*, or mysterious disconnected letters found at the start of certain chapters in the Quran</note>

And to be brief, the Arabic language in which the Quran of the Muhammadans is composed is so highly prized and esteemed by the aforementioned people that they have not wished to permit any version of it to be made in another language. Resembling Hebrew, Chaldean, and Syriac, it has today a very wide extent and popularity among many peoples of this Universe; for although the Tatars, Khwarazmians <note>original: "Corasiniens"</note>, Persians, and Turks have languages different from Arabic, and the Syrians, Arabs, Moors, and Africans have something similar, it remains that grammatical Arabic is common in religion and in the disciplines among the learned Priests and Judges, for almost all the inhabitants of Asia, Africa, and a third part of Europe. See A. Thevet <note>André Thevet (1516–1590), a French Franciscan priest, explorer, and cosmographer</note>, book 6, chapter 2 of his *Universal Cosmography*.

The entire system of letters and the art of grammar is essentially as we have set forth in the previous table and in the treatment of the Phoenician characters. Indeed, the art of all the languages of the East depends upon this one. For in both—namely, Chaldean <note>Aramaic</note>, which is used by the Jews in the Talmud, the Targums, and the Mishnah, and among Christians in the sacred books and rites, as well as the Syriac language used by Christ and recorded by various interpreters—and also in Arabic and Ethiopic, the same system of suffixes and "servile" letters <note>Letters used for grammatical functions rather than roots.</note> is preserved. This is true except that for the Ethiopians, *Za* is used for *Daleth*, and in Chaldean *Daleth* is used in place of the article *He* or as a relative pronoun. Furthermore, in Chaldean and Arabic, *He* stands at the end in place of the masculine relative *Vav*. All languages, when they fall away from formal art, return to the nature of Hebrew, led by Nature as if to a mother and a primary source.

These characters have always remained among the inhabitants of Syria who converted from circumcision to Christianity. They are found in the sacred writings of the New Testament—either written originally in this tongue or translated from Greek—and in the Old Testament translated from Hebrew into this common language. These people have labored under a great hatred for the Jews. Consequently, even though their script was derived from Hebrew, they strove to distinguish themselves from the Jews. Today, if someone well-versed in the Latin language wished to read the cursive script of the Spanish, French, or Italian merchants, they would be quite unable to do so using the standards of ancient Latin script; they might not even believe it was once Latin. So it happened with the Syrians, who swore allegiance partly to the Greek Patriarch and partly to the Roman Supreme Pontiff—such as the Maronites <note>A Catholic Eastern Rite church in Lebanon.</note> who live on Mount Lebanon, who perform their sacred rites in this language according to the Roman rite, while others follow the Greek rite.

### THE ALPHABET [ARABIC].

<margin>
This language, as the Arabs hold, was given by Abraham to Ishmael, the father of the Arabs and Ishmaelites. From this it is clear that the script divinely given to Moses was already common to the patriarchs, and was even divinely engraved for Adam. However, it was done in such a way that the true, secret figure was known only to the wise—that is, the Saints—while an adulterated and handwritten version was given to the sons of the handmaid, who, though illegitimate, were the firstborn. Thus it has happened that although nothing is more absurd than the doctrine of the Quran, nothing weaker than the Ishmaelite arms, and nothing more childish than their "wise men," they have nevertheless given their religion and empire, along with their language, over all the peoples and nations of Asia, Africa, and a third part of Europe, even over the most powerful Christians. This includes Caesarian and Tingitan Mauritania <note>Modern Algeria and Morocco</note>, Numidia, Africa proper <note>Tunisia</note>, Cyrenaica, Libya, Ethiopia, Egypt, Arabia the Fertile, the Stony, and the Desert, Syria, Coelesyria, Assyria, Chaldea, Parthia, Media, Persia, Gedrosia, Susiana, Ariana, India (on both sides of the Ganges), even to the new and recently opened world of the Antipodes, in Serica <note>China</note>, Scythia or Tartary, Arachosia, Chorasmia, Hyrcania, Armenia, both Cilicis, Georgia, Paphlagonia, all of Asia to the Massagetae and even to our own sea, in the Peloponnese, Greece, Macedonia, Thrace, among the Triballi, Dacia, Wallachia, the Jazyges, Serbia, Bosnia, Epirus, Slavonia, Illyria, Hungary, even to the borders of the Roman Empire. I have listed these provinces in this table so that the Christian world may see how useful and necessary this language is for traveling the whole world, so that the Decree of Clement regarding teachers <note>Referencing a 1311 church decree to teach oriental languages for missionary purposes.</note> may be fulfilled, whether we deal with them by reason or by arms.

Otherwise, having disturbed the order of the letters so that their Hebrew origin is not recognized, they call them thus: Alif, Be, Te, The, Gim, He, Che, Dal, Thal, Re, Ze, Shin, Sin, Sad, Dad, Ta, Za, Ain, Ghain, Fe, Qaf, Kaf, Lam, Mim, Nun, He, Vau, Lam-Alif, Ye. And so they claim to have twenty-nine letters from twenty-two, because they mark the shapes with dots for varied pronunciation.
</margin>

-> In the name of God, the Compassionate, the Merciful. <note>The "Basmala," the opening phrase of most Quranic chapters.</note> <-

A straight slanted line above letters counts as *a* or *e*; the same below them counts as *i*. A curve above counts as *o*, *u*, or *on*: if it is double above, it counts as *an* or *en*: in a double recurved or mutually inverted form, *un* or *on*. The single one above is called *Fathah*, the single one below is *Kasra*, the recurved one is *Rafa* or *Damma*, the double one above is *Nasb Tanwin*. The double one below is *Jarr Tanwin*: the double recurved one is *Raf Tanwin*. The entire art of Grammar consists of these dots. A "U" is commonly at the end of nouns that are subjects, and without the *al* or *el* article, *Un* comes in its place. *A* or *e* occurs in direct speech; and *an* if the article is missing, with a suffix or possessive attached. And the rest is as I have previously set forth in the Arabic Grammar.

It is true that **André Theuet** <note>A 16th-century French explorer and cosmographer</note> in Book 6, Chapter 3 of his *Universal Cosmography*, writes that some schismatic Germans, taught by a certain Bishop of the Island of Crete named **Spirion**, have maintained that a certain Cardinal named **Nicholas** helped this Muhammad to compose this Alcoran; which has no appearance of truth for the reasons alleged by the aforementioned **Theuet** in chapters 4 and following of his Book 6, cited above.

The first chapter of this Alcoran or Alfurcan was that which Muhammad assures was given to him in the cave by the Angel **Gabriel**, and the last, that of the *Fate* which signifies "of the Conquest" <note>This likely refers to Al-Fatiha (The Opening) or perhaps the surah Al-Fath (The Victory/Conquest)</note>. And it must be understood that this Muhammad never commanded that his Alcoran or Alfurcan be collected or reduced into books, nor into chapters, as it is at present; rather, he kept certain schedules or tablets in an Ark or chest as he wrote and composed them; and several of these schedules or tablets were lost, and were not found after his death. It is credible that if this Muhammad had remained alive for a hundred years, he would have continually increased these schedules and tablets, and he did not arrange this Alcoran or Alfurcan in writing during his life in the style and manner it is in at present. After he was dead, in the time when **Hozmen** [Uthman] his son-in-law was King and *Alcaliphe* <note>Caliph</note>—that is to say, Doctor—who succeeded immediately after his death to the office of King and *Alcaliphe*, **Vbecquar** [Abu Bakr], and after him **Homar** [Umar], this **Hozmen**, son-in-law of this Muhammad...

# History of the Origin of the

...took the notebooks, tablets, or bulletins from the chest of the said **Muhammad**: and began to arrange them in order and title them as Chapters, and made of them four books. In the first book, he put five chapters: the first, the chapter of the **Cow**; the second, the chapter of the **Family of Joachim** <note>original: "Ioachin"; referring to the Surah Al-Imran, as Joachim is traditionally identified in Christian tradition as the father of Mary</note>, father of our Lady; the third, the chapter of **Women**; the fourth, the chapter of the **Table**; the fifth, the chapter of **Beasts**.

In the second book, he put twelve chapters: the first, the chapter of the **Mute** <note>Possibly a reference to Al-A'raf or a corruption of another title</note>; the second, of the **Spoils**; the third, of the **Sword** <note>Usually referring to Surah At-Tawbah</note>; the fourth, of **Jonah** the Prophet; the fifth, of **Hud** the prophet newly introduced by **Muhammad**; the sixth, of **Joseph** son of **Jacob**; the seventh, of the **Thrones**; the eighth, of **Abraham**; the ninth, of the **Migration** <note>original: "l'Alihgere," referring to the Hijra</note> (which means, according to the book of *Azar* or *Azear*, stoning or banishment; it is the night of **Muhammad's** departure from **Mecca** to retreat to **Medina**); the tenth, of the **Flies** <note>likely Surah An-Nahl, the Bees</note>; the eleventh, of the **Death** of the said **Muhammad**; and the twelfth, of the **Cave of the Seven Sleepers**.

In the third book, he put nineteen chapters: the first, of **Mary** our Lady; the second, of **Taha**; the third, of the **Prophets**; the fourth, of the **Earthquake**; the fifth, of the **Believers**; the sixth, of the **Light**; the seventh, of the **Gibbet** <note>original: "gibet," likely referring to Al-Furqan (The Criterion), sometimes misinterpreted in old polemics</note>; the eighth, of the **Executioners**; the ninth, of the **Ants**; the tenth, of the **Stories** <note>original: "cazaz," for Al-Qasas</note>; the eleventh, of the **Spiders**; the twelfth, of **Luqman** <note>original: "Lucumen"</note>, a holy man and friend of **David**; the thirteenth, of **Prostration** <note>original: "l'inclination"</note>; the fourteenth, of the **Romans**; the fifteenth, of the **Creator**; the sixteenth, of the **Sabbath**; the seventeenth, of the **Additions**; the eighteenth, of **Man**; the nineteenth, of the **Angels**. In the fourth book, he put one hundred and seventy-five chapters and titled each by its name, so that the chapters of the **Alcoran** or **Alfurcan** <note>The Quran</note> make 211 in total; and there is as much written in the first as in the second, and as much in the third as in the fourth.

The aforementioned **Uthman** <note>original: "Hozmen," the third Caliph</note>, who collected this **Alcoran** or **Alfurcan**, did not put into these four books and these two hundred and eleven chapters the entire **Alcoran**, which the **Moors** and **Muhammadans** in the time of the said **Muhammad** read in notebooks, tablets, or bulletins written by the hand of his scribes. This is very well proven by the books of *Azar* and *Azzifa* composed in the **Arabic** language, in which it is written that the aforementioned **Uthman** found in the house of **Aisha** <note>original: "Axa"</note>, wife of the said **Muhammad**, behind a chest or crate, several notebooks, tablets, or bulletins of the **Alcoran** gnawed by rats and mice, from which he could recover nothing. This caused **Uthman**, at the time he wished to collect and arrange the said **Alcoran** or **Alfurcan** in order, to go and ask everyone what they knew of the said **Alcoran**, some telling him that they had forgotten much of it, others that on such a wall there were verses written; and in this fashion, this personage withdrew and collected all that he could.

The **Mahometans** now hold this **Alcoran** or **Alfurcan** in such great recommendation and reverence that, taking it in their hands, they kiss it and swear by it, holding it in the place of God, and they call it *Al Kutib, Alhazim* <note>original: "Al Kutib, Alhazim," meaning Al-Kitab al-Azim, or The Mighty Book</note>, the glorious book, otherwise *Alcoran alhadin*, the powerful **Alcoran**. **Friar Riccoldo** <note>original: "F. Ricold ou Richard"</note> of the order of Preaching Friars, alleged above in his *Confutation of the Law Given by Muhammad to the Saracens*, chapter 13, writes of it the following words:

"Since therefore it has been demonstrated that the **Alcoran**, namely the law of the **Saracens**, is not from God, it follows to inquire concerning the disciples of **Muhammad** and the constitution of the aforesaid **Alcoran**. It must therefore be known that it is most firmly [believed]..."

# Languages of this Universe

It is believed by their wise men, and shown by effective reasons, that the first author of the *Quran* was not a man, but the devil; for by his own envy and by divine permission—due to the sins of the people—he prevailed in solemnly and effectively beginning the treachery of the antichrist. You see, therefore, that the devil saw the faith of Christ growing greatly in Eastern parts and idolatry failing, now that *Khosrow* <note>Khosrow II, the last great Sassanid King of Persia</note>, King of the Persians and an idolater of the Medes, had been overcome by the most Christian Emperor *Heraclius*. This emperor destroyed the lofty tower which *Khosrow* himself had built of gold, silver, and precious stones for the sake of idolatry. Because the cross of Christ had already been exalted by *Heraclius* and was to be exalted further, and since the devil could no longer defend a multitude of gods, nor entirely deny the law of Moses and the Gospel of Christ (which had been spread throughout the whole world), he devised a deception for the world through the fiction of a certain law, a middle ground as it were, between the New and Old Testaments. 

And, to bring this to effect, he took up a certain diabolical man named *Muhammad*, an idolater by religion, poor in fortune, proud in mind, and famous for sorceries. Indeed, the devil would have more willingly taken a man of good reputation if it had been permitted to him, just as he would have more willingly tempted man through some other animal in which his malice could be better hidden than through the serpent. But divine wisdom did not permit him to take any but such an animal, or to invade the world through any but such a man, so that the world itself could easily perceive what kind of law it was that was given by such a lawmaker. 

Therefore, after *Khosrow* was defeated by the aforementioned *Heraclius*, and the Holy Cross was translated to Jerusalem in triumph in the six hundred and twentieth year from the incarnation of the Lord (the fifteenth year of the reign of *Heraclius*), there appeared a certain *Muhammad*, an Arab. He first became wealthy through a certain widow whom he took as his wife, and after this, having become a leader of thieves, he broke out into such pride that he wished to become the king of the Arabs. But because they did not accept him, as he was of base lineage and reputation, he feigned that he was a Prophet. 

And when he suffered from the comitial disease <note>original: "comitiali morbo"; an archaic term for epilepsy</note>, so that no one would firmly believe he was gripped by it as he was continually falling, he claimed that an Angel was speaking with him. He would afterwards give certain responses which (as I have said) he heard as if by the sound of a bell ringing around his ears. And because he was uneducated and illiterate, the devil gave him his own companions: certain heretics and *Jews*, and likewise *Christian* heretics. For a certain *Jacobite* <note>A member of the Syrian Orthodox Church</note> named *Bahira* <note>A monk who, in Christian polemics, was said to have taught Muhammad</note> stayed with him and remained with *Muhammad* until death. It is said that *Muhammad* afterwards killed him. But there were also certain *Jews*, namely *Phinees* and *Audia* (named *Salom*, but afterwards called *Abdullah*), and *Sele*, who also became *Saracens*. And certain *Nestorians* <note>Followers of Nestorius, who emphasized the distinction between Christ’s human and divine natures</note>, who mostly agree with the *Saracens* by saying that God was not born of the *Blessed Virgin*, but the man *Jesus Christ*. 

Then *Muhammad* composed certain things in the manner of a law, taking through his companions some things from the Old Testament and some from the New. However, the people did not have the *Quran* at that time. Yet it is said in their histories that *Muhammad* said: "The *Quran* descended to me in seven men, and whatever is enough, suffices." They say, however, that these were *Naple* and *Eon*, *Omar*, *Omra*, *Eleazar*, *Asir* son of *Cethir*, and the son of *Amer*. We said to them, therefore: "Did they read these things in the presence of *Muhammad*?" and they all said no, but in the presence of the elders, and so on down to *Muhammad*. It is certain, however, that these men did not agree with the earlier elders in the text which they now hold. This is proven by the fact that the text of the first part is contrary to the second part. For from the time of *Muhammad*, no one has been truly skilled in the *Quran*...

# History of the Origin of the [Sects]

...unless it was Abdallah son of Masud, and Zayd son of Thabit, and Uthman son of Affan, and the son of Ubayy son of Ka'b <note>original: "Audala filius Mesetud, & Zeith filius Tamphet, & Ocanan filius Ophyon, & filius Oeupe filius Tap." These names refer to historical companions of Muhammad involved in the early collection of the Quran.</note>. Regarding Ali, the son of Abu Talib <note>original: "Alete... Abitalem"</note>, some claim to know his part, while others do not. Each of these individuals composed a version of the Quran, very different from the Qurans of the others. Indeed, they fought among themselves even to the death, refusing to accept what belonged to the others. After Muhammad's death, the people disagreed over the Quran until the time of Marwan son of al-Hakam <note>original: "mermpan filij Elezen." While the text names Marwan, historically the standardization of the Quran is attributed to the Caliph Uthman; Marwan was a later Umayyad Caliph who reportedly destroyed some of the variant manuscripts.</note>, who composed for them this Quran which they now possess. He also burned the other versions of the Quran. At that time, even the governors of the cities disagreed with one another regarding the grammar and their own local dialects. 

We also find in their own histories that the "Chapter of Divorce" <note>Surah At-Talaq</note> once exceeded the "Chapter of the Cow" <note>Surah Al-Baqarah</note>, which originally consisted of two hundred and thirty verses, but is now established entirely in twelve. Others say that the "Chapter of the Cow" at one time contained a thousand verses, yet today it has only eighty-seven <note>These figures reflect medieval Christian polemical claims about "missing" parts of the Quranic text, which often exaggerated or misunderstood the history of Quranic abrogation or variant readings.</note>. They also report concerning a certain powerful man named Al-Hajjaj <note>original: "Elgas," likely referring to Al-Hajjaj ibn Yusuf, a governor famous for his role in standardizing the Quran's diacritics.</note> that he removed eighty-five verses from the Quran and added as many others of a different meaning. How then is it true what they say of the Quran, where God says: "We have sent down the reminder, and we shall preserve it"? 

Certain histories also relate that Muhammad died of poison, and the people did not yet have a single Quran. When Abu Bakr <note>original: "Empeumpecer"</note> took the leadership, he commanded that everyone collect what they could, and from this he composed the Quran that is now at hand, burning the rest. But in the chapter *Al-Imran* <note>original: "Elamram"</note>, it is said of the Quran that none but God knows its interpretation, and those who possess the depth of wisdom say: "We believe in it, for it is all from our God." 

And truly, in this book, many things are so scattered and so disordered—as was shown clearly above—that they express no coherent thought, but rather cover up madness and lies. It came to pass that they agreed this should be the Quran which they now have in their hands, and they claim God revealed it to Muhammad and wrote it from the mouth of God. However, the *Faqihs* <term>Faqihs: Islamic jurists or legal scholars; the text uses "AlphaKi" and "Aelphocaa"</term>, that is, the great teachers and expositors, have never agreed on its interpretation, nor will they ever agree. Thus, not only are those of the East at odds with those of the West, but the Easterners disagree among themselves, as do the Westerners. Even in the same schools there are diverse sects, so different that one condemns the other. For some follow Muhammad—and they are the majority—while others follow Ali; these are fewer and considered "less evil," claiming that Muhammad usurped for himself through tyrannical power what belonged to Ali. 

Moreover, some experts in <term>Philosophy</term> rose up against both groups; beginning to read the books of Aristotle and Plato, they abandoned all the sects of the Saracens <note>A common medieval term for Muslims</note> and the Quran itself. A certain Caliph <note>original: "Calyphas"</note> in Babylon <note>Likely referring to Cairo or Baghdad, centers of Islamic learning</note>, perceiving this, built a school at the Academy and the *Mustansiriya* <note>original: "Stanzeriam"</note> which are very costly. He redirected the curriculum toward the study of the Quran and ordained that whoever comes to Babylon from the provinces to learn the Quran should have housing and necessary expenses provided by the public treasury. He decreed that Saracens who devote themselves to the Quran should in no way labor at philosophy. For this reason, they do not consider those who study philosophy to be "good Saracens," because such people tend to despise the Quran for the reasons stated above in the eighth and ninth chapters.

To make it short, we will say that we have learned by reading the histories of the Arabs, Turks, and Moors, that after the death of Muhammad there were four principal captains of his following named Abu Bakr, Omar, Uthman, and Ali: who, having collected the Quran, made each...

The second interpretation is that of **Umar** <note>original: "Omar," the second Caliph</note>, who was Caliph—meaning a great captain or High Priest of the Muslims <note>original: "Machumetãs." This one is believed, supported, and stubbornly defended by the inhabitants of Syria, by certain Saracen Arabs, by the Turks, and the African Berbers who have their *Cobeilas* <note>tribes or assemblies</note> and families in the **Sahara**.

This one, along with the two preceding it, are inviolably observed by the Turks and the other nations mentioned above. 

As for the interpretation of the fourth doctor named **Ali**, it was called *Iménia* <note>The Imami or Shi'a tradition</note>, which is to say the "Pontifical Law"; it was also named *Hambelia* <note>The Hanbali school</note> after a certain *Hambeli* who glossed it and wrote commentaries and expositions upon it. This law is superstitiously <note>The author uses "superstitiously" in a period-typical sense to mean "strictly" or "devoutly"</note> kept by the Persians and some Arabs, as well as by the Muslims scattered throughout **East India**, the African Gelbins, and others neighboring them. 

And although there are sixty-eight known, notable, and illustrious sects and opinions among the disciples of the **Quran** <note>original: "Alcoran"</note>, these four cited above are the most famous. Two of these have caused as much relief and rest to Christians as they have caused perdition and ruin to the lands and provinces of the Muslims. This is because the Turks, adhering to the observation of the first three interpretations (which were gathered into one volume and reconciled by an Arab named *Leshary* <note>Al-Ash'ari, a major theologian who reconciled traditionalism and rationalism</note>, the leader of the false theologians of Arabia), hate the Persians to death. The Persians defend with great heart and animosity the *Asafie* sect maintained by **Ali**, whom they hold to be the most truthful of all the "liars" <note>The author’s bias labels all Islamic writers as such</note> who have written on the Quran.

### History of the Origin of the [Sophys]

...Muhammad al-Mahdi <note>original: "Moaidin," referring to the Twelfth Imam of Shia Islam, who went into occultation</note> did not pass through the way of mortality to which all men are bound. Rather, they hold this delusion (much like the Jews regarding the Messiah) that he is to come, and that it will be he who converts the rest of the world to the sect of **Ali** <note>The cousin and son-in-law of Muhammad, central to Shia Islam</note>. For this reason, in a certain city named **Kufa**, they celebrate a festival for him every year and carry in procession a richly harnessed horse, offering prayers to their Ali. They keep this horse in their principal Mosque, and direct their prayers so that Ali might soon send them Muhammad al-Mahdi, his nephew <note>The author likely means descendant; the "Twelve Imams" are the central figures of this lineage</note>, for the advancement of their false religion. From this heretical follower of the Quran <note>original: "Alcoraniſte"</note> issued the **Sophys** <note>The Safavid dynasty of Persia</note> of Persia; one should not be surprised if they have always aspired to the greatness of which Ali was deprived by his companions, even though Muhammad wished for and had named him as successor to the lordship he held over the Arabs.

Now it must be noted that just as the children descended from the other daughters of Muhammad <note>original: "Machumet"</note> were called **Xeriphes** <note>Sharifs; the author refers to the Saadi or Sharifian dynasties in North Africa</note> or **Xorphas**, those also who came from Ali and Fatima bore the name of **Sophys**, which signifies wise and learned men, well-instructed in the law, according to **Paolo Giovio** <note>original: "Paüle Ioue," a 16th-century Italian historian</note> in the 13th book of his *Histories*. And thus, to remove the error of those who think that the modern Kings of Persia are all called "Sophys" in the same way the Kings of Egypt were once named "Pharaohs" and "Ptolemies," or the Emperors of Rome were named "Caesars": the word "Sophy" is a name of religion, and not of race or a title used to distinguish families. 

Furthermore, there are those of the opinion that this word "Sophy" is Arabic, descended from *Cof* <note>Suf</note>, which signifies wool, because those who make profession of the sect of Ali—as do the Sophy and his adherents and accomplices—cannot, according to the statutes of their rule, wear any sort of silk upon their heads, nor ornaments of gold or silver; they have instead taken colored wool for their Turbans. **Johannes Leunclavius** <note>A 16th-century German scholar of Ottoman history</note> in his *Turkish Onomasticon* says: <note>original Latin: "Sophy, Arabicè Lanâ ſignificat. Sofilar & Sofiler, religioſi homines qui humilitatis & modeſtiæ cauſa tegumẽto laneo vtũtur, nõ lineo tulipáto ſu-perbè Caput inuoluunt. Etenim conſecuti ſunt hoc nomen ab Arabico Sophy, non à Græco vocabulo σοφὸς..."</note> *Sophy, in Arabic, signifies wool. Sofilar and Sofiler are religious men who, for the sake of humility and modesty, use a woolen covering; they do not proudly wrap their heads in a linen turban. Indeed, they obtained this name from the Arabic Sophy, not from the Greek word "sophos," which signifies wise and learned. And there were "Sofileri" among the Muslims long before Ismail the Sophy.* 

In short, this race of Ali and of the other children born to the daughters of Muhammad have thrown all the Muslims <note>original: "mahumetiſtes"</note> into great conflagrations and extreme ruin, especially in our time, or within the memory of our fathers. In Asia and Africa, the **Sharifs** <note>original: "xerifes"</note> have risen, and in Persia these **Sophys**, such that the Sharifs have ruined the African Kings and seized their lands and lordships while making war on the Christians and holding no friendship with the Turk; and the Sophys have annihilated the race of the **Uzun Hassan** <note>original: "Vſſuncás," a ruler of the Aq Qoyunlu Turkmen federation</note>, a Turkish race, to seize the monarchy of the Persians in this fashion. 

In the year of our Salvation 1248 (or according to some, in the year 1258) when the Tartars ruined the state of the Caliph of **Baghdad** <note>original: "Baldach"</note> and slew Al-Musta'sim <note>original: "Munibila," the last Abbasid Caliph of Baghdad</note>, the last great Muhammadan High Priest of Assyria—as this man had pursued the followers of Ali’s opinion unto death—with him dead and his greatness brought to nothing, there was one of the blood of the aforementioned Muhammad al-Mahdi named **Musa al-Kazim** <note>original: "Muça Cacé," the seventh of the Twelve Imams</note> who frankly and publicly began to preach the sect, follies, and delusions of Ali. Seizing a small province of Media named **Ardabil** <note>original: "Arduel"</note>, he held firm there and fortified himself with the strength of his disciples, as others of his accomplices had already done in various countries and regions of the earth. And because this country was the place of his retreat, those who made profession of his doctrine were called **Arduelins**, otherwise known as **Etnaxarins** <note>Twelvers, or Ithna 'ashari</note>, because *Enaxar* in the Arabic language signifies the number twelve; and they did this in memory of the 12 children of Ali and **Husayn** <note>original: "Huſcoin"</note>.

Strengthening himself with these captives—much as the Sultan of Great Cairo did with the **Mamluks** and the Great Turk does with the **Janissaries** <note>Elite military corps of the Ottoman Empire</note>—this false prophet used them to attack the Christians and laid waste to the lands of his neighbors, the Georgians, who refused to receive his false doctrine.

Meanwhile, Yaqub Beg happened to die, and **Hossein** <note>original: "Hoscen"</note> succeeded to the crown of Persia. These two children, raised outside the power of their tyrannical uncle and removed from the furious hands of their cousin, were carefully maintained by **Pyrai** <note>original: "Pirraih," likely a local Sufi leader or Pir</note>, Lord of **Lahijan** <note>original: "Legiā"</note>, who with his people favored the sect of **Ali**, of which the Safavids made such strict profession. While these children lived thus exiled and banished, a strong and furious war broke out among the children of Yaqub, King of Persia; so much so that in less than two years, the state of this great kingdom was seen to change five different times. # History of the Origin of the [Safavids]

...to fish in troubled waters, and accompanied by several of his relatives and friends, he went into his own country, where he was received with extreme joy by his subjects, who attributed to him the name and title of **Sophy** <note>original: "Sophy," from the Safavid dynasty, though European writers often confused it with the term "Sufi"</note>, as the principal head of their sect. It was then that the **Ardebil** accomplices began to publish everywhere that **Ismail** was the Prophet promised by God, come to plant the **Religion of Ali** <note>Shia Islam</note> throughout the East by force of arms; and they did so well that the army of the **Qizilbash** <note>original: "Cuſelbas," the "Red-Headed" Turkic tribesmen whose distinctive headgear marked their loyalty to the Safavids</note> increasing, the **Sophy** grew bold enough to attack **Tabriz** <note>original: "Tauris"</note>, the Metropolitan city of the land of the **Medes**, which he took in the year 1500 from **Alvand** <note>original: "Aluant," Alvand Mirza of the Aq Qoyunlu</note> who was its King, whom he defeated in battle. Entering that city by force, he committed such strange and furious cruelties upon the **Turcomans** that from that time on the name of the **Sophy** has been so hateful and fearsome to the Turks, his adversaries, that it could not be more so.

And since **Jacob** <note>Yaqub Beg of the Aq Qoyunlu</note>, his maternal uncle, had been the cause of his father's death, being unable to take revenge on him as he was already deceased, he commanded that the body of the deceased be pulled from its coffin, which he had burned, and its ashes scattered in the air, and the tomb completely ruined, in order to totally erase the memory of this prince. This **Sophy** was not content with having vented his rage upon the bones of his uncle; because his own mother—sister of the same Jacob—reproached him for this cruelty, he had her put to death, killing her with his own hands.

**Tabriz** having been won and **Alvand** in flight, the latter strengthened himself with men so much that having raised a large army, he came again against the Sophy, who, standing his ground, conquered him and put him to death in a combat. To him succeeded **Murad Khan** <note>original: "Morat Cam," the last ruler of the Aq Qoyunlu</note>, his elder brother; seeing what cruelty the Sophy exercised upon the **Turcomans**, and fearing he would drive him from his seat and take the crown of **Persia**, he raised the largest army possible. Taking the route to **Tabriz**, he felt strong enough to defeat his enemy and secure his Lordship. 

But however well-armed the Persians of **Murad Khan** were, and though both they and their horses were covered in mail and breastplates—just as the men-at-arms do in our **France**—nevertheless he lost the day; and all he could do was save himself in the city of **Baghdad** <note>original: "Bagadet"</note>, built near the ruins of ancient **Babylon**. The victorious Sophy did not leave a single man alive among those who fell into his hands; however, he was quite courteous to the women, who were, following the Persian custom, in the train of the royal camp, whom he gave as wives to his soldiers. It was then that he made himself Lord of the great city of **Shiraz** <note>original: "Siras"</note>, formerly named **Persepolis** <note>Modern Shiraz is near the ruins of Persepolis; early modern writers often conflated the two</note>, Capital of all this great kingdom, in the year of Salvation 1514. 

Thus this **Sophy Ismail**, from the poor fugitive and exile that he was, having become a powerful and fearsome King, resolved to extend the limits of his empire as far as **Egypt**, and as far as the lands of the **Turk**, who reigned, as he still does, in the city of **Constantinople**. If not for a sectarian pretending to be a new Prophet who rose up in Persia (the kind of man whom the wisest and most well-advised Muslim Kings fear and abhor no less than we Christians do heretics), there is no doubt that this Sophy would have struck a remarkable blow in the Asian territories subject to the Turk and in the lands of Egypt—despite the strength of the **Mamluks** <note>original: "Mamelus," the ruling military caste of Egypt and Syria at the time</note>—so strong and powerful had he entered into **Mesopotamia** and **Syria**. What has further incensed the Kings of Turkey against the Persians is that whenever one of the royal children of the Ottoman family, unhappy with his father and fleeing the fury of his relatives, has left and abandoned his country, he has almost always retreated to the Sophy for refuge. ### Concerning the Prediction or Prophecy of Muhammad regarding the duration of his Religion and Empire.

The Turks and other Muslims <note>The original uses "Mahometistes," a term used in the Renaissance to describe followers of Muhammad.</note> commonly hold and believe that their religion and empire will last little more than a thousand years. They assert that this was revealed to them by their Prophet Muhammad shortly before his death through certain signs. Specifically, while he was discussing the duration of the religion and empire he had founded with his followers, he extended and raised both hands, spreading out his ten fingers. His principal disciples first interpreted this as ten years; but once these had passed, they extended the term to a hundred years. When that time expired, they concluded that each finger signified a hundred years. Many Armenians have learned this from the aforementioned Turks and Muslims themselves and have revealed it to Christians. This is confirmed by P. Camerarius <note>Philipp Camerarius (1537–1624), a German scholar and magistrate.</note> in the second volume, third chapter of his *Historical Meditations*, and by J. Leunclavius <note>Johannes Leunclavius (c. 1533–1594), a prominent historian who specialized in Ottoman history.</note> in the preface to his *Turkish Muslim History*.

See what I write hereafter regarding another prediction or prophecy concerning the duration of the aforementioned religion and Empire of Muhammad in the subsequent chapter toward the end, citing T. Bibliander <note>Theodor Bibliander, the Swiss linguist who edited the first printed Latin Quran.</note> and B. Georgijevic <note>Baron Bartol Đurđević, a Croatian writer who had been a captive of the Turks.</note>. The late Guillaume Postel <note>A famous French polyglot and visionary (1510–1581) who traveled extensively in the East.</note> writes in the first book, third chapter of his *Oriental Histories* that because God gave Abraham and Hagar great blessings through Ishmael—as contained in the Holy Scriptures—it was necessary for the people and nation originating from him to reach the greatness of Empire seen for the last 900 years among all the peoples descended from Ishmael in the doctrine of Muhammad. In fact, in chapters 16, 17, and 20 of Genesis, it is written that Ishmael shall be great, and that his seed shall be beyond measure or numbering because of its immense size; this was not because of his mother Hagar, but because he was the seed and posterity of Abraham, since his seed was blessed in his body.

### Concerning the Al-Furqan or Al-Quran of Muhammad.

A certain person named Peter, Abbot of Cluny <note>Peter the Venerable (c. 1092–1156), who famously commissioned the first translation of the Quran into Latin.</note>, a great friend of Saint Bernard, was the first among the Latins to translate the Al-Furqan <term>Al-Furqan: An Arabic title for the Quran meaning "The Criterion" (the standard for judging right from wrong).</term> or Quran of Muhammad from the Arabic language into Latin. He shared it with scholars of the Latin language with the help of Peter of Toledo, Peter the Monk of Cluny, and Robert of Ketton <note>Robertus Ketenensis, a 12th-century English astronomer and translator.</note>.

& Herman the Dalmatian <note>Hermann of Dalmatia (c. 1100–c. 1160), a key figure in the translation of Arabic scientific and religious texts into Latin.</note>, very learned individuals in the Arabic language living in the year of Salvation 1143, wrote in their annotations on this *Alpurcan* or *Alkoran* <note>original Hebrew: אלקורן</note> (which is commonly interpreted as the *Doctrine of Muhammad*) that this word *Alkoran* signifies in the Arabic language a **Gathering, or Collection of precepts, or the Law of Muhammad, Prophet of the Arabs**. This *Alpurcan* or *Alkoran* is composed in very elegant and copious Arabic verses, and it is in no way permitted by the Muslims and "Mahometists" <note>A term used in the Renaissance for followers of Islam.</note> to translate it into any language whatsoever, as confirmed by the author of the *Fortress of the Faith* <note>Refers to Alfonso de Espina’s *Fortalitium Fidei* (c. 1460).</note>. It is divided and partitioned into 120 *Azoares* <note>The author uses "Azoares" for "Suras" (chapters). While the standard Quran has 114, historical counts by Western scholars sometimes varied.</note>, which we can interpret in French as faces, oracles, clauses, or distinctions. (For *Azoara* in Arabic is called "face" in Latin <note>original: "Nam Azoara Arabicè vultus Latinè dicitur..."</note>, from which that which the Latins call a "Chapter," the Arabs call an *Azoara*; for just as the face most clearly indicates who or what kind of man a person is, so the "Chapter" indicates what the following writing wishes to say. According to some, *Azoara* sounds like "oracle." For to it alone he attributes judgment.) These *Azoares* contain several rhapsodies from the Old and New Testament, the Jewish Talmuds, and many infinite heresies and false doctrines, as is very well known by those who have carefully seen and read this fine book printed in Germany, Italy, and other Provinces of this Europe. 

Friar Ricold or Richard <note>Riccoldo da Monte di Croce (c. 1243–1320), a Dominican missionary whose polemics against Islam were widely read.</note> of the Order of Preachers, a Florentine by nation, in his book on the *Refutation of the Law given by Muhammad to the Saracens*, asserts that the Alcoran is so named as if one were saying in Latin, **A collection of divine mandates** <note>original: "Diuinorum mandatorum collectionem"</note>. Because of this (according to them), the Prophet Muhammad called his wicked and unhappy doctrine by this name, which he redacted into writing—according to the history of the Saracens—with the help of a Naphé, Eon, Omar, Eleafar, Afir the sons of Chetir, and the sons of Aser or Amer; because this Muhammad
