But he profited as little as the first time; for this reason, he took and pillaged **Vera**, and **Plasencia**, **Santa Cruz**, **Trujillo**, and **Montánchez**, and in short, he left no corner of the Kingdom of **Toledo** where he did not exercise his fury and rage. Then passing into **Portugal**, he took the city of **Silves**, **Alcácer do Sal**, and destroyed **Sesimbra**, and **Palmela**, and other fortresses; then he went to **Andalusia** and from there to **Africa** to his city of **Morocco**, where he died full of riches and victories in the year of our salvation 1200. He had for his heir his son called **Muhammad the Green** <note>Muhammad al-Nasir, known as 'al-Nasir' or 'the Green' due to his standard or attire</note>, because he usually wore a green wig; he passed into **Spain** in the year 1210 and made great conquests over the **Christians**. He crossed over again in the year 1212 with more forces than any **Miramemolin** <note>original: "Miramomelin"; a corruption of the title 'Amir al-Mu'minin' or Commander of the Faithful</note> ever brought to **Spain**, and it is held that he had 80,000 horses, and a great number of **Moorish** Kings, and an infinity of footmen. Against him marched the Christian Kings of **Navarre**, **Leon**, and **Castile**, and the battle was furious and bloody on all sides; but in the end, the **Muslims** had the worst of it, and lost 200,000 men dead, and a great number of prisoners. **Aben Muhammad** and his brother **Abenzeit** escaped on horseback, and fearing to lose **Morocco**, he recrossed the sea as soon as possible, leaving the miserable **Moors** of **Spain** so discomforted that they did not know from what wood to make their arrows <note>original: "ne fçauoient de quel bois faire flefches"; an idiom meaning they were at a complete loss or lacked any means to defend themselves</note>. This rout greatly diminished the authority and credit of **Aben Muhammad the Almohad**, as many who previously feared and respected him abandoned him. Among others was his own brother **Zeitabozeit** <note>Abu Zayd</note>, who seized **Valencia** and made himself King and Lord. **Aben Muhammad** his cousin named himself King of **Baeza** and usurped **Cordoba**, the lands of the domain of **Toledo**, and **Andalusia**. In the year 1227, **Aben Hut** <note>Ibn Hud, a leader who rose against the Almohads</note>, hearing that **Aben Mahomet** King of **Baeza** was dead, came to **Murcia** and made himself King there under the pretext of chasing the heretical **Almohads** out of **Spain**, and wishing to restore the original faith as they held it from their fathers. He killed the **Almohads** without any mercy, having the **Mosques** washed and cleaned very superstitiously, deeming them polluted by the others. This gave him such favor that in a short time he was made King of **Murcia** and of the greater part of **Andalusia**: although **Zael**, the last King of **Valencia**, and one **Abenillale**, King of **Seville**, resisted him. These were descended from **Abdelmon** <note>Abd al-Mu'min</note>, the first King of the **Almohads**, whose line came to an end eighty-one years after **Abdelmon** planted the doctrine of his agent **Almohadi** <note>Ibn Tumart, the Mahdi</note> and established his power there. 

But in the year 1235, the **Christian** Kings coming to assail **Cordoba**, they took it. King **Aben Hut** having been slain by one of his servants, and the **Spanish Moors** being in turmoil, they began each to usurp his own lordship; but their greatest strength and power was transferred to the Kingdom of **Granada**, as I describe hereafter. From what we have described above, we can judge how difficult it would be to demonstrate the predecessors of all the **Moorish** Kings, both of **Africa** and of **Spain**, since the most vile and abject have attained the Crown there. Such we have seen in **Abdelmon**, son of a potter, and he who was the first King of **Granada**, who was also of low birth and a native of **Arjona**, who was surnamed **Alhamar** <note>Muhammad I ibn al-Ahmar, founder of the Nasrid dynasty</note>. After the death of **Aben Hut**, he was raised to the Royal throne by the **Moors** in the year 1236, with several cities of **Andalusia** pledging him obedience, among which was **Granada**. This city grew large because, as the **Christian** Kings of **Spain** made great conquests over the **Moors**, those who fled the captured towns took refuge in **Granada**, and by settling there, they were also the reason the Kings established their seat and residence there. 

Against this **Muhammad**, the first King of **Granada**, there opposed himself at the beginning a powerful **Moorish** Lord called **Soysemel** <note>Likely a corruption of a name like Abu Sa'id or Zayyan</note>, who subjected the King of **Murcia** and took several towns in the land of **Andalusia**. He also constrained this **Muhammad** to be his tributary and, leaving him in peace, threw himself upon the **Sevillians**, who had not pledged obedience to the King of **Granada**, and who in the year 1248 surrendered to the King of **Castile**. The King then resolved to cross into **Africa** against **Caid Arrax**, King of **Morocco**, but he died in **Seville**.

In the year 1252, four years after the capture of this city <note>Referring to Seville, which fell to the Christians in 1248</note> which had remained for 534 years under the subjection of the **Moors**, **Muhammad**, King of **Granada**, renewed the peace and confederation with **Don Alfonso**, King of **Castile**, whom he went to visit as far as **Toledo**. All of **Andalusia** did not yet obey this King **Muhammad**, for there was a King at **Algarve** named **Aben Mofad**; and without fail, if the **Moors** had not thus divided their power, the **Christians** would hardly have so quickly regained possession of the Kingdom lost by the **Goths**. At **Jerez** and **Niebla** there was another petty king named **Aben Amet**. Both were vassals of the King of **Castile**, but in the year 1261, along with the King of **Granada**, they revolted against the **Castilian** and took several towns and fortresses from him. To pursue this King, **Muhammad** brought from **Morocco** a thousand horses; the soldiers arriving upon them called themselves *Merins* or *Marins* <note>The Marinids, a Zenata Berber tribe who eventually replaced the Almohads as rulers of Morocco</note>, all of the same family, and sent by **Yusuf**, King of **Morocco**. These men were so well favored by **Muhammad** that his subjects, feeling envy and spite, revolted and committed many evils in the lands subject to their Princes. I have spoken here of **Yusuf**, King of **Morocco**, descendant of **Jacob**, and father of this **Muhammad** surnamed the **Green** <note>Likely referring to the Almohad Caliph Muhammad al-Nasir, though the author’s genealogy conflates Almohad and Marinid leaders</note> who was defeated in **Spain**. Upon his death, his nephew **Caid Arrax** <note>The Almohad Caliph al-Sa'id</note> reigned in **Morocco**, of whom we spoke above, the fifth of the **Almohad** race in **Africa**, governing all the country from the **Atlantic Ocean** as far as **Egypt**. Among other governors, this man had one at **Tlemcen** <note>original: "Tremissen"</note> called **Yaghmurasen ibn Zyan** <note>original: "Gomarança Aben Zien"</note>, of a race called the **Abdalwadids** <note>original: "Abdalnés"</note> subject to the **Almohads**. Because he did not conduct himself as he should have in his government, he fell into the enmity of King **Caid Arrax**, who went to besiege him in a castle called **Tremezezir**. However, a cousin of the besieged man, feigning to surrender to the King and show him the weakest points of the place, treacherously killed him. While the soldiers were troubled and astonished by the death of the King, **Yaghmurasen** came out of the castle, fell upon them, and made a great massacre. He then made himself King of **Tlemcen**, and their dynasty lasted a long time. At the same time, there was a lineage or family at **Fez** called the *Merins*, from a powerful citizen named **Merin**, who was first a **Christian**, but his successors became **Moors** <note>This claim of Christian origin is a common medieval historiographic trope or error; the Marinids were Berbers</note>. One of this race named **Abu Bakr ibn Merin** <note>original: "Bucarben Merin"</note>, being governor of **Fez** for **Caid Arrax**, hearing of the success of the **Almohads** at **Tlemcen** and how the fugitives had been defeated by his own men, also named himself King of **Fez**. Another brother of his, called **Aben Yusuf**, was made lord of **Rabat** <note>original: "Ribaté"</note>, much to the great astonishment of the **Almohads**, who made **Al-Murtada** <note>original: "Almorcada"</note>, a relative of the deceased **Caid Arrax**, King of **Morocco**. He immediately made war on the **Marinids** of **Fez**, who defeated him, and from then on the lordship of these two cities was separated. **Abu Bakr ibn Merin**, upon dying, left a son of young age named **Yahya** <note>original: "Hiaya"</note>, who was placed under the guardianship of his uncle **Aben Yusuf**. But the child dying, the uncle was made King of **Fez** and was greatly esteemed among the **Africans**, so that he was called the "Great Old Man of the Marinids." To him fled a cousin of King **Al-Murtada** of **Morocco**, whose name was **Abu Dabbus** <note>original: "Budebuz"</note>, revolting against his Prince and praying for help from this **Marinid**, promising him a great expanse of country for the enlargement of the Kingdom of **Fez** if he would help him obtain the lordship of **Morocco**. **Yusuf the Marinid** was joyful at...

Furthermore, you see how much this account serves the history of the **Saracens**, **Africans**, and **Spaniards**, in which mention is made of the **Merins** and the **Almohads**. The race of the latter has not been so completely extinguished that even today the Kings of **Tunis** <note>The Hafsid dynasty</note> are not descended from them, a fact in which they glory because of the great men who have come from that line—even though their origin was (as has been said) from a potter. Such was also the origin in former times of **Agathocles**, King of **Sicily**, and in our own time that of **Barbarossa**, King of **Algiers**, a native of the island of **Mytilene** <note>Original: "Meletin"</note>. He was born to a potter, but because that trade displeased him, he became a corsair and was one of the greatest captains of our century.

Returning to **Muhammad**, King of **Granada**, and his successor: seeing that his affairs were not going well while he was at war with the King of **Castile**, he sought a way to confer with him. Having come to an interview, it was agreed that the **Moor** would leave the league of the King of **Murcia** and his **Moors**, and that he and his heirs would pay the Kings of **Castile** two hundred and fifty thousand *maravedis* <note>A medieval Spanish currency</note> in **Castilian** money. In exchange, the **Castilian** King would return the lands of **Malaga** and **Guadix** to him, and the **Granadan** would provide aid to the **Christians** to conquer the Kingdom of **Murcia**.

When the **Castilian** failed to fulfill the contents of what had been agreed, **Muhammad** asked for help from the King of **Morocco**. The latter granted it all the more easily because he was aggrieved that the **Castilian** had taken the city of **Cadiz** <note>Original: "Calix"</note> on the strait, which had been recommended to his protection. Even this was not enough, for **Muhammad** managed to ensure that several of the greatest lords of **Castile** revolted against their King. To win them over, the **Castilian** employed the King of **Morocco**, but they would never listen to him until the **Castilian** fulfilled all the articles of the agreement made between him and **Muhammad**, King of **Granada**.

During these events, in the year 1273, in the month of January—which the **Moors** call *Jumada* <note>Original: "Iudemi," likely referring to the Islamic month of Jumada al-Thani</note>—King **Muhammad**, the first of that name in **Granada**, died. He was succeeded by his son, also named **Muhammad**, surnamed *Commander of the Muslims* <note>Original: "Mir Almus Lemin," a corruption of the title Amir al-Muslimin</note>. It was not that many **Moors** did not try to let the crown fall into the hands of the younger of **Muhammad's** children, named **Yusuf ibn al-Ahmar** <note>Original: "Iucep aben Alhamar"</note>, but the **Castilian** lords who were in **Granada** blocked this move and had the crown given to the eldest as his just due. This **Muhammad II** solicited the King of **Morocco**, **Abu Yusuf** <note>Original: "Aben Iucep"</note>, to cross over into **Europe**, offering him the ports of **Algeciras** <note>Original: "Agerize"</note> and **Tarifa**. **Yusuf** sent people to take these places in his name for his greater security, and then he himself passed into **Spain** with 17,000 horsemen. He and **Muhammad** met and agreed to attack the **Christians** from two directions. **Abu Yusuf**, for his part, defeated a general of the King of **Castile**, whose head he sent to **Muhammad**. After this, **Aben Iucep** <note>Abu Yusuf Yaqub ibn Abd al-Haqq</note>, King of **Morocco**, died, and he was succeeded by **Aben Iacob** <note>Abu Yaqub Yusuf al-Nasir</note>, the second King of **Morocco** of the family of the **Merins** <note>The Marinid dynasty</note>, in the year 1288. He, wishing to cross the strait to come into **Spain**, was hindered near **Tangier**, or **Tingi**, and for that reason returned to **Africa**. And **Muhammad**, taking advantage of the Christian quarrels, overran **Andalusia** and acquired some lands there; at last, bearing the title of victor, he died in the year of grace 1302, in the month of May called **Ramadan**.

He was succeeded by **Muhammad Alhamar** <note>Muhammad III al-Ahmar</note>, third King of **Granada**, his son, who had another male sibling named **Muhammad Aben Naçar** <note>Muhammad ibn Nasr</note>. The eldest, who was King, was blind, though not from birth; nevertheless, he did not cease to make war on the Christian Kings by means of **Farrachen** <note>Faraj ibn Isma'il</note>, Lord of **Ceuta**, his brother-in-law. Nonetheless, it was necessary in the end that he do homage to the King of **Castile**. While living in peace with them, there was a Moorish subject who, usurping the city of **Almería**, declared himself King; this fellow was named **Aborrabé** <note>Possibly Abu al-Rabi</note>, and he crossed into **Africa** to usurp **Ceuta**, which belonged to the Kings of **Granada**, to harm the poor blind **Muhammad** by every means. Though perhaps not dispossessed of his kingdom by the Christians, he was so by his own brother **Muhammad Aben Azar** <note>Muhammad IV</note>, who seized it and became the fourth King of **Granada**, cruelly putting to death his poor, innocent, and blind brother.

This murderous King, thinking to be at rest after the death of his brother and having peace with the King of **Castile**, saw himself attacked from elsewhere. For the entire city of **Granada** mutinied by means of one of his nephews called **Ismail**, son of his sister and wife of the aforementioned **Farrachen**, Lord of **Ceuta** and **Málaga**. This **Ismail** was supported and favored by his father and by **Osmin** <note>Uthman ibn Abi al-Ula</note> of the race of the **Merins** of **Morocco**, and other Moors of their league. Coming to blows, **Muhammad** was defeated and besieged in the Citadel of **Granada**, which he surrendered by agreement, yielding the crown to **Ismail** and going to **Guadix** to spend the rest of his days in the year of salvation 1313.

**Ismail** was the fifth King of **Granada** on the female side, the male line having failed through him. He was attacked by the Christians in favor of his uncle **Muhammad**, and lost a battle and several towns. For this reason, to take advantage of the Castilian forces, he sent to the King of **Morocco** for aid, giving him some lands in compensation. In this war, the Princes of **Castile**, **John** and **Peter**, were slain. After their death, he lived in peace until a cousin of his named **Muhammad** conspired against him because of a very beautiful Christian slave girl whom **Muhammad** had captured and whom the King wished to keep. He took his pretext from elsewhere, saying that the Kingdom belonged to him more than to **Ismail**, as he was of the royal blood on the male side, whereas the other only came to it through the females. However, he did not achieve his design; for although he mortally wounded the King, by the great loyalty and valor of a Moor, the conspirators were taken and executed before the King died. He was succeeded by his son **Muhammad**, King of **Granada**, in the year 1322. Nevertheless, the traitorous author of the conspiracy escaped, as we shall say hereafter. Thus Albohadi was the seventh Moroccan King, but assailed by his father he lost the Royalty, and Aben Iucep, re-entering into his dignity, disinherited him and named as his successor Albohacen, of whom we spoke recently, who was the eighth of the blood of the Merins: against whom was Albohali, who besieged the city of Morocco, where he could do nothing other than pillage its territory, but Albohacen went to besiege him at Soiumança <note>Sijilmasa</note> and constrained him to give up his Royal title and to give him Bozien his son as a hostage: and then he made war on the King of Tremissen who had helped Albohali, whose lands he conquered, making himself King of Morocco, of Soiumança, and of Tremissen, toward whom, as we have said, the King of Granada came to Garant. As has been said above, having strengthened himself with the children of Osmin <note>Uthman ibn Abi al-Ula</note>, his old friend, he also seized the palace of Granada and drove Mahomet Lagus <note>Muhammad V of Granada, also known as al-Ghani</note> from his lordship. Then, using his customary ruses, he made an alliance with the King of Castile, while simultaneously maintaining secret dealings with the King of Aragon against the Castilian, and he even tried to bring the King of Morocco into this league. 

But Albohanen <note>Abu Inan Faris</note>, son of the aforementioned Alboacen, did not wish to betray the Castilian; instead, he warned him of the treasons of this Alnahar <note>Muhammad VI, often called "the Red" (al-Ahmar)</note>. For these reasons, King Dom Pedro <note>Peter of Castile, known as "the Cruel"</note> of Castile had this Mahomet publicly executed in the city of Seville, under the pretext of carrying out justice against those who had treacherously murdered King Ismael <note>Ismail II</note>; and this justice was carried out in 1362. At that time, Mahomet the Old <note>Muhammad V, restored to power</note> was returned to his lordship, and he came to the aid of Dom Pedro in all the wars he fought against the Aragonese. 

After this, King Mahomet conquered several lands from the Christians, taking advantage of the quarrels and factions that existed between Dom Pedro and Henry the Bastard <note>Henry II of Castile, who led a civil war against his half-brother Peter</note>. In this time, Abaifer Abdelazis <note>Abu Faris Abd al-Aziz I</note>, descended from the blood and race of the Merins <note>The Marinid dynasty</note>, reigned in Fez. Mahomet refused to make peace with Henry, King of Castile, so great was his friendship with the deceased Dom Pedro; for this reason, he went to besiege Algeciras, which he took and ruined from top to bottom because of the great disasters it had caused the Mahometan sect. Then this old man died in the year of our Salvation 1379.

He was succeeded by Mahomet Guadix, his son, the tenth in the number of the Kings of Granada. He was surnamed Guadix because from his childhood he had always been very dedicated to enlarging, enriching, and embellishing the city of Guadix, one of the principal cities of the country of Granada. He was the first of the Kings of Granada to hold his lordship without being disturbed by any violence whatsoever. He was also loyal to his word, and having made a peace or a truce, he never broke it, whether it was with the Castilian or with the Moors of Africa. He occupied himself well with fortifying the frontier towns and arming himself for the future with everything necessary for war, should it come to that; he died in the year 1392, having reigned only eleven years.

He was succeeded by Yusuf <note>Yusuf II</note>, his son, who, having not yet reigned for long, saw his son Mahomet revolt and attempt to take the crown from him, incited by a great Moorish Lord called Aben Mohayà. But the King of Morocco, acting as arbiter, settled this dispute and ensured that the son submitted to the will of his father. This Yusuf had four children: namely, Yusuf the eldest, Mahomet the rebel, the third Cidi Aly, and the last Cidi Amet. 

He lived in peace with his neighbors, never thinking there was anyone who bore him hatred; but the King of Fez took a dislike to him, and to remove him from this world, he sent him beautiful presents, as one friend sends to another. Among these were magnificently worked shirts, but they were so poisoned that when the King put them on, it was impossible to escape death. Thus the poor Prince, accepting the gifts and putting on one of these shirts, was seized by the strength of the poison in such a way that, despite all remedies, he died thirty days later, in the year of our Salvation 1396. Mahomet, his second son, who had rebelled against him, was his successor and was surnamed Aben Balua <note>Muhammad VII</note>, usurping the crown from his elder brother, Yusuf <note>Yusuf III</note>, since he had not been able to snatch it from his father. As soon as he became King, he tried to make friends with the Kings of Africa, and then he made war on the Kings of Castile, but he lost two battles: one in the year 1406 and the other in 1407.

And the year after, he died at the Alhambra; which was the palace and fortress of Granada, where the Kings were accustomed to retire; and his eldest son Yusuf <note>Yusuf III, reigned 1408–1417; though the text suggests 1423</note> became King after him, who had been a prisoner at Salobreña <note>original: "Salobrenan," a coastal fortress used as a royal prison</note>: but as soon as the Tyrant was dead, they brought the legitimate heir to Granada, who waged war against the Castilians, against whom he sent his brothers Sidi Ali and Sidi Ahmad <note>original: "Cidi Aly, & Cidi Amet"</note> with 5,000 horsemen and 80,000 footmen, who were defeated, with 15,000 Moors dying there. And because in Gibraltar there were many African Moors, strongly devoted to the Marinids of Morocco, they revolted against Yusuf, aided by the King of Morocco, who sent his brother Abu Sa'id <note>original: "Aben Bucid"</note> there with a thousand horsemen: but Yusuf went to besiege them, and winning over the African Prince, he urged him to conquer the kingdom of Fez and Morocco, which he did by stripping his brother of power, and Yusuf subdued the rebels of Gibraltar. After this conquest, and having made a truce with the King of Castile, and left his country at peace, he died in the year of our Lord 1423, and the fifteenth of his reign. Muhammad ibn al-Aysar <note>original: "Mahomet Aben Azar"</note>, nicknamed the Left-handed <note>Muhammad IX of Granada</note>, succeeded his father Yusuf, and was three times driven from his lordship, first by means of a gallant named Muhammad the Little <note>Muhammad VIII</note>, who made himself King in the year 1427. Muhammad al-Aysar fled to Tunis, where he was well received and given help to recover his lands. Meanwhile, the Tyrant went about mistreating the friends of the fugitive King, and among others one called Ibn al-Sarradj <note>original: "Aben Carrax," leader of the noble Abencerrages family</note>, whom he drove from Granada; it would have been better for him to have put him to death, as he was the cause of his ruin. Seeing that by negotiating with the Kings of Castile and Tunis, the fugitive Muhammad returned with forces, and recovering his lands, he had this usurper beheaded. But he was ungrateful toward the King of Castile, so God permitted that he be punished for his ingratitude; for the Moorish lords of the blood of Muhammad al-Ahmar <note>The founder of the Nasrid dynasty</note> revolted, and one named Yusuf ibn al-Mawl <note>original: "Iucep Aben Almad," Yusuf IV</note> made himself King of Granada in the year 1432. This Al-Mawl was not King for long, for he lived only six months after his advancement to the crown; rather, he died in that same year 1432, in the month of June, called by the Moors Shawwal <note>original: "Sauel," the tenth month of the Islamic lunar calendar</note>, and once again the Left-handed Muhammad was placed on his throne. Being a man who could not live in peace, he began war against the Castilians; but meanwhile there was a nephew of his named Muhammad ibn Osmin <note>Muhammad X</note>, who, coming to Granada, made himself master of the Palace and of the King himself, whom he imprisoned, and declared himself King of Granada, this deprivation occurring in the year of grace 1445, in the month of September called by the Moors Al-Mu'tazz <note>original: "Almuhataz"</note>. Against this Ibn Osmin, the friends of Muhammad al-Aysar, seeing they could not pull him from prison, raised up a cousin of his named Ibn Ismail <note>Ismail, later Yusuf V or Saad</note>, who was in Castile, and who with the permission of the Castilian King came to Granada and was made a rival King to the other. But Ibn Osmin, fighting the Christians valiantly and defeating them, dispossessed the one who challenged him for the crown, yet very soon after found himself stripped of it by the same. Ismail II <note>original: "Aben Iſmael ſecond du nom"</note> came to the crown in the year of our salvation 1453, and had great wars with the Castilians: but in the end he lost more than he gained in them, for the Christians conquered the city of Gibraltar, which served as a retreat and passage for the Moors of Barbary <note>North Africa</note>; this was the reason that Ismail made peace with the Christians, then passed from this world in the year 1465, in the month of April, which the Moors call Sha'ban <note>original: "Sahaben," the eighth month of the Islamic calendar</note>. He was driven from his lordship three times: first, by means of a rogue named Muhammad the Little <note>Muhammad VIII, known as *al-Saghir*</note>, who made himself King in the year 1427. Muhammad Azar fled to Tunis, where he was well received and received help to recover his lands. Seeing that by negotiating with the Kings of Castile and Tunis, the fugitive Muhammad returned with forces and, recovering his lands, had the head of this usurper cut off. But he was ungrateful toward the King of Castile, so God allowed him to be punished for his ingratitude; because the Moorish lords of the blood of Muhammad al-Ahmar <note>The founder of the Nasrid dynasty</note> revolted, and one named Yusuf Aben Almao <note>Yusuf IV</note> made himself King of Granada in the year 1432. 

This Almao was not King for long, for he lived only six months after his advancement to the crown; rather, he died in that same year 1432 in the month of June, called *Shawwal* <note>original: "Sauel"</note> by the Moors, and once again Muhammad the Left-Handed was placed on his throne. Being a man who could not live in peace, he began a war against the Castilians. But meanwhile, there was a nephew of his named Muhammad Aben Hozmen <note>Muhammad X, known as *al-Ahnaf*</note>, who, coming to Granada, made himself master of the Palace and of the King himself, whom he imprisoned, and styled himself King of Granada, this deprivation occurring in the year of grace 1445, in the month of September, called *al-Muharram* <note>original: "Almuhataz"</note> by the Moors. 

Against this Aben Hozmen, the friends of Muhammad Aben Azar, seeing they could not pull him from prison, raised up a cousin of his named Aben Ismael <note>Ismail II</note>, who was in Castile; he, with the permission of the Castilian King, came to Granada and was made a rival King. But Aben Hozmen, fighting the Christians valiantly and defeating them, dispossessed the one who challenged him for the crown, and all too soon saw himself stripped of it by the same man.

### History of the Origin of the [Turks] ###

It is written regarding this matter that in the time of Shalmaneser <note>Shalmaneser V, King of the Neo-Assyrian Empire</note>, King of the Assyrians, the Jews were led into captivity in Assyria, then placed in settlements in the cities of Halah and Habor near the river Gozan in Media, just as is contained in Book 4, chapters 17 and 18 of the Kings <note>modern 2 Kings 17–18</note>. These Jews, being scattered and dispersed throughout the East and North, gave rise to the stories told of the "lost," "enclosed," and "reserved" Jews of the East, from whom the Turks and Tartars have descended and proceeded. Even today, some of the Hordes of these people in the northernmost provinces have retained and still retain the name of Dan <note>original: "Dam"</note>, others of Zebulun, others of Naphtali, and others of Tabor. See A. Thevet <note>André Thevet (1516–1590), a French Franciscan explorer and writer</note>, book 10, chapter 17 of his *Universal Cosmography*. Furthermore, Rabbi Solomon <note>Solomon ben Isaac, known as Rashi (1040–1105), a medieval French rabbi</note> in his commentaries on chapter 27 of Isaiah reported that it was contained in the *Annals of the Hebrews* that the ten tribes of Israel were lost in the East in ancient times. This was the reason that their children and successors, named Turks and Tartars, so freely embraced Islam <note>original: "Mahometisme"</note>, because from all ancient times they had been circumcised and were already imbued with the character <note>original: "couleurs" (literally "colors")</note> of the Islamic religion, according to G. Génébrard <note>Gilbert Génébrard (1535–1597), a French Benedictine theologian</note>, book 1 of his *Chronography*. The ancient authors Pliny, Mela, and Ptolemy make some mention of them when they made their home near the Caspian Sea and Mount Caucasus.

Laonikos Chalkokondyles <note>A 15th-century Byzantine historian</note>, book 1, writes that he does not know what the ancient name of the Turks was, though there are authors who trace their descent from the Scythians called Tartars, as they do not differ greatly in customs, and their language is nearly the same. They also say that the Scythians, crossing the Taurus <note>original: "Taues," likely referring to the Taurus Mountains</note> seven times, passed into Upper Asia, which they plundered and ravaged while the Parthians were then in command there, enjoying lands that had once been under the hand of the Medes, Persians, and Assyrians. Having done this, they subjugated Lower Asia and the provinces of Phrygia, Lydia, and Cappadocia; as it is said, one can still see many of these men dispersed throughout Asia, who live and interact just like the Scythians called Nomads—whom one might call shepherds or cattle-drivers—having no fixed place nor certain house. In any part of Asia, they have yet another conjecture by which they wish to prove that the Turks are descended from the Scythians, insofar as Lower Asia is now inhabited by the barbarian Turks, and those who stay in Lydia, Caria, Phrygia, and Cappadocia have nothing that differs—whether in language, clothing, customs, or way of life—from the Scythians who dwell in that region which lies between the river Tanais <note>The Don River</note> and Sarmatia. Others estimate that the Turks took their source from the Parthians; for the latter, being afflicted by the wandering Scythians called Nomads and being unable to prevail against them, went into Lower Asia where they also lived as wanderers without any fixed stay, keeping themselves in their portable houses inside wagons. Finally, one sees that they spread through the cities where they now dwell; from which it happened that these men were called Turks <note>original: "Turs"</note>, just as one might say "wandering shepherds" or "Nomads." On this subject, one should see Aeneas Sylvius <note>Enea Silvio Piccolomini, later Pope Pius II</note> in his *Asia*, chapter 100, alleging a certain philosopher Aethicus <note>original: "Ethique," referring to Aethicus Ister, the purported author of a late-antique cosmography</note>.

Hayton the Armenian <note>Hethum of Korykos, a medieval chronicler</note> in his histories, chapters 3 and 15 on the Tartars, holds that the Turks came from the Parthians and from that province which even today is called Turkestan, and was called Aria by the ancients and by Ptolemy.

<summary>This page explores various 16th-century theories regarding the ethnic and geographical origins of the Turks and Tartars, notably the legend that they were descended from the Ten Lost Tribes of Israel. It cites a mix of biblical, rabbinical, and classical sources to link Central Asian nomads with ancient Middle Eastern migrations.</summary>

# Languages of this World #

...having Bactria and Margiana <note>original: "Mangiane"</note> toward the North, the region of the Parthians to the West, and the desert of Caramania, Drangiana <note>original: "Dragiane"</note> to the South, and the land of the Paropamisadae <note>a region of the Hindu Kush</note> to the East, who are subjects of Turkestan under the rule of the Tartars. <margin>a André Thevet, book 9, chapter 3 of his *Universal Cosmography*.</margin> André Thevet speaks thus of the Turks and their country: the Turks formerly came out of Turkestan; now the province which is still called Turkestan, quite near the Caspian Mountains and those named the Tapurs <note>a tribe near the Caspian Sea</note> joining the Medes, and consequently in Northern Scythia, is not far from the Parthians and Hyrcanians, along the great river Chesel <note>likely the Jaxartes or Syr Darya</note>, which comes from the sunrise and flows into the Caspian Sea at the borders of the land of Hyrcania. It should be noted that the Turks have no difficulty confessing their origin to be from that land. However, because this land has changed its name today—indeed since the Eastern Tartars <note>the Mongols</note> came to attack it in the time of Ogedei Khan <note>original: "Occatam Cam"</note>, for previously they were in their full liberty under the name of Turkestan—it is necessary to show by what means the said Turks left their infertile land to find new seats. This occurred at the time when the great overflows of the Northern peoples were causing the ruin of the world: namely the Huns (who were also European and Asiatic Scythians), the Goths, Visigoths, and Ostrogoths, the Alans and Vandals having passed their fury, and the Lombards afflicting Italy in the time of King Pepin, father of Charlemagne. It was then that these Turks passed the Caspian Gates at Derbent <note>original: "Derbenth"</note> and occupied Armenia in the year of salvation 764. Not that they were yet so powerful as to be able to wage war or hold status against neighboring princes; rather, they kept to the mountains and the depths of the woods and forests, not daring to attack the armies of their neighbors in the open field, but being only on the lookout to pillage and ransack the places they saw without great defense, etc. <margin>b See what he continues to write next in chapter 4 following these Tartars, this same Thevet, and in his book 11, chapter 1, on the origin of the Turks and their successes.</margin> <margin>c G. Génébrard, book 4 of his *Chronography*.</margin> Those who are well-versed in the knowledge of the most ancient languages know well enough that this word "Turks" signifies, in the Hebrew language, "cursed people, excommunicated, detestable, exiled, driven out, and banished." The Muslims <note>original: "mahometistes, Musulmans"</note> and Turks of today hold this word among themselves, as I have already remarked, in great contempt and hatred; indeed, they hold it to be an atrocious and execrable insult. This has some appearance of truth, insofar as their Prophet Muhammad <note>original: "Machumet"</note>, in order not to offend them—and the Tartars who began to awaken around the year of salvation 1200—retained in his Quran <note>original: "Alcoran or Alfurcan"</note> circumcision, and the purifications and ceremonies of the law of Moses for the reasons previously deduced by us. <margin>d Sigismund the Ambassador in his *Commentaries on Muscovite Affairs*.</margin> <note>original: "Turcas se vocari ægrè ferunt..."</note> "They take it poorly to be called Turks, and consider it a disgrace, but they rejoice to be called 'Besermani' <note>a corruption of 'Musulmans' or Muslims</note>, and by that name the Turks also wish to be called." <margin>e J. Leunclavius in his *Turkish Onomasticon*.</margin> <note>original: "Iurki, Tzurki, Zurki Turki nomen idē quod Nomades..."</note> "Iurki, Tzurki, Zurki, and Turk are names that signify the same as Nomads or wandering Shepherds." At the beginning, the Turks lived like the Nomads, and even in Anatolia <note>original: "Natolie"</note> those who lead livestock are still called "Turcomanleri" <note>Turkmens</note> by them. Indeed, these Turks are currently ignorant of the name "Saracens" <note>original: "Sarrafins"</note>, by which they were called in preceding centuries, although they still boast and brag at present of being children descended from Hagar <note>Abraham's handmaid and mother of Ishmael</note>...

...written regarding this matter that in the time of Shalmaneser <note>original: "Salmanafar"</note>, King of the Assyrians, the Jews were led into captivity in Assyria, then placed in settlements in the cities of Halah and Habor <note>original: "Hala & Habor"</note> near the river Gozan in Media, as is contained in the Fourth Book of Kings <note>modern 2 Kings</note>, chapters 17 and 18; and that these Jews, being scattered and dispersed through the East and the North, gave rise to the stories of the "lost Jews," enclosed and reserved in the East, from whom the Turks and Tartars have come and proceeded. Furthermore, Rabbi Solomon <note>Rashi, the famous medieval commentator</note> in his commentaries on the 27th chapter of Isaiah reported that it was contained in the Hebrew Annals that ten tribes of Israel were lost in the East in ancient times. Laonicus Chalcondyles <note>a 15th-century Byzantine historian</note> writes in book 1 that he does not know what the ancient name of the Turks was, as there are authors who make them descendants of the Scythians called Tartars, insofar as they do not differ greatly in customs, and their language is almost identical. They also say that the Scythians, crossing the Taurus <note>original: "Taues"</note> seven times, passed into High Asia, which they pillaged and ravaged while the Parthians commanded there and enjoyed the lands that had formerly been under the hand of the Medes, Persians, and Assyrians. Having done this, they subjugated Low Asia <note>Asia Minor</note> and the provinces of Phrygia, Lydia, and Cappadocia; and as it is said, one can still see many of these men dispersed through Asia, who live and converse exactly like the Scythians called Nomads, whom one may call shepherds or cowherds. Having no fixed place or certain house in any part of Asia, they have yet another conjecture by which they wish to prove that the Turks are descended from the Scythians: because Low Asia is now inhabited by the barbarian Turks, and those who stay in Lydia, Caria, Phrygia, and Cappadocia have nothing that differs—whether in language, clothing, customs, or way of life—from the Scythians who stay in that region between the river Tanais <note>the Don River</note> and Sarmatia. Others estimate that the Turks took their source from the Parthians; for these latter, being afflicted by the wandering Scythians called Nomads and unable to prevail against them, went away into Low Asia, where they likewise lived as wanderers and without any fixed stop, staying in their portable houses inside wagons. Finally, we see that they spread through the cities where they now live, from which it happened that these men were called Turks, which is to say "vagabond shepherds" or "Nomads." On this subject, one should see Aeneas Silvius <note>Pope Pius II</note> in his *Asia*, chapter 100, citing some Ethic philosopher or other.

### Languages of this World ###

...having Bactria <note>An ancient region in Central Asia, mostly in modern Afghanistan</note> and Margiana <note>original: "Mangiane", an ancient region around the city of Merv</note> toward the North, the region of the Parthians to the West, the Caramanian desert, Drangiana <note>original: "Dragiane", an ancient region in modern-day Iran and Afghanistan</note> to the South, and the land of the Paropanisadae <note>People of the Hindu Kush mountains</note> to the East—all of whom are subjects in Turkestan under the obedience of the Tartars. André Thevet, in book 9, chapter 3 of his *Universal Cosmography*, speaks thus of the Turks and their country: From Turkestan in former times came the Turks; now the province which is still called Turkestan, quite near the Caspian mountains and those called the Tapuri <note>original: "Tapurs"</note> bordering the Medes, and consequently in Northern Scythia, is not far from Parthia and Hyrcania. It lies along the great river Chesel <note>likely the Jaxartes or Syr Darya</note>, which comes from the rising sun and flows into the Caspian Sea at the borders of the country of Hyrcania. Here it must be noted that the Turks have no difficulty confessing their origin to be from that country. However, because this country has changed its name at present—indeed since the Eastern Tartars came to attack it in the time of Ögedei Khan <note>original: "Occatam Cam", the son and successor of Genghis Khan</note>, because previously they were in full liberty under the title of Turkestan—it is necessary to show by what means the said Turks left their infertile land to find new seats. 

This occurred at the time when the great overflows of Northern peoples took place for the ruin of the world: namely the Huns (who were also European and Asiatic Scythians), the Goths, Visigoths, and Ostrogoths, the Alans, and Vandals. After their fury had passed, and while the Lombards were afflicting Italy in the time of King Pepin, father of Charlemagne, it was then that these Turks passed the Caspian Gates at Derbent <note>original: "Derbenth", a city in modern Dagestan known as the gateway between the Eurasian Steppe and the Middle East</note> and occupied Armenia in the year of salvation 764. They were not yet so powerful as to be able to wage war or establish a state against neighboring princes; rather, they kept to the mountains and the depths of the woods and forests, not daring to attack the armies of their neighbors in open field. Instead, they were merely on the lookout to pillage and ransack places they saw were without great defense, etc. See what the same Thevet continues to write in the subsequent chapter 4 regarding these Tartars, and in his following book 11, chapter 1, on the origin and successes of the Turks. 

Gilbert Génébrard <note>original: "G. Genebrard", a 16th-century French scholar</note> in book 4 of his *Chronography* writes: Those who are well-versed in the knowledge of the most ancient languages know well enough that this word "Turks" signifies, in the Hebrew language, "Cursed people," excommunicated, detestable, exiled, driven out, and banished. This word is held among the Muhammadans, Muslims, and Turks of today—as I have already remarked—with great contempt and hatred; indeed, they hold it as an atrocious and execrable insult. This appears likely because their Prophet Muhammad <note>original: "Machumet"</note>, in order not to offend them—and the Tartars who began to stir around the year of salvation 1200—retained in his Quran <note>original: "Alcoran"</note> or *Al-Furqan* <note>original: "Alfurcan", an Arabic term for the Quran meaning "The Criterion"</note> the practice of circumcision, purifications, and ceremonies of the Law of Moses for the reasons we have previously deduced. 

Sigismund von Herberstein <note>original: "Sigismundus Liber"</note> in his *Commentaries on Muscovite Affairs* says: They take it ill to be called Turks and consider it a term of reproach, but they delight in being called *Befermani* <note>original: "Befermani", likely a corruption of "Mussulmans" or the Slavic "Busurman"</note>, and it is by this name that the Turks wish to be called. Johannes Leunclavius <note>original: "I. Leuclauius"</note> in his *Turkish Onomasticon* <note>A dictionary of proper names</note> states: The name Turk—also written as Iurki, Tzurki, or Zurki—signifies the same as Nomads or wandering Shepherds <note>original Latin: "idẽ quod Nomades siue Pastores vagabundi"</note>. The Turks in the beginning lived like the Nomads, and even in Anatolia <note>original: "Natolie"</note> those who drive livestock are called "Turcomans" <note>original: "Turcomanleri"</note> to this day. Indeed, these Turks are currently ignorant of the name "Saracens," by which they were called in previous centuries, although they still boast and vaunt themselves for the present to be children descended from Ha... <note>likely Hagar, referring to the "Hagarenes"</note>

# History of the Origin of the #

...from Hagar, the chambermaid <note>original: "chábriere"</note> of Abraham, and not from Sarah, his legitimate wife; and that from the ancient Saracens <note>A term used by medieval Christians to refer to Arabs and Muslims</note> and the ancient Turks, there has now been formed and composed one and the same people, just as I have fully deduced above according to the opinion of Guillaume Postel <note>A 16th-century French polymath and orientalist</note> in chapter 10 of his *Eastern Histories*. These people do not care to be named or called by any names other than that of **Muslims** <note>original: "Mussulmans"</note>, which signifies in the Arabic and Turkish languages "faithful," "circumcised," or "saved" by the effusion of their blood shed during their circumcision, as has been well noted by F. Ricold <note>Riccoldo da Monte di Croce, a 13th-century Dominican missionary</note>—or Richard, cited above—in chapter 7 of his refutation of the law given to the Saracens by Muhammad, and the great Cardinal of Cusa <note>Nicholas of Cusa, a 15th-century theologian and astronomer</note> following him in book 3, chapter 3 of his *Sifting of the Quran* <note>original: "cribration de l'Alcoran"</note>. And the aforementioned G. Postel in chapter 10 of his said *Eastern Histories*.

This name of *Muslim* was first given, according to the Turkish Annals, to one of the sons of Bayezid <note>Bayezid I, Sultan of the Ottoman Empire from 1389 to 1402</note>, the great lord of Turkey who was defeated and overcome by the great Tamerlane <note>Timur, the Turco-Mongol conqueror</note>. In fact, according to several historians of the last century, this name *Muslim* is none other than that of the younger son of the said Bayezid, brother of Çelebi <note>original: "Cyriscibey"; Çelebi was a title of nobility or "gentleman"</note>, who is called "Calapin" in the common and vulgar histories written about the deeds of the Turks, as verified by Chalkokondyles <note>Laonikos Chalkokondyles, a Byzantine historian</note> in book 4 of his *History of the Turks*. He recounts that Bayezid the Great had the six children named hereafter: Çelebi (or Calapin), surnamed Joshua; Muslim; Musa <note>original: "Moseh"</note>; Muhammad; Joshua the Younger; and Mustafa.

The Latin and Italian authors who have described the history of the Turks mention only four children of this Bayezid—namely Çelebi, Musa, Muhammad, and Mustafa—without including Muslim, nor Joseph, or Joshua the Younger. Most modern writers join these Latin and Italians in this view, as the word *Muslim* is actually the same as Çelebi, whom the common people call Calapin, and whom the Greek historians knew by the name of Joshua.

Sansovino <note>Francesco Sansovino, author of works on the Ottoman Empire</note>, in book 3, part 3, chapter 31 of his *History of Turkey*, recounts that the Mahometan <note>Muslim</note> minister who performs and gives the circumcision of the Turks asks the one placed in his hands to be circumcised if he wants to be a *Muslim*—that is to say, circumcised—and intends to receive the religion and law of Muhammad. When he says yes, the minister makes him promise to keep and observe it well forever, to be an intimate friend to those who observe it, and on the contrary, a mortal enemy to its adversaries. And then the minister sets about performing his duty and office with several other ceremonies required and necessary for this purpose, described very specifically by Giovanni Antonio Menavino <note>An Italian who was enslaved and served in the court of the Sultan</note> in book 2, part 2, chapter 24 of his *History of Turkey*; Hugo Favolius in his *Voyage to Constantinople*; and François de Belleforest in volume 2, book 2, chapter 8 of his *Cosmography*.

Furthermore, these Turks have themselves called, besides this name of *Muslims* mentioned above, by the name and appellation of *Islams* <note>original: "Islames"</note>—that is to say, "unanimous" and "peaceful" among themselves—ordinarily praying to God that the *Giaours* <note>original: "Gaures", a derogatory term used by Muslims for non-believers, especially Christians</note>, meaning the Christians, may be perpetually discordant and enemies among themselves, according to the report of Johannes Leunclavius <note>A prominent German historian of the Ottoman Empire</note> in his *Muslim and Turkish History*.

These discourses having been set forth, they will give us to understand that the Turkish language is similar and like the Tartar language, according to the words of Matthias Miechowita <note>original: "Matthias Michou Polonois", a Polish scholar</note> in his book on *Sarmatia* <note>A historical region in Eastern Europe</note>, inasmuch as the Turks have come and proceeded (as I have already said) from the same place and origin as the said Tartars, all of whom have the same or nearly similar customs, languages, words, and way of life...

-> # Languages of this World # <-

...common among them, as those who have seen and frequented these peoples and nations know very well: for it is quite certain that the **Turkish language** and the **Tatar language** differ from each other only slightly, just as the **Italian language** differs from the **Spanish language**, and the **Polish language** from the **Bohemian** <note>Czech</note>: this is confirmed by **Paolo Giovio** <note>An Italian physician and historian known for his accounts of the Ottoman Empire</note> in the introductory epistle of his *Commentaries on the Deeds and Exploits of the Turks*; by **Guillaume Postel** in chapters 6 and 7 of his *Eastern Histories*; and by **Theodor Bibliander** <note>A Swiss reformer and linguist</note> in his commentary on the common reasoning of all languages and letters, asserting that these common languages—Turkish and Tatar—not only retain a firm analogy in their derivation, composition, and the inflection of words in their structure (much like the **Latin** or **Greek** languages), but also possess their own particular force and eloquence. Furthermore, **Bartholomew Georgevich** <note>original: "Barthelemy Georgieuitz," a Croatian writer who was captured and enslaved by the Ottomans</note>, formerly a slave in Turkey and consequently very learned and knowledgeable in this Turkish language, has written the following regarding the **Scythian** or **Tatar** language, which he calls **Persian**.

<margin>cc cc cc cc cc cc cc cc cc cc cc cc cc</margin>
> *The Turks and Priests together use **Arabic** letters and characters. The **Persian** language is the easiest and simplest of all the other languages in this world; knowledge of it allows the speaker, through its help, to be easily understood without any trouble and to conduct business throughout all the lands and regions of **Turkey, Persia, Greece, Armenia**, and others of the **Levant** inhabited by **Jews, Christians**, and **Muslims** <note>original: "Mahometistes"</note>. Today, the aforementioned Turks use this language, though slightly altered and corrupted, which can be easily verified by the use and understanding of both these languages. The **Slavonic** language <note>The Slavic dialects of the Balkans</note> also holds great credit, reputation, and fashion at the court <note>original: "porte"</note> of the Grand Seigneur <note>The Ottoman Sultan</note>, especially among the neighbors of **Slavonia**; and the aforementioned author, in the place cited above, provides observations on this language.*

**Pierre Belon** <note>A French explorer and naturalist</note> in book 2, chapter 32 of his *Observations of the Levant*: The **Egyptian Moors** or **Arabs** are more superstitious and ceremonial in their religion than the Turks; and although both are of the same law, following **Muhammad** and being subjects of the **Great Turk** who conquered them in battle, the Turks nevertheless esteem a certain holiness in the Arabs more than in themselves. The reason is that the **Quran** <note>original: "Alcoran"</note> was written and composed in **Arabic**, which has since been translated into the **Turkish** language, and also because the most learned Turks do not make a profession of the Turkish language, but rather of the Arabic. Their written characters are the same thing, though the languages themselves are somewhat different. In fact, these Turks have no letters that did not come and proceed from the Arabs. The author of the discourse on the order of the Turkish government, both private and general, has left in writing that in **Anatolia** <note>original: "Natolie"</note> during his time, there were several languages in use: namely **Greek, Italian, Scythian, Armenian, Ajam** <note>original: "Aggiamesque," likely referring to Persian or non-Arab dialects of the Caucasus</note>, **Circassian** <note>original: "Cercasicque"</note>, **Zykhi** <note>original: "Ziffique," an ancient people of the northern Caucasus</note>, **Egnasian**, **Mingrelian**, **Wallachian** <note>Romanian</note>, and **Ruthenian** <note>East Slavic</note>. This same author goes on to say that because the Great Lord of Turkey commands many different nations of diverse and dissimilar languages, it is necessary for him to have various secretaries and interpreters, learned and skilled in these languages, so that he has them write the dispatches he sends to the Greeks and Italians in **Greek** letters and language; and those he...

This is why in the Turkish court this language is more commonly used than others, although everyone may use whatever language pleases them according to their own mind. After Turkish, the language of the Arabs prevails because the Quran was written in that language. Third place is held by the Illyrian, otherwise known as Slavonic, most in use by the Janissaries, which by its abundance is judged to excel all other languages of the world. This is followed by the Greek language used in Constantinople among the citizens, and in Pera <note>Pera: a district of Constantinople, modern-day Beyoğlu</note>, and throughout all of Greece. Besides these, several others are in frequent use in the Turkish court, according to the diversity of Nations subject to the Turkish empire." **André Thevet** <note>original: "A. Theuet"</note>, in chapter 9 of his *Universal Cosmography*, clearly shows that there is a great diversity between the Arabic language and the Turkish language, by providing the translation of the Lord’s Prayer in these languages.

### On the name of Sultan, Soltan, Soldan, or Souldan, and other Turkish names of the great Saracen, Turkish, and other lords.

<image-desc>Decorative woodcut initial 'Q' set within a square frame featuring floral and scrolling foliate patterns.</image-desc>
As for the names of Sultan, Soltan, Soldan, or Souldan, which the ancient Saracens and Turks along with the Arabs formerly used and still use today as names for their Sovereign Princes and great lords, they signify in the Saracen, Turkish, and Moorish languages: King or Sovereign Prince. Thus the Turks of today call their Great Lord "Sultan" when they speak of him familiarly, and as if by affection and friendship; but...

The authority and power of the Sultans of **Egypt** and the **Mamluks** began at the time when King **Saint Louis** was captured at **Damietta**. <note>King Louis IX of France was captured during the Seventh Crusade in 1250, a turning point that led to the Mamluk rise to power.</note> Furthermore, **Mamluks** in the Syrian, African, and Moorish languages signifies servants or soldiers who lived according to the manner of their religion without marriage, in the fashion of the Knights of **Rhodes**. <note>The author compares the Mamluks to the Knights Hospitaller, a Christian military order.</note> And just as there were four **Vizier Pashas** <note>original: "Viſi Baſchas"</note> alongside the Great Turk, so too the Sultan had four **Emir Kabir**, that is to say, Great **Emirs** or **Admirals** under them; in addition to these, there was a Great Constable whom they called **Dawadar Kabir** <note>original: "Derdard Quibir"</note>, named by **Paolo Giovio** as the Great **Diadoro**. They were nearly all **Liveroyas**—as those anciently called **Iberians** and **Circassians** are named by the Turks—now called **Circassians**; and those who were **Colchians**, **Georgians**, and **Albanians**, and other **Jacobite** and **Nestorian** Christians living near the river **Faso**, anciently called the **Phasis**, whom the Tartars captured and brought in troops to sell to the **Emirs** who bought them, raised them, and made them Mamluks. This is confirmed by **Chalcondyle** in the third book of his history of the Turks; **Friar Antoine Geuffroy**, Knight of Malta, in his book on the *Conquest of the Turks*; **Paolo Giovio**, cited above, in his book on the Turks and in books 17 and 18 of his histories; and **Giovanni Maria Angiolello** of Vicenza, who also affirms having read, as did **Paolo Giovio**, what a **Kazasker** <note>original: "Cadileſcher," a chief military judge</note>—that is to say, a supreme pontiff or bishop in the Muhammadan superstition—had written of it, having accompanied the Great Turk **Selim** on the journey he made to ruin the authority and power of **Tuman bay II** <note>original: "Tomumbey"</note>, the last of the Sultans of the said Egypt. All the above has been transcribed and repeated by **André Theuet** in book 8, chapter 12 of his *Universal Cosmography*.

Those who wish to see who the **Beylerbeys** <note>original: "Beglierbeys," provincial governors</note> or Lieutenant Generals of the Provinces subject to the domination of the Great Turk are, should read the aforementioned **André Theuet**, book seven, chapter ten of his aforementioned *Cosmography*, and even better, book nineteen, chapter 2 of the same *Cosmography*.

As for the word **Mulei** or **Muley**, it signifies in the **Arabic**, **Turkish**, and **Moorish** languages, King or Lord; and by this word, the Kings of Africa have in these times carried the title of **Muleys**, just as the Arabs and Saracens from their beginning carried that of **Admiral**, and later that of **Sultan**, which signifies, as has been said, Lord and Prince. Regarding the *Caliphs* <note>original: "Calyphes"</note>, it should be known that among the followers of Muhammad, they were formerly held in such authority and veneration as the Popes are among Christians. They resided in the city of *Babylon* <note>likely referring to Baghdad; original: "Bylonne"</note>, called by the Persians *Baghdad* <note>original: "Boughedot"</note> or *Baldac*, and for this reason were called *Caliphs of Baghdad* throughout the *Orient*. But since the *Mamluks* mentioned above held the *Empire of the Levant* under the power and authority of a *Sultan* <note>original: "Soldan"</note> elected from among them, and having seized *Egypt*, *Arabia*, *Palestine*, and *Assyria*, they deprived the *Caliph* of his temporal patrimony, leaving him simply with authority in spiritual matters. 

This method was followed by the *Great Turk* <note>The Ottoman Sultan</note> when he defeated the *Sultan of Egypt*; and the *Sophy* <note>The Safavid Shah of Persia</note>, having driven the ruler of *Baghdad* from his seat, acted more discourteously than the *Saracens* ever were—except for that great and valiant Prince *Saladin*, who killed the *Caliph of Baghdad* to seize his treasures and invested himself with the possession and lordship of *Babylon*, transferring the seat of these *Caliphs* to the city of *Aleppo*. 

It is true that *Paolo Giovio* <note>original: "Paule Ioue"</note>, in the seventeenth book of his histories, speaks of it differently, saying that the *Caliph* who lived in the time of *Amalric* <note>original: "Almaury"</note>, successor to *Baldwin, King of Jerusalem*, called for help to defend himself against the aforementioned *Amalric* who was making war on him. He called upon a very renowned Captain named *Shirkuh* <note>original: "Sarraco"</note> who was in the service of the *Sultan of Syria*. This *Shirkuh*, having resisted the warring efforts of the said *Amalric*, seized the aforementioned *Caliph*, put him in prison, and occupied his state. From that time on, the *Caliphs* lost their power and Empire, and thereafter concerned themselves only with spiritual things and with confirming the *Sultans*. From this *Shirkuh* came *Saladin*, who in his time waged war for so long against the Christians who had gone on the conquest of the Holy Land. They also have another name for the dignity of Kings, *Hunker* <note>Hünkâr, a title for the Ottoman Sultan</note>. But I have never heard any of the Kings, whether Christian or infidel, called by this name except for Suleiman himself, their King who now holds power; however, I do not know if it signifies "Lord of the Huns." Indeed, it seems to be indicated by a word almost identical to the German *Hunc heer* <note>original: "Hunc heer", meaning "Lord of the Huns" in a pseudo-etymological guess</note>, that is, Lord of the Huns. *Chiaferum* <note>Kafir</note> is a name that signifies a gentile or a pagan. For all Turks are accustomed to calling Christians this, although they also have other words for addressing Christians, such as *Gyaur* or *Kaur*, that is, "Christian," or in the plural *Giaurlar* or *Kaurlar*, meaning "Christians." (The Jews call every man who is not an Israelite *Goi*, as if to say he is of another nation; they call a woman *Goiah*, and in the plural number they say *Goyim* <note>original Hebrew: גויה, though the text discusses plural forms</note>, although Elias <note>referring to the scholar Elia Levita</note> in his work *The Tishbite* <note>original: "Thesbe"</note> says this is not entirely congruent.) But *Chiafer* even without that termination which is attributed to the plural number, designates a multitude of nations; but because the text has *Chiaferum*, it is in the genitive case by the addition of *Vn*, as in *Chiaferum*, that is, "of the gentile" in the genitive, as if they were saying "of the Gentile King" or "of the Gentiles."

*Memleket*, moreover, signifies a kingdom, although they also have various other words to signify a kingdom, such as *-istan*. Because when they make mention of the Kingdoms of Italy or France, or even Spain, they then say *Frankistan*: which signifies the kingdoms of the Italians and Gauls as well as the Spaniards. *Frank* signifies a man of these regions, as in *Frank Gyaur*, that is, an Italian, French, or Spanish Christian. Furthermore, when they wish to name Greece, they change the word, saying *Vrum Elli* <note>Rumeli</note>, that is, Greece, and not *Vrum istan*, that is, "the Greek Kingdom." Sometimes they are also accustomed to saying *Vrum Memleket*, and then they understand the whole empire of the Greeks. Briefly, this word *Memleket* signifies an empire rather than a kingdom among those nations of the Turks and Persians.

This great and learned figure of languages, Guillaume Postel, in his discourse on the universe or *Cosmography* in his twelfth table, has spoken of this word, *Gyaur*, as follows: *Tharsis*, or the land of the Kings of Tharsia, is toward the western region of the Cathayan Tartars, a very wealthy and noble region called *Iogour* <note>The Uyghur region</note>, from which even to this day the Turks call all enemies of their sect, and especially Christians, *Iagour* or *Gyaour* or *Chaour*, because before they departed from *Turkestan*, they held those people as enemies. From there came the Magi to worship Christ, led by their knowledge of the stars and incited by a supernatural star; their name and a race believing in Christ still remains there. See what is written of this Province or kingdom of *Tharsis* by Hayton the Armenian <note>A 13th-century monk and historian</note> in the first book, second chapter of his *History of the Tartars*, and in the fifteenth chapter following, speaking of the Empire of the Saracens. ...and they call their great Lord by a particular title, which they never attribute to any other, namely, *Cumchiera* <note>Likely a corruption of *Hünkâr*, a title for the Ottoman Sultan</note>, which is the same as if they said Caesar, or Great Emperor, as the sovereign of their Empire. J. *Leunclavius* <note>Johannes Leunclavius, a 16th-century German scholar of Ottoman history</note> in his Turkish dictionary says: <note>original Latin: "Hunggiar nomen dignitatis à turcis ita Sultanis ſuis tribuitur, vt Romani Principes appellari ſolebant Imperatores Cæſares, enunciandum ſyllabis duntaxat duabus."</note> "*Hunggiar* is a title of dignity attributed by the Turks to their Sultans, just as Roman Princes used to be called Emperors or Caesars; it is to be pronounced in only two syllables." *Franc-beg* signifies an Italian Prince, or Prince of the Italians. Likewise, the Roman Pope is called by the Turks—according to *History of the Muslims*, book 16—*Rum-beg* <note>original Latin: "Rum-beg Romæ Princeps,aut Romæ Dominus"</note>, the Prince of Rome, or Lord of Rome. Thus, in the same 16th book of the *History of the Muslims*, the Turks call the Roman Pope by this name, whom the Persian ambassadors (sent last year during the life of *Sixtus V* <note>Pope from 1585–1590</note> to solicit aid against the Turks) called *Rum Schach*, or King of Rome. *Rum Schaoh* <note>original: "Rum Schaoh, Romæ Rex"</note>: King of Rome. Thus was the Roman Pope called by the Persians. The same *Leunclavius* notes that the Sultan of the Turks is called *megas Aphendis* <note>original Greek: "megas Aphendis", meaning "Great Lord"</note> (Great Lord) by the Greeks, a title which, following the Italian custom, is translated as nothing other than *The Grand Seignor* <note>Il Grand Signore</note>.

The Tartars of today call the Pope and all Christians *Dezinthis*, which signifies Pagans, and *Chaur* <note>Giaour</note>, that is to say infidels, dogs, and Idolaters, because they honor wood and stones <note>A common Muslim and Mongol criticism of Christian use of icons and crucifixes</note>. This has been the case since they were summoned by Pope *Innocent IV* <note>reigned 1243–1254; he sent famous embassies to the Mongols</note> to receive the Christian Religion. While they were almost inclined to do so, Satan stirred up the Muslims who did not want to lose such a choice morsel; they admonished the Tartars to take up the religion of the *Alcoran* <note>The Quran</note> as the purest, since it taught only the adoration of a single God, while that of the Christians was stuffed with Idols. Furthermore, they argued their own religion was vigorous and permitted everything to a free man while putting arms in his hands, whereas the religion of Jesus Christ was fit only for the effeminate and people who ask for nothing but rest. These proponents of the Quran knew so well how to harangue them that those who had no certain Religion embraced the worse one. Leaving behind that law which is entirely spiritual, they grasped the doctrine of the flesh, apostasy, and abomination around the year of grace 1247.

In the Kingdom of *Narsingue* <note>The Vijayanagara Empire in Southern India</note>, the word *Gurupe* is a title of dignity, as one might say a learned and scholarly Priest; and the word *Deleuay* as well, meaning Captain and General of the army, according to *F. P. du Jarric* <note>Pierre du Jarric, a Jesuit historian</note> in book 2, chapter 21 of his *History of the East Indies*. In the kingdom of *Decan* <note>The Deccan Sultanates of India</note>, the word *Sabaio* <note>Likely referring to the 'Savai' title or the ruler of Goa</note> is a title of dignity, as one might say Captain of the King’s personal guards. The word *Idalcan* <note>Adil Khan</note> is another title of dignity, being the King’s Lieutenant General throughout all his lands, according to *Duarte Barbosa* <note>original: "Edouard Barbosse"</note>, a Portuguese, in his summary of the Indies.

He who is commissioned as *toldan* by the King in the city of *Pegu* <note>The capital of the Toungoo Empire in modern-day Myanmar</note>, the capital of the Kingdom of *Pegu*, has full authority; no one would dare present themselves to him without a gift, as it is the custom of the country not to approach one’s King, Prince, or Lord without acknowledging his power. But near the person of the King is the *Cobraim*, called *mattacqui* by the Cathayans <note>The Chinese</note>, who holds more credit than the *Toldans* and *Haozamants*, because he is the Lieutenant General and acts as Regent throughout the whole country and Kingdom of *Pegu*. After the *Cobraim* and *Toldans* are the *Talcadas*, which is to say Captains—one for the port of *Dogom* <note>Dagon, modern Yangon</note>, a day's journey from *Pegu*, and another for *Martaban*, four days away.

# Languages of this World. #

In the Isle of Taprobane <note>The author uses 'Trapobane,' a name historically associated with Sri Lanka, but notes its identification here with Sumatra</note> or Sumatra, there are two most notable Royal officers who oversee the entire state and administration: the general of the army whom they call *Nacauda-Roua* <note>original: "Nacauda-Roua", likely from the Persian/Malay 'Nakhoda' (captain) and 'Raya' (royal)</note>, meaning Royal Captain; and one named *Chambendure* <note>original: "Chambendure", a corruption of 'Shahbandar', the Persian-origin title for a Harbor Master or Chief of Trade</note>, who is tasked with setting the price for all merchandise brought to the Island. Without his license, no one is so bold as to dare buy or sell, and he collects the tributes and taxes owed to the King. In the Island of Haiti, otherwise known as Hispaniola, there have been Kings named *Huibo*, which signifies "Highness"; others *Tureiguahobui*, which means "King more resplendent than gold"; another was called *Starei*, meaning "flaming"; and another bore the name *Duiheiniquen*, which means "rich river." Modern navigators, speaking of the names of the Kings and Princes of the West Indies, write the following: as languages differ in the West Indies, the Lords of those lands also have various designations. In some places they call them *Queri*, in others *Caciques* <note>A Taino word for a tribal chief or leader</note>, in certain places *Tibà*, and in others *Guaʃirò*. But most commonly, the word *Cacique* is of great breadth, and in several regions the sovereign Prince is so called. Those who, after him, are the most wealthy and powerful and have a good number of vassals and subjects under them are called *Sachò*. Just as these are submitted to the Cacique, they also have under their jurisdiction Lords who possess lands and lordships, whom they call *Cabrà*. These are like knights, or simple Gentlemen distinguished from the common people and more authorized than the vulgar, over whom they command. The lowliest come to the honor of *Cabrà* by bearing themselves valiantly in war; for just as in our lands the King ennobles those who have behaved as men of worth in combat and makes them knights of the accolade, so the Cacique makes *Cabrà* of those who fight fiercely and are wounded in battle while performing some signal act, giving testimony of their valor. From then on, they no longer mingle with the common people but are honored and respected, and their children succeed to the nobility of their fathers and are named *Cabrà*, and are consequently obliged to go to war if the Cacique has need of their service. The greatest Lords are called *Morbi-chatz*. See José de Acosta, book six, chapter 25, of his *History of the Indies*, treating the titles and dignities that existed among the Mexicans.

<margin>F</margin>In China, the *Tutans* <note>A transliteration of 'Dutan', a high-ranking governor</note> are absolute Governors of Provinces, and after them are the *Ponchases* <note>The 'Buzhengshi', or Provincial Treasurer</note>, and under those the *Anchases* <note>The 'Anchashi', or Provincial Surveillance Commissioner</note>. The Constable or master of the Men-at-Arms is called *Aitan*, and his lieutenant *Luitilius*. Some write that there are five orders of dignity in this China: the first being the *Cunixes*, compared to our Princes and Counts, otherwise called *Toans*: as reported by Father Pietro Maffei in the sixth book of his *History of the Indies*.

Persia to Ptolemy, <term>Persis</term> <note>original Greek: περσὶς</note>, a region of Asia once famous for its most powerful Empire, and today it does not seem to have degenerated much from it under the Safavids <note>original: "sub Sophys"</note>. # Of the Persians.

## CHAPTER 47.

->Elam <note>original Hebrew: עילם</note> Elan <note>original Greek: ἠλάν</note> Ailan <note>original Greek: αἰλαν</note>.<-

**AElam**, **Ailam**, or **Elam**—meaning in the Hebrew language "adolescent," "virgin," "hidden," or "an age" <note>These are traditional etymological interpretations of the Hebrew root 'lm</note>—the son of Shem and grandson of Noah (Genesis 10), was the first to give his name to the region of **Persia**. This land is not far from Mesopotamia, and it is where **Susa** is situated, according to the testimony of **Josephus** in Book 1 of the *Antiquities of the Jews*, chapter 6, and **Strabo** in Book 16. From this name, the **Elamites** are called the Jews living in Elam or the region of Persia. Regarding this, the "Bundle of Myrrh" <note>A metaphorical reference to a collection of historical or religious truths, or possibly a reference to a specific text titled *Fasciculus Myrrhae*</note> reports that the Persians—descended from the blood and race of **Japheth** and the **Medes**—entered the region of the Elamites (successors of Elam) and imposed upon them the name of "Persians." This is confirmed by **Benedictus Pererius** <note>A 16th-century Jesuit theologian and scholar</note> in his *Commentaries on the Book of Daniel*, Chapter 9. Indeed, in Daniel chapter 8 and in the Acts of the Apostles, chapter 2, we find this word "Elamites" used to mean the Persians, because the Persians are close neighbors of the Medes. **Xenophon** even mentions the **Elamite** tribe, which he takes to be the Persians. In more ancient times, they were called the **Elymaites** or **Elymeans** in Persia. These were the people living near the River **Eleee** (or **Tiritiri**), who are currently called the **Azamians** <note>Likely a variation of "Ajam," a term used in the Islamic world for non-Arabs, particularly Persians</note>, and their region **Elam**. This word encompasses **Susiana**, what is properly called Persia, and the land of the **Parthians**, as this was formerly the patrimony of the Kings of Persia, according to **Ludovico di Varthema** <note>An Italian traveler known for being one of the first Europeans to enter Mecca</note> in his books of travels. Today, the Persians carry the name of **Azamians**, as do the Parthians.

The most eastern part of Persia includes **Molitene** and **Cabanden**—now **Yazd** <note>original: "Iecxt"</note> and **Lorestan** <note>original: "Iurestan"</note>—all surrounded by mountains and more spacious than any other part of Persia. It is a wondrous thing of nature to see how these mountains form a narrow pass such as that of the **Caspian Gates** or **Thermopylae**, which is also called the **Gates of Susa**. Through this pass, called Lorestan, one enters the country of Persia; the place is so difficult that one cannot pass through except one after another <note>meaning in single file</note>. Josephus, in Book 1, Chapter 6 of his *Antiquities*, writes that Shem, the son of Noah, had five children who possessed Asia from the Euphrates all the way to the Indian Ocean. For Elam left his blood to the Elamites, from whom the Persians are descended. But as for the name "Persian," it is not of such ancient standing; for a time, the Persians were called **Pancheans** after a king of that name, then **Cephenians** <note>original Greek: κηφῆνες</note>, and **Arteans** <note>original Greek: ἀρταῖοι</note>, and finally **Persians**, from **Perseus** <note>original: "Perse"</note>, the son of Jupiter, according to the fables of the Greeks. This is written in **Herodotus**, Book 7 of his *Histories*, which should be consulted along with **Strabo**, Books 15 and 16 of his *Geography*; **Pliny**, Book 6, Chapter 27; **Marco Polo** the Venetian, Book 1 of his travels; **Sir John Mandeville** in his travels; **Josafat Barbaro** in his travels to Persia printed in Venice; and **Messire Ambrogio Contarini**, Ambassador of the Venetians, in his travels to Persia, also printed in—
