In fact, the Turkish language differs only very little from the Tartar language, just as the Italian language differs from the Spanish, or the Polish language from the Bohemian. Theodore Bibliander <note>A Swiss linguist and theologian (1506–1564) who wrote one of the first works on comparative linguistics</note> in his *Commentary on the Common Reason of All Languages and Letters* confirms the above. Marco Polo the Venetian, in Book 1, Chapter 8 of his *History of the Tartars*, reports that in his time the Tartars primarily used four different kinds of writing and languages, without taking account of several other diverse kinds of languages from infinite Provinces and cities of Tartary, of which he makes particular mention in the aforementioned book and others following.

History of the Origin of the [Tartars]

Sebastian Münster, in Book 4 of his *Universal Cosmography*, in the chapter on Lithuania, asserts that in the Duchy of Lithuania, near the city of Vilnius, there live certain Tartars in their own hamlets or villages in the surrounding fields, where they plow and sow just as we do. They bring their grain and goods to sell in the neighboring areas and keep themselves ready and equipped to go to war at the simple command given to them by the Grand Duke of Lithuania. They speak their Tartar language and believe in Muhammad, because they call themselves and maintain they belong to the sect of the Saracens <note>A term used by early modern Europeans to refer to Muslims.</note>. Modern navigators and travelers assert that in the kingdom of Mangi <note>A name used by Marco Polo for Southern China.</note>, under the subjection of the aforementioned Grand Cham of the Tartars, there grows a certain tree named Tal <note>Likely the Talipot palm, whose leaves were historically used as writing material (pothi).</note>, from the leaves of which these Tartars help themselves to write for lack of paper; for in no part of the East Indies, except in Cambay <note>A major trading port in Gujarat, India.</note>, is any paper to be found, and thus this leaf must serve in its place for making their writings, as confirmed by André Thevet in Book 11, Chapter 23 of his *Universal Cosmography*.

The Cozanians <note>The Tartars of the Khanate of Kazan.</note>, people of Asiatic Sarmatia who live today in Tartary, and who were formerly subjects of the Tartar [Khan], are presently Muslims. Although they obey the Muscovite <note>The Grand Duchy of Moscow, or Russia.</note>, they nevertheless speak the Tartar language and use the same and similar way of life as those Tartars, as confirmed by Matthias Michovius in Book 2, Chapter 4. In short, we are assured by the accounts of moderns that the Tartar language of today is understood throughout the North and a large part of the East.

->Of the Grand Cham, Emperor of the Tartars.<-

# CHAPTER 51.

<image-desc>A decorative woodcut initial 'L' featuring floral and leafy scrollwork patterns.</image-desc>

The Tartars of today are for the most part commanded by an Emperor or sovereign King called the Grand Cham or Chan <note>original Hebrew: חן</note>, which signifies as much as *Mahanah* <note>original Hebrew: מחנה</note>, "Camp" or "Tent." <note>The author is attempting to link the Mongol/Turkic title 'Khan' to Hebrew roots meaning camp or favor.</note> Marco Polo the Venetian, in Book 1, Chapter 2 of his travels in Tartary, asserts that in the Tartar language the word *Cham* signifies "Great King of Kings" <note>original Latin: *magnum Regem Regum*</note>, which is to say the same as the words Sultan <note>original Hebrew: שולחן or סולחן</note> or Soltan, meaning Emperor or King, among the Muslims and Turks. For the word *Sultan* in Hebrew and Chaldean sounds like "prefect" or "ruler." <note>original Latin: *nam Soltan Hebraicè, & Chadaicè sonat præfectum.*</note> Some authors hold that the word *Cham* with an aspiration <note>Pronounced with a breathy 'h' sound.</note> signifies "Lord" in the Tartar language, and without aspiration, it signifies "blood."

Sigismund von Herberstein <note>original: "Sigismundus Liber"</note>, in his *Commentaries on Muscovite Affairs*, writes: "Lake Kitai, from which the Great Cham of Cathay—whom the Muscovites call the *Czar Kithaïski*—takes his name; *Cham*, however, means King to the Tartars. The names of dignities among the Tartars are roughly these: *Cham*, as I said above, is King; *Sultan* is the son of the King; *Bij* is a duke; *Murza* is the son of a duke; *Olboud* is a noble or counselor. *Olboadulu* is the son of some noble; *Seid* is the high priest; *Ksi* is a private person. Regarding offices: *Ulan* is the second dignity from the King, for the Kings of the Tartars have four men whose counsel they use most especially in grave matters; of these, the first is called *Schirni*, the second *Barni*, the third *Gargni*, and the fourth *Tziptan*." <note>original Latin: "Lacus Kitai, à quo magnus Chá de Cathaia... ex his primus Schirni vocatur..."</note> Matthias Michovius the Pole, in Book 1, Chapter 8 of *Asiatic Sarmatia*, says: "There are four Hordes of Tartars, and as many Emperors of them, that is to say..." <note>original Latin: "Quatuor sunt Hordæ Tartarorum, totidem Imperatores eorum idem scilicet"</note>

# History of the Origin of the

> ...honored. This man [Sziachmet] was called upon by *Albert, King of Poland*, and by *Alexander*, Grand Duke of *Lithuania*, to provide aid against *Meñli Giray*, Emperor of the *Precopian Tartars* <note>The Crimean Khanate, based at Perekop</note>, in the year of our Lord 1500. He arrived just before winter with sixty thousand warriors; the women and children, however, numbered over one hundred thousand. Because the winter was horrific and the cold intense, his wife—having been secretly summoned by the *Precopian* Emperor—could not endure the cold and hunger and fled to *Perekop* with a large portion of the army, leaving her husband *Sziachmet* <note>Sheikh Ahmed, the last Khan of the Great Horde</note>. Thus, *Sziachmet*, his forces diminished and pressed by the most intense frost, was attacked by *Meñli Giray of Perekop*. His army was scattered in the conflict, and he fled with three hundred horses toward *Bayezid*, the Emperor of the *Turks*. When he reached *Bialigrod*—which means "White Castle" <note>Akkerman, modern Bilhorod-Dnistrovskyi</note>—near the Black Sea, he learned that he was to be captured by order of Emperor *Bayezid*. Therefore, he fled back at a swift pace with fifty horses and escaped into the fields near *Kiev*. The Captain of *Kiev*, however, having been informed of him by scouts, surrounded him with his men, captured him, and sent him to *Vilnius* in *Lithuania*. He escaped from there several times, but was pursued, caught, and brought back. Later, while *Alexander*, King of *Poland* and Grand Duke of *Lithuania*, was holding a general assembly in *Brest of the Ruthenians* <note>Brest-Litovsk</note>, *Sziachmet* arrived from *Vilnius* by his order. He was received magnificently by King *Alexander*, who went out a mile to meet him. Subsequently, it was decreed by the *Poles* that he should be returned to *Tartary* across the Volga via *Radom*, with a few light-armed soldiers escorted to him. To ensure a proper return and a more praiseworthy reception by his people, they sent ahead *Cazac Soltan* <note>Qasim Sultan</note>, the biological brother of *Sziachmet*, who arrived across the Volga and stayed with *Albugerim Czar* <note>Abul Khair Khan</note>, the paternal uncle of *Sziachmet*, in their ancestral land of *Chagatai*. However, as *Sziachmet* was passing through *Lithuania* for the military expedition, he was captured once again by the *Lithuanians* at the suggestion of *Meñli Giray*, the Precopian Emperor, and was thrown into prison in *Kaunas*, which is a castle near the *Baltic* Sea. Indeed, he was called *Sziachmet* by his people, which is to say, "the Martyred One." <note>original: "martyrizatus"</note>

That is as much as there is to say regarding the Emperors of the Zavolhensian Tartars, otherwise called the Chagatai. The other race of Tartars, called Precopians, who are nonetheless descended from the aforementioned Zavolhensians (for they were the source and origin of all the others), had their beginning with a certain *Vlam* <note>likely Haci I Giray</note>, a man of illegitimate and unknown birth. He was the first to seize that point of land called the *Tauric Chersonese* <note>The Crimean Peninsula</note>, which is almost entirely an island stretching into the Maeotian marshes <note>The Sea of Azov</note>, above the Black Sea <note>original: "Mer maiour" (Great Sea)</note>, being some 24 leagues long and fifteen wide. In it are three cities of some note: *Solat*, *Kirkee*, and *Cassan*, along with two castles, *Maucup* and *Azov*. The principal city is *Solat* <note>Staryi Krym</note>, which the Tartars call *Chrim*, from which the Lord of these Precopians takes his name, being called the *Chrimesian* <note>Crimean</note> Emperor. The other, smaller city is *Kirkee* <note>Qirq Yer/Chufut-Kale</note>, where there is a castle made of wood and sod atop a rock. It is said that in ancient times there was a dragon there that devoured everything, so much so that the country was in danger of remaining a desert, if some Italians who had settled there had not had recourse to the Virgin Mary. ...hollow, where they found an image of our Lady, before which a candle burned, and at her feet lay the dragon split through the middle. This was the reason that Acigeri <note>Hacı I Giray, founder of the Crimean Khanate</note>, Lord of Precop <note>Perekop, the gateway to the Crimean Peninsula</note>, being at war with his brothers, commended himself to the blessed Virgin and vowed many fine things to her if she would aid him in this matter. For the Mohammedans <note>Muslims</note> themselves hold her in very high honor and reverence, confessing that without the company of any man, and without any harm to her virginity, she conceived and gave birth to the great Prophet Jesus Christ, as they call him. Having then obtained the help he had requested, he sold the two best horses he had and bought wax, from which he had two candles made that burned continually day and night before the holy image. His successors have maintained this tradition until today. 

The third city is Capha <note>modern Feodosia</note>, formerly called Theodosia, which Mehmed <note>Mehmed II</note>, Emperor of the Turks, took from the Genoese; he put to death two brothers who were Lords of the castle of Maucup <note>Mangup</note>, who were the last remnants of the race of the Goths <note>The Crimean Goths, a Germanic-speaking people who survived in Crimea until the late Middle Ages</note>. He similarly took the castle of Azov at the mouth of the river Tanais <note>the Don River</note>, which he fortified. But the Tartars hold and occupy the plains and countrysides from the entrance of the Island, along the Maeotian Sea <note>Sea of Azov</note> and the Euxine Sea <note>Black Sea</note> as far as Moncastre <note>Akkerman, modern Bilhorod-Dnistrovskyi</note>. This entrance, facing the setting sun, they fortified with a causeway or earthen wall a good league in length—though quite crudely made, for water still passed through it in several places. This is why the Island, which used to be called Taurica <note>The Crimean Peninsula</note>, is now called Prezecop <note>Perekop</note>, which in the Tartar language signifies "ditch" or "trench." 

But leaving that aside, after Vlan <note>Ulan</note>, Tachtamis <note>Tokhtamysh</note> reigned; he accompanied Vytautas, Duke of Lithuania, against Tamerlane <note>Timur</note>, Emperor of the Zauolhiens <note>the Trans-Volga Tartars</note>, even though Tamerlane was his own brother; however, they were defeated by him. His son Sciameth <note>Sheikh Ahmed</note>, who has been mentioned, succeeded him, but was driven out by Acigeri, who reigned in his place. Acigeri left seven children, of whom Hayder, the eldest of all, obtained the lordship. But Mendligeri <note>Meñli I Giray</note>, his brother, retreated to the Turk, who married him <note>allied him by marriage</note> and gave him aid; by this means, he drove out Hayder, Iamurci, and all his other brothers. They went to surrender themselves to Ivan Vasilyevich <note>Ivan III "the Great"</note>, Grand Duke of Muscovy, who received them very willingly and gave them the Duchy of Kazan. 

Mendligeri had nine children: namely, Mahomet Cerei <note>Mehmed I Giray</note>, Achmet, Machmut, Bechy (who drowned in Wallachia in the year 1510), Burnas, Mubarch, Sadech, and two others whose names are unknown. And although the Precopian Tartars, because of the mildness and clemency of the air in the "sixth climate" <note>An ancient geographical system; the sixth climate was considered temperate and conducive to civilization</note> where they live, ought to be more human and gracious than the others, they have not for all that abandoned their ancient cruel and predatory nature, just as if they were wild and ferocious beasts; for not a year passes that they do not miserably overrun and pillage Russia, Lithuania, Wallachia, Poland, and quite often even Muscovy itself. 

The Tartars of the third Horde are called Casanians <note>from the Khanate of Kazan</note>, after the castle of Kazan situated on the Volga River, on the borders and frontiers of Muscovy, where they make their home. They came, as did the others, from the principal Horde of the Zauolhiens or Zagatai <note>Chagatai</note>. These can field twelve thousand fighting men, and in a time of need up to thirty thousand, if they choose to call upon any of their allies for help. These people can muster twelve thousand fighting men, and in a time of need up to thirty thousand, if they wish to call some other of their allies to their aid. ...covite <note>referring to the Grand Prince of Moscow or a high official</note>, who disposes of it as he pleases, and gives them such lords as seem good to him. The fourth Horde, the newest and most recent of all the others, is that of the Occassians <note>the Nogai Horde</note>, or Nahaiens, who also came from the Zavolhense <note>the "Great Horde" located "beyond the Volga"</note>: for after Occass <note>Nogai</note>, a subject of the Great Khan but a very valiant and courageous personage, was put to death, his children—who numbered thirty—departed from those Zavolhians and retreated to the environs of the castle of Sarai <note>the capital of the Golden Horde</note> around the year of grace 1450. And in a short time, they grew and multiplied so greatly that it is now the most populated of all the Hordes. However, they are more Northerly than the others, and the region where they live is much colder, neighboring Muscovy <note>Russia</note> on the side of the Levant <note>the East</note>, which they often enter, and there they commit great evils and ruins, just as the Precopians <note>Crimean Tartars</note> and Zavolhians do in Russia, Poland, and Wallachia. The successors of Occass still rule among them, and they have no use for money, but trade by exchanging slaves, livestock, and horses. These are the four principal Hordes of the Tartars, so feared and dreaded, not only by their neighbors but also by nations far removed from them, at whose name children still tremble at the breast. And in truth, one can call them one of the true plagues and ruins of the human race.

There are still many other branches and offshoots of this vermin, who nevertheless are part of those mentioned above and have set out to handle their own affairs. For they have very large and spacious plains, or rather wildernesses, which extend toward Cathay <note>Northern China</note> and China where the sun rises. Therefore, this people is without number, almost like the sand of the sea or the stars in the sky. And although they are very brutal and far removed from all civility, they still have some order and governance among them, and above all, they bear great honor and obedience to their Emperors, whom they call **Khans**. The other degrees of honor and dignity among them are **Sultan**, who is the son of their Lord; **Bij**, a Duke; **Murfa**, the son of a Duke; **Olboud**, a counselor; **Olbaudulu**, the son of a gentleman; and **Seid**, their sovereign Priest or Pontiff. They hold the Seid in such high regard that even the Emperors, when on foot, salute him and hold out their hand to him, without him having to dismount from his horse for that reason. This they do for no other person whatsoever; for the highest of their subjects, whether Dukes or others, only touch their knees, the gentlemen their feet, and the common people their clothing. There are also four figures, the first of whom is called **Schioni**, the second **Barni**, the third **Gargni**, and the fourth **Tziptzan**, who are accustomed to assist the Emperor in council when it is a question of some matter of importance.

Some modern travelers affirm in their journeys that the King or sovereign Prince who commands today over Turkestan—so named after the Turks, just as they say France or *Freisten* <note>original: "Freisten"; likely a variant of Franconia or "Land of the Franks"</note>, who since then have been called Turkmans, and later *Turquizel* <note>possibly a corruption of a tribal name or "Turcomans"</note>, from whom the said Turks took their name, who at that time had no law or governance—and also who has power over the Province of Zagate <note>the Chagatai Khanate in Central Asia</note>, bears the title of Sultan Chapar <note>possibly Chapar Khan, a descendant of Kaidu</note>. He is the nearest of the Northerners to the Great Emperor of the Tartars; and he is so powerful that when it pleases his lord, he will easily lead a hundred thousand men on horseback, all men of action and valiant in war. The one stretching further toward the Tanais <note>the River Don</note> is called Sultan Hochtay, and he borders Asiatic Sarmatia <note>an ancient term for the lands between the Volga and the Vistula</note>, having command over the Tartars as far as Europe. He can lead more cavalry than the other, though his men are not considered as brave or as abrupt in the conduct of war, even though they possess better horses than all the rest of the Scythians <note>an ancient name often used by early modern writers to describe the Tartars and other nomadic peoples of the Eurasian steppe</note>. Whatever the case may be, these people are furious and redoubtable, with whom it is bad to have dealings—proud, cunning, and calculated in their actions. The Turks feel no dishonor in being descended from such a gallant nation, rather than tracing their origin back to the Trojans—as some historians have falsely tried to do—suggesting they traveled all the way to Scythia. But the Scythians were not so easy to handle that the Trojans could have made an entry there; rather, it is the Scythians who have made raids as far as Asia Minor, and then into Europe as far as Rascia <note>a medieval name for Serbia</note>, Poland, and Lithuania. Likewise, they still hold the Sophy <note>the Shah of Persia, of the Safavid dynasty</note> in check, because the Great Khan <note>the supreme leader of the Tartars</note> tries from one day to the next to take his lands. This is the thing that most hinders the said Sophy from expanding against the Turks, as he must defend himself against such a powerful enemy as the Tartar. 

Now, the source of their quarrel came from the greed of Sheikh Ismail <note>Shah Ismail I, founder of the Safavid dynasty</note>, father of the Sophy, from the year 1543 until 1552 <note>the author’s dates are historically inconsistent, as Ismail died in 1524; he may be conflating Ismail with his successor Tahmasp I</note>. For having heard that Iesilbas <note>likely a reference to the Kizilbash or "Red Heads," the elite Persian soldiers</note>, lord of Samarkand and ally of the Sultan of Chagatai and Turkestan, had entered his lands, he went out to meet him, following the fortune that had always accompanied him. So it was that the Tartar, hearing what the Sophy's forces were, retreated by a day's journey and went to pitch his camp on the River Jarit, now called the Esra, <term>Thevet, book 9, chapter 4, folio 292, Universal Cosmography.</term> Thus leaving Lake Khorasan, the battle given was so furious that the Sophy saw himself in danger of losing his life; his men twice were on the verge of being completely routed, had it not been that, seeing how he exposed himself to hazard, they took such courage that in the end Iesilbas (or Kizilbash) was taken, along with the General of his army named Uzbek, and his children. 

To these leaders, the Persian immediately had their heads cut off; as for the children, after making them swear obedience, he returned to them the lordship of their late father. When the Lord of Chagatai was informed of this, he went to his nephews in Samarkand and pointed out to them the wrong they were doing to the Tartar name and to the greatness of their Khan by having sworn obedience to the Sophy, and that the Great Khan might well resent it. Consequently, this—along with the hatred the Samarkandis held against the Sophian sect <note>the Shia branch of Islam, which the Safavids followed, as opposed to the Sunni Islam of the Tartars</note>—made them take to the field once again, and the aforementioned children of Iesilbas took several cities from the Sophy. The Sophy, irritated by such a revolt, marched against them, but in vain; for after giving a thousand raids and skirmishes to his camp, they retreated toward Turkestan, awaiting new forces from that country and the will of the Great Khan, whom they had informed of the war being waged against them. Thus, at the same time, the Sophy saw himself enveloped in two great wars against the two greatest monarchs in the world: namely the Turk and the Tartar. This was the occasion that made him come to an agreement with the aforementioned children, relinquishing the obedience he claimed over the city and country of Samarkand. Not that the Tartar was appeased by the fact that he had overrun his country; this happened at the time when the Great Turk Selim <note>Sultan Selim I</note> made his expedition into Persia, before attacking the Sultan of Egypt in the year of salvation 1512. In short, although Tartary is the country from which the Turk is descended, they are nevertheless different from one another in several ways...

It is true that the Great Tartar King is a bit more scrupulous, and the lords who surround him more magnificent than those who stay in the Northern parts, who differ in no way from the lowliest of the country in their clothing or preparation of food, seeing as the people are not abundant in the riches of this world. This is also the reason that in the morning you will see a Tartar who will go to gather some herbs or small fruits in the fields for his sustenance, such forage seeming very good to them, and being content with beautiful clear and pure water. Not that they lack the means to nourish themselves better than that, given the abundance of beasts they kill and those they raise in their pastures, such as oxen, cows, horses, mares, rams, and sheep, whose meat they eat while drinking their milk—especially that of mares, which they find the best, most flavorful, and healthiest. Some modern travelers have reported that the Great Khan of Tartary <note>a historical term for the vast region of North and Central Asia</note> is called Tamerlane <note>originally "Tamirlāgue"; the author appears to be conflating the title of the Great Khan with the specific conqueror Timur</note> by his Tartar subjects; the seal which this great Emperor uses in his letters patent is thus, according to the report of Master Marco Polo the Venetian <note>original: "M. Master Marco Polo the Venetian, in book 1, chapter 1 of his travels in Tartary, writes that Kublai <note>original: "Cublai"</note>—or Cobila, as he is called by Hayton <note>Hetoum of Armenia, a medieval chronicler</note>—the fifth Emperor of the Tartars, was the first of the Khans of Tartary to make profession of the Christian religion; having sent his ambassadors to Pope Gregory X to obtain from his holiness some doctors <note>learned teachers/theologians</note> to instruct him and his subjects in Christianity. To this effect, the Pope sent them two preaching brothers of the order of Saint Dominic, doctors of Theology named Nicolas of Vicenza <note>original: "Nicolas de Vicefe"</note> and William of Tripoli, in the year of our salvation 1272. When these men arrived before this Emperor, he received them graciously, but he was not baptized and did not make a public profession of Christianity; for Hayton, in chapter 23, is content to say only that he was a Christian in the respect that he favored the Christians, kept them in his retinue, and used their counsel. This seems to be amply stated by the aforementioned Master Marco Polo in book 2, chapter 2 and following, where he mentions that during a solemn feast, this Emperor summoned all the Christians to him, wishing them to bring the book of the four Evangelists <note>the Gospels</note>, which he had censed with great ceremony, kissed humbly, and commanded his Princes to do the same. He did this at all the great feasts of his Empire, whether Christian, Mohammedan, or Idolatrous <note>Buddhist or Shamanist</note>; and when he was asked the reason why he practiced such inconsistency in religion, he replied that there are four Prophets who are adored, and whom everyone believes in and reveres. Since the Christians confess Jesus Christ to be their God; the Saracens <note>Muslims</note> hold Muhammad as their Holy Envoy; the Jews have Moses; and the Idolaters know Sogomonbar Ca <note>likely a corruption of Shakyamuni, the historical Buddha</note>, who was the first author of Idols among the Tartars. This empire commands more than seven hundred leagues of well-inhabited and populated land, filled with beautiful and excellent buildings, villages, boroughs, castles, towns, and rich, fortified cities, with every abundance of goods, food, and conveniences, along with all kinds of exquisite and excellent artisans. In conclusion, we shall assert that those are greatly mistaken who have believed and continue to believe that the Great Khan of Tartary commands all of the Indies, both on this side and beyond the River Ganges, because his jurisdiction extends to the furthest corners of the Orient, and to the land of Mangi and the islands of the sea as far as Taprobana <note>historically identified as Sri Lanka or sometimes Sumatra</note> which pay him tribute and recognize him. However, they do not consider the vast distance from the North to the southern parts, nor the great separations of land made by both mountains and rivers, seeing as it is certain that on the side of Gujarat <note>original: "Guzerath"</note> and Cambay <note>original: "Camboia"</note>, the lands of the Great Khan are separated from those of the Indian Kings. Thus, according to this consideration, and taking regard of the Caromoram River <note>The Yellow River</note> and the mountains that separate Mangi from China, one can also see that the Indian Kings have their lordships extended that far, and that the Tartar commands in the more northern parts of what we call the East Indies.

...districts, or Cantons of the Tartars of today are as follows: namely, in the Country formerly called Scythia <note>A vast region of central Eurasia inhabited in antiquity by nomadic peoples</note>, the Hordes of the Siberians <note>original: "Zibierairoans"</note>, neighbors of Turkestan; toward the Caspian Sea, the Hordes of the Bashkirs <note>original: "Baschidores"</note> and the Chiefans, who live along Lake Kitana, toward the Northern Sea. Likewise, along the same sea and further still toward the North, are the Hordes of the Vsezucanores and the Cheremissians <note>original: "Ciremissores," an ethnic group of the Volga region</note>. At the farthest corner of the earth, where the Scythian promontory lies, are the Danites, from whom the people of Denmark are descended, though Krantzius <note>Albert Krantz (1448–1517), a German historian</note> is of the opposite opinion, believing the Danes to have come from the Egyptian Dan. It is quite certain, through the reading of good books, that from this cold side of Scythia have overflowed all the nations that for the last twelve or thirteen hundred years have made terrifying raids into Europe and Africa. 

After the Danites, one sees the Horde of the Nephthalites <note>The Hephthalites or "White Huns"</note>, who, according to the report of Agathias <note>A 6th-century Byzantine historian</note> in his fourth book, defeated the King of Persia, Peroz, in the year of grace 476. These are otherwise called Euthalites, who, following the name, are held to be of the race of the Jews and of the tribe of Naphtali <note>One of the twelve tribes of Israel; early modern writers often tried to locate the "Lost Tribes" in Tartary</note>, as I have noted before. After this Horde, which is neighbor to the Scythian Ocean, is that of the Turbores, named after a nearby lake called Turb. Then is that of the Mesctritores, which extends as far as the Kingdom of Tabor and to the deserts of Aspastacht and Carcoran, neighboring the Country of the Saces <note>The Saka, an ancient Iranian nomadic people</note>. All these regions are in the Northern part of Scythia and are thus subject to the cold, and furthermore, the people are inclined toward cruelty. 

According to the Astronomers, this is because the angle of the Northern <term>Aquilon: a classical term for the North Wind or the North</term> where these Scythians and Tartars are placed, is under the influence of the triangle of Northern signs, which are called golden. These are at the command of Saturn, along with the sign called Aquarius, which renders this corner of the earth wild and terrifying in those who inhabit it. This is because Saturn is described—with his weight and coldness—as being angry, troublesome, unpleasant, and inexorable. Also, according to the opinion of Astronomers, this burden-bearing Saturn has a malignant and very dangerous influence; he is a cruel enemy of the human race, whom he always opposes with qualities repugnant to ours: namely, with his coldness and dryness, from which no sweetness or moderation of any kind can result. So Ptolemy wrote in the second book of his *Tetrabiblos* <note>original: "quadripart," referring to Ptolemy's foundational work on astrology</note>, and as I have already noted above. 

And truly, it is a great matter that in these parts of the North—following the saying of the Prophet Jeremiah—there was never anything but iniquity and misfortune spreading across the earth <note>Refers to Jeremiah 1:14: "Out of the north an evil shall break forth upon all the inhabitants of the land"</note>, as Jordanes <note>original: "Iornande," a 6th-century historian of the Goths</note> verifies in his book on Gothic matters. And the more Northern these peoples are, the more horrible and enraged they are in their faces and gaze—as much by nature, which makes them thus hideous, as by their own actions, for they artificially fashion themselves into such fury and deformity. Nevertheless, the thick air that beats upon the most Northern peoples makes them fat, heavy, and pot-bellied, because their humors <note>In ancient medicine, the bodily fluids that determined health and temperament</note> cannot evaporate, the air keeping them inside and thus making them bloated. In fact, just as the Scythians who neighbor the Indies are of quite handsome stature, cheerful, fit, and nimble, one sees also those who belong to the aforementioned Hordes are swollen, heavy, small, flat-nosed, hairy, having short legs and other such imperfections.

...as has been deduced previously. Beyond the Hordes mentioned above, there is that of the **Colmack** <note>The Kalmyks, a nomadic people of Mongol origin</note>, who are among the most Northern; they honor and adore the sun, or else they have a piece of **red cloth** which they hang at the end of a pole, and to this they show reverence, bowing their knees before it and adoring it, praying to it in their times of need. The Tartars who are further away, and who closest approach the Northern Sea, are all either Idolaters or without any knowledge or opinion of any divinity. I say that they have not forgotten their ancient follies, especially in the Country of **Tarsent**—which is the true Tartary beyond **Turkestan**—where the Tartars living there, named **Kirgesses** <note>The Kirghiz people</note>, live like the others in Hordes. Gathering in a great multitude within a wood or an open field where there are trees, the one who performs the office of Priest among them takes blood, milk, and the dung <note>original: "fiens"</note> of their herds and horse-studs <note>original: "haras"</note>, and mixes earth into it within a vessel. Then, climbing a tree, he delivers to them I know not what sermon on their foolish opinions; when it is finished, he scatters this liquid over the people in the manner of **holy water**. The abominable abuse of these Kirgesses is that they take and receive this fine sprinkling as their God, and adore or recognize no other, such that their God is filthy, daily, and dependent on the will of the one who dispenses it.

Furthermore, even though the **Turks** are descended from these Tartars, as we have demonstrated before, they are nonetheless different from one another in several things, namely in that they have different religions. For although the Tartars admit the law of **Mahomet** <note>Muhammad</note>, they mix it with Idolatry; additionally, the Turks are quite civil and friendly to everyone, whereas on the contrary, the Tartars are fierce and wild. Their clothing is also different, even the head ornament: the Turks wearing **Turbans**, and the Tartars pointed caps, around which there is a white band, very well furred, along with the rest of their garments.

In matters of war, there is likewise a great difference, as it is the case that the Turks are good foot soldiers, and the Tartars are not, being unable to do anything if they are not on **horseback**. Besides this, the Turks have retained the use of the **bow**, which was formerly, and is still today, familiar to their brothers the **Scythians**; for of **arquebuses** <note>An early type of long-barreled firearm</note> and pistols, they know not what they are. As for the Prophet Mahomet, the Tartars take him into account for lack of any other religious practice; however, they mock him and his Prophets, just as the black Moors of Africa do for the most part. Moreover, they despise the general resurrection and many other things which are observed and believed both in our Religion and in the Mahometan superstition.

It is quite true that the **Great Khan** <note>original: "grand Chã," the supreme ruler of the Mongol/Tartar empire</note> is a little more scrupulous, and that the Lords who are his neighbors are more magnificent than those who stay in the Northern parts, who differ in nothing from the least of the country in their clothes and preparation of meats, seeing as the People are not abundant in the riches of this world. This is why in the morning you will see a Tartar—I mean even among the greatest—who will go gathering through the fields some herbs or small fruits for his sustenance...

Furthermore, one must know that the dating system of the Tartars <note>The author uses "Tartars" as a general term for the various Mongolic and Turkic peoples of Central Asia</note> follows the number twelve. When twelve years are accomplished, they begin another dozen again, having the twelve signs for a guide, each carrying one year in its power. Thus they say: "this one was born in the year of the Lion," "the other in that of the Dog," or "of the Dragon," continuing thus until the last; when it has expired, they begin again with the first sign.

### Of Africa, the third part of the world.

<image-desc>A large decorative woodcut initial 'A' featuring intricate foliage and scroll patterns within a square frame.</image-desc>

A. Ortelius <note>Abraham Ortelius (1527–1598), a famous Flemish cartographer and geographer</note>, in his geographical synonyms and treasury, writes what follows concerning this third part of the world.

Africa <note>original: "Africa Αφρική"</note>, which is called Libya by the Greeks and Africa by the Latins; in the sacred scriptures <note>The Bible</note> it is called *Chamesia* <note>A reference to the Land of Ham, son of Noah</note>. Josephus calls its people the *Phutos* <note>Phut, another descendant of Ham</note>. It is considered the third part of the world by the ancients. John Leo <note>Leo Africanus (c. 1494–1554), a famous Berber Andalusi diplomat and author of "Description of Africa"</note> writes that it is called *Iphricia* by its inhabitants. Thevet <note>André Thevet (1516–1590), a French Franciscan priest and explorer</note> says it is named *Alkebulam* by the Arabs and Ethiopians, and *Besecath* by the Indians. It is called *Moorenlandt* <note>meaning Land of the Moors</note> by our own countrymen. In place of *Africa*, Serapio reads *Lyonoi* and *Linoa*, as well as *Lintouin* in Dioscorides.

There is also *Africa proper* <note>original: "Africa propria"</note>, according to Ptolemy <note>Claudius Ptolemy, the 2nd-century Greco-Egyptian geographer</note>, which is the part of Africa on the Mediterranean Sea between the regions of Mauritania and Cyrene. It is called *Zeugitana* by Pliny, who divides the same into the old and the new, as does Dio. It is *Naphthuhim* to the Hebrews, according to the witness of Arias Montanus <note>Benito Arias Montano (1527–1598), a Spanish orientalist and editor of the Antwerp Polyglot Bible</note>. Today the Kingdom of Tunis is in this location. See *Carthage, Libya, and Zeugitana*.

Libya <note>original: "Libya λιϐύη"</note>, a region which Stephanus <note>Stephanus of Byzantium, a 6th-century author of a geographical dictionary</note> writes is also called Olympia <note>original: "ὀλυμπία"</note>, Oceania <note>original: "ὠκεανία"</note>, Eschatia <note>original: "ἐσχατία"</note>, Cotyphe <note>original: "κορυφή"</note>, Hesperia <note>original: "ἐσπερία"</note>, Ortygia <note>original: "ὀρτυγία"</note>, Ammonis <note>original: "ἀμμωνίς"</note>, Ethiopia <note>original: "αἰθιοπία"</note>, Cyrene <note>original: "κυρήνη"</note>, Ophiusa <note>original: "ὀφίεσα"</note>, Cephenia <note>original: "κηφηνία"</note>, and Aeria <note>original: "ἀερία"</note>. To the Hebrews, Libya is *Ludim*, according to the testimony of Arias Montanus. In ancient inscriptions, Libya is more often read with a "y" in the first syllable. In the time of Procopius <note>a 6th-century Byzantine historian</note>, that part of Africa which is from Alexandria to the city of Cyrene was called Libya, as he himself testifies in the sixth book of *On Buildings*. In this tract there is also a Libya according to Ptolemy, which he designates as "proper" at the beginning of the fourth book of his *Geography*, where he numbers it among the eleven regions of Africa; however, in the description of the same, he calls it the *Nomos* <note>district</note> of Libya. In the eighth book, he indeed names it and makes only seven regions of Africa, little...

# Languages of this World

...remaining consistent with himself, Gerard Mercator <note>A famous 16th-century Flemish cartographer and cosmographer</note> identifies this same region as "Outer Libya," though I must admit that his reasoning is not entirely clear to me. Libya, according to Antonius, is also a city in Spain near Calagurris.

The part of Africa specifically called "Africa Propria" <note>original Latin: *Africa que dicitur Propria*; refers to the Roman province in modern-day Tunisia</note> is named Zeugitana, on the authority of Pliny, while Aethicus calls it Zeugin. Marius Niger believes that from this part of Africa emigrated that wandering race of men who, in the manner of **Nomads**, roam through our Europe region by region. These people are called *Zingani* and *Zingari* by the Italians, *Ziegeiner* by the High Germans, and *Egyptenaren* or *Heylieden* (as if to say "heathens" and "Egyptians") by the Low Germans. We call them **Egyptians** <note>The root of the English word "Gypsy"</note> because they claim to be exiles from "Lesser Egypt." (Where on earth that might be, I confess I do not know; while Egypt is known to everyone, I have never heard any reliable author distinguish between a "Greater" and a "Lesser" Egypt). The French call them *Baumiens* <note>Bohemians</note>, according to Pierre Belon. Pope Pius II says they emerged from the region of Zogoria, located near the Caucasus. Aventinus leads them to us from the borders of Turkey and Hungary. Philippus Bergomas says they come from Chaldea <note>An ancient region in Mesopotamia</note>.

Rhodiginus considers them to be *Maurusios* <note>Moors or North Africans</note> expelled by the Saracens. Belon says they originate from Bulgaria and Wallachia (where the word *Sicynni* was once used, a term not unlike *Ziegeiner*). He adds that he encountered this same race on the road from Cairo to Macarea, and also in various places along the banks of the Nile, though even there they are considered foreigners. André Thevet says they are called *Rasolheramy* <note>original: *Rasolheramy*, likely from Arabic *ras al-harami*</note> by the Arabs and Moors, which means **"Thieves."** The same Belon records that this class of women has a house near Constantinople, in the city of Pera, divided into many small rooms; there they prostitute themselves to both Christians and Muslims, saying they are permitted to do so by a privilege from the Turkish Emperor. Leo Africanus also mentions that these *Zinganos* live in certain places in Africa, such as in Agades and on the borders of the kingdom of Nubia. It is established from historians that this nation first became known to our Europeans around the year 1417. They are a race of men living in extreme poverty under the open sky, filthy, sunburnt, and dressed everywhere in exotic fashions. They profess to be Christians, but they seek their living through theft and **divination** (for they all wish to be seen as *chiromancers* <note>palm readers</note>), with which they deceive simple women and children. They have a leader chosen from their own dregs, whom they obey. Among themselves, they use a specific and peculiar language that no one else understands, though Aventinus asserts he has confirmed through experience that it is a Slavic <note>original: *Venedicam*, referring to the Wends or West Slavs</note> tongue.

Regarding these *Baumiens* <note>Bohemians/Romani</note>, one may see what I have written above in the chapter on the Canaanite language.

Africa, one of the most notable parts of the world, is called *Africa* in Latin, from the Greek word *Aphrike* <note>Greek: Αφρική</note>, otherwise called Libya, and in the Holy Scriptures *Chamesia* <note>The Land of Ham, son of Noah</note>. Josephus, in Book 1, Chapter 15 of the *Antiquities of the Jews*, calls the Africans *Phutos*, and reports that Africa was so named after **Afer** or **Efer**, son of the Patriarch Abraham and Keturah; this Afer had previously settled in Libya. Some others believe it is named *Aphrike* in Greek (*Africa* in Latin) as if one were saying "without cold," because it receives no cold weather—given that the *a* <note>the Greek alpha-privative</note> acts as a negative and *phrike* <note>Greek: φρική</note> signifies a "chill" or "shivering." For this reason, it is surnamed in Hebrew *Lehabim* <note>Hebrew: להבים</note>, meaning **"enflamed"** or **"burning."** Leo Africanus, in Book 1 of his description of Africa, assures us that this part of the earth...

...is called Iphrichria from the Arabic word *Faraca* <note>original: "Faraca", likely referring to the Arabic root *f-r-q* (farraqa), meaning to divide or separate</note>, which signifies as much in the language of the Arabs as it does in our common tongue: "divided" or "parted." There are two reasons for this name. The first is because the Mediterranean Sea divides it from Europe, and the Nile divides it from Asia. The second is that King Iphric, having been defeated in battle by the Assyrians and driven from his kingdom, fled to this country; having crossed the Nile, he did not stop until he reached the region where the city of Carthage is situated. This is the reason why the Arabs call nothing "Africa" except for that which is Western <note>Refers to the Maghreb region of North Africa</note>. There is no small dispute among African historians to know truly who first populated this third part of the world. Some say they were Palestinians; others say they are descended from the Sabaeans <note>An ancient people of South Arabia, modern-day Yemen</note> and certain other peoples of Asia. The Arabs, Adamians, and Ethiopians give it the name <term>DalKebulam</term> <note>Possibly a corruption of an Arabic or Ethiopic phrase meaning "The South" or "Land of the South"</note>, while the Indians and Javanese call it <term>Behecath</term>, according to André Thevet in his *Universal Cosmography*. As for Africa proper, which extends along the Mediterranean Sea between Mauritania and the region of Cyrene—which Pomponius Mela calls "Lesser Africa," Pliny calls "Zeugitana," and the Hebrews call <term>Naphthuhim</term> <note>A name from the Table of Nations in Genesis 10:13, historically associated with the people of Egypt or Libya</note>, according to the report of Benito Arias Montano—it is bounded differently according to Leo Africanus in his *Description of Africa*, Duarte Barbosa in his *Navigations*, André Thevet in the preface of his *Cosmography* (Book 5, Chapter 12; and Book 6, Chapter 1), and Abraham Ortelius in Table 4 of his *Great Theater of the Universe* and in his *Geographical Synonyms*.

## On the Origin of the Africans.

<image-desc>Decorative woodcut floral initial letter I.</image-desc>Josephus, the Hebrew author, in Book 1, Chapter 13 of the *Antiquities of the Jews*, holds along with the Holy Scriptures that the Africans took their source and origin from the Hebrew Patriarch Abraham, saying these words:
> After the death of Sarah, Abraham took Keturah in a second marriage, by whom he had six sons, all wise and industrious men: namely Zimran, Jokshan, Medan, Ishbak, and Shuah <note>The original text uses variant spellings: Zembrané, Iazaré, Madané, Lufubac, and Sua</note>. Each of these also had children: for Shuah had Sheba and Dedan, Epher (or Apher), Hanok, Abida, and Eldaad. Abraham sent them all to inhabit other regions; they occupied Troglodytica <note>An ancient term for the coast of the Red Sea</note> and all of Arabia Felix, which lies along the Red Sea. It is also said that Epher (or Apher) departed with great troops and took possession of Libya, which the children of his successors have possessed since then, and who named it Africa after the name of their ancestor.

This is why Leo Africanus, speaking of the source of those of his nation, says that their historians are in little agreement on this origin. Some hold that they are descended from the Palestinians, who, having been driven out long ago by the Assyrians, fled to Africa; finding it good and fertile, they settled there. Others are of the opinion that they are descended from the Sabaeans, a people of Arabia Felix, before the Assyrians or Ethiopians ever drove them from that country—and this reasoning agrees with the aforementioned advice of Josephus. But the third opinion is that the Africans are said to be descended from certain peoples of Asia who, being at war with their enemies, came to find safety in Greece, which at that time was but sparsely inhabited; but being pursued further...

by their enemies they were forced to cross the Sea of the Morea <note>The Peloponnese peninsula in Greece</note> and came to make themselves lords of Africa, while their adversaries remained in Greece. But he says that this is to be understood regarding the Africans who are white, namely those who reside in Barbary and Numidia <note>Modern-day Maghreb and northern Algeria</note>, especially since he seems to intend by this to support the voyage of the Tyrians under Dido when she came to found the city of Carthage. However, the land of the Negroes <note>original: "Negres"</note> was already populated, given that King Iarbas the Getulian—who ruled the country of the Negroes or Nigritians <note>Historical term for the peoples of the Sahel/Sub-Saharan region</note>—threatened to ruin Dido if she did not fulfill his suit, which was to marry her, according to the words of Virgil in his *Aeneid*. And thus he concludes that the Negroes or Nigritians are all descended from the lineage of Cush, son of Ham the accursed, and the eldest of the children of the great Noah. Even with this consideration, the Nigritians would still be of the blood of the whites, insofar as Mizraim <note>A biblical figure often identified as the ancestor of the Egyptians</note>, from whom the Palestinians and Egyptians emerged, was a close relative of Cush, as the aforementioned Josephus <note>Flavius Josephus, a 1st-century Romano-Jewish historian</note> maintains in the first book, sixth chapter of the aforementioned *Antiquities*. This leads to a conclusion that is more than necessary: that in any case, the Africans are descended from the race of Ham, and all the Negroes, both of Ethiopia and other lands in Barbary down to the Cape of Good Hope, have no other source than Cush, as almost all authors are in common agreement.

Thus one can see how Africa is divided into White Moors and Black Moors <note>16th-century ethnic classifications based on geography and skin tone</note>; some are esteemed to descend from Ophré or Apher <note>Associated with the name "Africa" in some early traditions</note>, and from the Palestinians and Sabaeans, and the others from Cush, father of the Ethiopians, who have never had difficulty calling themselves Cushites after the name of the first of their race and family. But these peoples are further divided into their respective groups, insofar as the whites are further divided among themselves into five peoples: those of the Sanhagia, Musmuda, Zeneta, Haoara, and Gumera. The Masmuda are those who stay at Mount Atlas in the western part, from Hea as far as the Servi River; they also reside in the valleys near the aforementioned mountain on the side that faces the south. These people hold four provinces: Hea, Sus, Guzula, and Morocco. The Gumera also inhabit the mountains of Mauritania—specifically on the side where the Atlas faces our Mediterranean—and stay along the river called the Rif, which is near the Pillars of Hercules <note>The Strait of Gibraltar</note> and waters the entire kingdom of Tlemcen, which is that part of Mauritania the Latins called Caesarea. These five peoples have always been at war with one another; those who were the strongest also made themselves masters of the open country, and by forcing the defeated to serve them, they also forced them to stay in the cities. The greatest and most victorious built their houses in the fields, just as the nobility does in France and other provinces of Europe. Some of these—namely the five white peoples of Africa—spread throughout the African countryside. Such were the Zenetes when they drove out the true lords of the family of Idris <note>original: "Iddris," referring to the Idrisid dynasty</note>, from whom the Kings of Fez had taken their origin. Likewise, the Zenetes were later driven out by certain Numidians called the Zanhagi, who ruined the entire country of Tlemcen and Temesna, putting everything to the sword except those who were of their own language and family, and who remained in Ducala.

### *On the African Language.*

<image-desc>Decorative woodcut initial letter 'I' with scrollwork patterns.</image-desc>
It seems to be very necessary, before speaking of the African language, to discourse a little more on the Africans themselves. Thus we shall learn that the Romans anciently made themselves lords of Africa, and after them the Vandals, Northern peoples immediately occupying the lands that the former had conquered therein, as is amply deduced by Diodorus Siculus in book 17 of his *Library*; Dionysius of Halicarnassus in book 7; Titus Livius <note>Livy</note> in the *Punic Wars*; Plutarch in the *Life of Hannibal*; Appian in his *Libyan History*; Jordanes in his *History of the Goths*; Paul the Deacon in his *Roman History*, book 4; Victor of Vita in his *History of the African Persecution*; Egnatius in book 2 of the *Lives of the Emperors*; and Procopius in books 1 and 2 of the *Vandalic War*. After which peoples, this same Africa came into the hands and subjection of the Greek Emperors <note>The Byzantine Empire</note> in the year of salvation 534, in the time of our Emperor Justinian, as the same Procopius confirms in books 1 and 2 of the *Vandalic War*; although the Saracens, Moors, or Maurusians <note>A classical name for the Moors</note> made frequent raids into it, as Paul the Deacon reports in book 16 of the *Roman History*, and did not let the agents of the Empire enjoy it peacefully. For in the year of salvation 638, according to the *Annals of Constantinople*, book 19, during the reign of Constans <note>Constans II</note>, grandson of Heraclius and son of Constantine, these Saracens, otherwise named Arabs, entered into this Africa. They defeated a certain Gregory <note>Gregory the Exarch, who had declared himself Emperor of Africa</note> who wished to occupy it under the authority of the Empire, drove him out, and made the Africans tributary, who, along with the aforementioned Gregory, had revolted against the Emperor. This occurred when Martin I sat at Rome <note>as Pope</note> and Clovis II, otherwise called Louis I of that name and son of Dagobert, reigned in France. And although these Barbarian Muhammadans did not establish their lordship in this Africa from that moment, they nevertheless settled there so well that it has since been impossible to drive them out. For those who made this raid were not those who had conquered Egypt, but rather a group led by Othman <note>original: "Odmen"</note>, their self-styled Caliph, under whose authority passed an Arab captain named Uqba ibn Nafi <note>original: "Huba Ibnu Nafich"</note> into Africa with a troop of eighty thousand combatants. Having built castles and fortresses there, and the city of Kairouan <note>original: "Cairaohan"</note> in the ancient region of Cyrenaica, he so attracted the inhabitants by gentleness that he made them embra- [embrace]... <note>catchword: "ſer la" / "embrace the (faith/law)"</note>

Ten lineages of Arabs, under these conditions, passed from both Arabia Deserta and Arabia Felix <note>Classical geographical terms for the northern/central desert and the fertile southern region (Yemen) of the Arabian Peninsula</note>, numbering fifty thousand combatants along with an infinite number of women, children, and livestock they brought with them. They made great conquests in Barbary, ruining several cities from top to bottom, among others the city of Kairouan. We must learn in this place that the Arabs who came to inhabit Africa were divided into three types of people: the first named Zughba <note>original: "Chachni"</note>, the second Hilal <note>original: "Hilel"</note>, and the third Maqil <note>original: "Mahchil"</note>. ...the reign of John the First <note>John I of Portugal, reigned 1385–1433</note>, there were found in the very city of Morocco certain ancient families called **FARFANES**, still holding the name and profession of Christians more than 680 years after those Arabs or Saracens had seized Africa. Some of these came to Spain, to Alcalá de Henares, as recorded in the *Histories of Spain*, Book 15, Chapter 27. Furthermore, it has been seen in recent days, after the city of Tunis was taken by the Emperor Charles the Fifth from the pirate Hayreddin Barbarossa <note>A famous privateer and Ottoman admiral</note>, that there were many Christian dwellings within it. These people had retained and inherited from father to son, for a space of over 800 years, the articles of our faith—not without great admiration for divine providence. They lived in a village outside the city of Tunis, at the South Gate, and were highly esteemed by their Kings as valiant and bold in war. They had a Temple <note>Church</note> separate from those of the Moors, who called them **Rabatins**. From these men were composed the bodyguards of the Moorish Kings; these Rabatins were later transported to Naples by the said Emperor Charles the Fifth in order to be fully instructed in the Catholic, Apostolic, and Roman religion, as I have already remarked previously when speaking of the Saracens. André Thevet, in Book 1, Chapter 6 of his *Universal Cosmography*, writes on this subject that about sixteen leagues from the city of Morocco in Africa, toward the rising sun <note>the East</note>, there are very beautiful and fertile mountains. In these mountains resides a certain Moorish people who bear, from father to son, a cross on the right cheek. He could not learn the reason for this except from three slaves, who told and assured him that it was in memory of their ancestors, who were formerly Christians. He also noted that in the houses of these Moors were a great number of books, such as Bibles and New Testaments, and some Roman histories written by hand. This had been noted before Thevet by Joannes Leo <note>Leo Africanus, a famous 16th-century diplomat and author</note> in his *History of Africa*, as I touched upon above. With him, we shall remember to relate in this place all that we discussed in the preceding chapter concerning the Punic and Carthaginian language, and the Latin characters and letters which the Africans used for several centuries after they were brought under the rule and Empire of the Romans.

All that we have discussed above being presupposed, we shall report that concerning the generality of the Africans of today—divided into so many lineages and families, and spread over such long distances of country in Africa and through such diverse regions—they all speak the same language which they call **Aquel Amarig**. This is a noble and illustrious language, called the "Barbary language" <term>Barbareſque: the language of the Berbers</term> by the Arabs of Africa. It is the native and natural African tongue, a word derived from the verb *Barbara*, which means as much as "to murmur." This is because the said language of the native Africans is, to the Arabs, like the voices of brute beasts, inasmuch as they seem to form no accent in speaking, but only a certain clattering cry that represents I know not what unpleasant murmur. This language is entirely different from other languages, although it has several words in common with the language of the Arabs, even in its most ancient parts, so that one cannot say it was corrupted by the arrival of the Arabs in Africa; and this provides a greater argument...

### Languages of this Universe.

...many Moorish and Black peoples and nations, each of whom use several and diverse languages, all different and dissimilar, not understood by others except by those who speak them as their mother tongue. This is confirmed by all modern travelers and navigators.

**Leo Africanus** <note>Joannes Leo Africanus (c. 1494–1554), a renowned diplomat and author of "A Geographical History of Africa"</note>, cited above in the first book of the description of Africa, writes that the greater part of the Arabs who are in **Numidia** <note>an ancient region in North Africa, covering parts of modern-day Algeria and Tunisia</note> are rhymers who compose beautiful songs, in which they describe their battles along with the manner of hunting, and the passions of love with such great grace and eloquence that it is a marvel. They make their compositions in verse and meter in the style of the common people of Italy, such as **Stanzas** and **Sonnets**. This same author, following what was said above, states that the Arabs hold poetry in high regard and admire it greatly. Devoting themselves to it, they compose **verses** <note>original: "Carmes"</note> most often enriched with perfect elegance, although their language is corrupted in many places. Even a poet of little renown among them is very welcome before their Lords, who, for the pleasure they receive from their verses, reward them generously; assuring you that it would be impossible for me to express the great grace they possess in their verses. These Arabs are those who currently live toward **Tunis** and **Tlemcen** <note>original: "Teleusin," a major center of Islamic culture in modern Algeria</note>, who are in the pay of the Kings of these lands, and who go in summer to the frontiers of these lands to receive in the month of October from the treasurers of these Kings the pension given to them. After receiving it, they withdraw to their deserts to spend the winter there according to their ordinary custom.

A certain African, **Abdul Malik** <note>original: "Habdul Malich"</note>, a chronicler from the city of **Marrakech** <note>original: "Maroc"</note> in Africa, has composed histories in his language divided into seven parts.

Beyond what we have reported above regarding the common poets among the Arabs, there are also some among the Africans, and principally in the city of **Fez** in Africa, who compose verses on various subjects, and above all on love. They express the passions they suffer for the things they love, for their affections extend without shame to all sexes—as almost all **Muslims** <note>original: "Mahometistes"</note> are touched by this vice <note>The author here reflects 16th-century European prejudices regarding North African social mores</note>—every year on the day of the birth of their false Prophet **Muhammad** <note>original: "Mahometh"</note>. On this day, these Poets assemble in the morning in the great square, where the Magistrates and the leading citizens of their cities attend. To these people, the poets recite their compositions made in praise of the said Muhammad. Whoever is judged to have done the best is praised and gifted by the judgment and sentence of the magistrates. In times past, the Kings had this trial performed in their palace and gave to those who did best one hundred **ducats** <note>a gold coin used throughout Europe and the Mediterranean</note>, a horse, a slave, and one of the most beautiful robes from his wardrobe; each of the others received fifty ducats to encourage them to do well. But the Kings have forgotten this courtesy, though the Lords of the city of Fez still continue it.

that this country was first populated by the Arabs who came from **Arabia Felix** <note>original: "l’Arabie heureuſe"; an ancient term for the fertile southern region of the Arabian Peninsula, modern-day Yemen and Oman</note>: but these people at present use the Arabic language more than their own native tongue, due to their constant interaction and frequent dealing with the Arabs. The inhabitants of Borno and Gaoga have their own particular language, as do those of **Nubia**, the latter having elements of Arabic, Chaldean, and Egyptian. In the present day, all the peoples of Africa along the Mediterranean Sea speak the Arabic tongue, albeit a corrupted version, except for the inhabitants of **Morocco**, **Fez**, **Sous** <note>original: "Su"</note>, **Tlemcen**, **Tunis**, and **Algiers**, who use the ancient **Berber** <note>original: "Barbareſque"</note> or African language, otherwise called Syrian or Moorish. This is because the Arabs frequent these regions very little; it is true, however, that some among them nevertheless use the Spanish language, because the Spaniards are ordinarily among them, as reported by: **Leo Africanus** <note>a diplomat and author born in Granada</note>, a member of that nation, in book 1 of his description of Africa; **Duarte Barbosa** <note>original: "Odoard Barboſſe"</note>, a Portuguese, in his voyages and navigations; **Paolo Giovio** <note>original: "Paule Ioue"</note> in his *Summary of Muscovite Affairs*, chapter 5; **Guillaume Postel** in his treatise on the *Alphabets of the Twelve Languages*, and in his work on Phoenician letters, as well as in the preface to his Arabic grammar; **André Thevet** in book 1, chapter 4, and book 5, the last chapter, book 18, chapter 3, and book 20, chapter 1 of his *Universal Cosmography*; **Abraham Ortelius** on table 41 of his *Great Theater of the World*; **Louis Le Roy** in books 2 and 8 of *The Vicissitude of Things*; and **François de Belleforest** in book 3, chapter 32 of volume 2 of his *Cosmography*, and book 6, chapters 3 and 4 of the same volume.

Those who have seen and visited Africa far and wide over the last two or three hundred years have asserted that there are one hundred and ninety-seven Kingdoms within it, not including several great and fearsome deserts, some of which span more than a hundred leagues. Thirty-two of these Kingdoms are **Muslim** <note>original: "Mahometiſtes"</note>; the others are Christian, who are subject to the great <term>Prester John</term> <note>original: "Preſtegiani"; a legendary Christian patriarch and king of Ethiopia</note>, Emperor to the King of the Ethiopians. Others are heretics partaking in Judaism and Christianity, such as the kingdom of Nubia. Still others are half-idolatrous and partly steeped in the errors of Muhammad, and some are entirely steeped in the abomination of Idols. There are also others who recognize neither God, nor Religion, nor Law, such as those of the **Cape of Good Hope**.

And so as not to omit anything that serves the decoration of this present discourse, we shall say that **Alvise Cadamosto** in his voyages and navigations, and **Andrea Corsali** in his voyage to the Indies, have asserted that there are, in the lands of the said Africa stretching toward the Cape of Good Hope,

I have occasionally found myself in places where such a "figure" was being constructed, which took from morning until evening to complete, even during the longest days of the year, and it was traced in this manner:

They draw several circles one inside the other. In the first, they form a cross, and at its extremities, the four parts of the world—namely, the East, West, North, and South. At the summit, they place the two poles, and outside the first circle, the four elements are situated. Then they divide the circle into four parts, and finally the following: after that, they divide each part into seven, where they imprint certain large Arabic characters, which number twenty-seven or twenty-eight <note>The number of letters in the Arabic alphabet, depending on whether the glottal stop 'Hamza' is counted separately.</note> for each element. 

In the next circle, they place the seven planets; in the one following, the twelve signs of the <term>Zodiac</term>; and in another, the twelve months of the year, according to the Latins <note>The Julian or Gregorian calendar used in Europe, as opposed to the Islamic lunar calendar.</note>. In yet another, the twenty-eight <term>Lunar Mansions</term> <note>The divisions of the sky through which the Moon passes in its monthly cycle.</note> or seats of the Moon; in the last, the three hundred and sixty-five days of the year; and outside of all this, they place the four principal winds. 

Then, they choose a letter from the question being asked and proceed by multiplying it with all the things numbered until they know what number the character bears. After that, they divide it in a certain manner, putting it into parts according to what the character is and where the element is situated: so that after the multiplication, division, and measurement, they know which character is appropriate for the remaining number. They treat the character found in the same way as the first, and so on consecutively until they find twenty-eight characters, from which they form a word, and they reduce that word into a prayer—always in metered verse according to the primary type of Arabic verse called *at-tawīl* <note>original: "Ethauel"; the "long" meter, the most common meter in classical Arabic poetry.</note>, which consists of eight feet and twelve beats according to the poetic art of the Arabs, which we have treated in the last part of our Arabic grammar. 

Therefore, from these verses, which come from the characters, emerges a true and infallible response. First, the thing asked for proceeds from it, then the response to what is requested, and it never fails in this. It is certainly a miraculous thing, and all the more admirable because I do not think I have ever seen anything considered natural to possess so much divinity, nor anything that seemed more supernatural than this. 

I have also seen another figure made at the College of King Abu Inan <note>original: "Abul henō"; referring to the Bou Inania Madrasa in Fez, built by the Marinid Sultan Abu Inan Faris.</note> in the city of Fez in an open place, which was paved with fine, white, polished marble. There was a distance between each angle of fifty cubits, of which two-thirds were taken up by the things from which the figure was to be made. To supply it, there were three men, each of whom kept watch over his own side; nevertheless, they remained there for an entire day. 

I similarly saw another made in Tunis by an excellent master, who had begun a work on the aforementioned rule in two volumes; those who have understanding of it are held in great reputation. Since I gained knowledge of it, I have been in places where three such figures were made, and I have also seen two commentaries on this rule, and another by al-Marjani, who was the father of the master I saw in Tunis, along with another by Ibn Khaldun <note>original: "Ibnu Caldun"; the famous 14th-century historian and philosopher who discussed the Zairja in his work, the "Muqaddimah."</note> the historian. And if anyone had a desire to see this rule put into practice, they would not need to spend fifty ducats because, by passing through Tunis, which is close to Italy, they could obtain it.

# Languages of this Universe.
## Of the Region of the Ethiopians.

**Abraham Ortelius** in his *Synonyms and Geographical Treasury* <note>original: "Synonimes & Thresor Geograph." — A major 16th-century geographical dictionary.</note> includes **Ethiopia** <note>original Latin: "Aethiopia"; Greek: "Αιθιοπια"</note>. According to him, there are two regions of this name: **Ptolemy** in his work on **Africa** names one located below **Egypt** and another which he calls "Interior" Ethiopia. The latter is perhaps what is today called **Zanzibar**; the former is now inhabited by the **Abyssinians** and is called *Abexim* by **Garcia da Orta** <note>original: "Garcia ab Horto" — a Portuguese Renaissance physician and pioneer of tropical medicine.</note>, who also uses the name *Hhabas*. With the addition of the Arabic article, it is called *Alhabas* by **Benjamin** <note>Benjamin of Tudela, a 12th-century Jewish traveler.</note>, with the names differing only in their vowel sounds. 

**Pliny** writes that all of Ethiopia was once named *Aetheria* and *Atalantia*. These Ethiopians are called *Chusæi* <note>Cushites, referring to the biblical Cush.</note> both by themselves and by all Asians, according to the historian **Josephus**. **Arias Montanus** <note>A 16th-century Spanish orientalist and editor of the Polyglot Bible.</note> testifies to me that they are still called *Cushios* by the inhabitants of **Cufitana** today. **Isaac Tzetzes** records that they are called *Cepheidas*. You will also read that they were called **Indians** under the entry for the **Rhizophagi**. 

Ancient history, however, mentions both Eastern and Western Ethiopians, as **Heliodorus** names them in his ninth book. The latter he places in **Asia**, and the former in **Africa**. **Herodotus**, in his books *Thalia* and *Polymnia*, also places these same people in Asia among the Indians, where the difference between the two groups is described. The *Chronicle of Eusebius* <note>original: "Eusebii Chronicon"</note> records those rising near the **Indus River** around the year of the world 3580, adding that they later settled around Egypt. **Philostratus** writes in his third book (or perhaps he trifles) that they once lived near the **Ganges River** before there was an African Ethiopia. 

But a serious author, **Pausanias** in his second book *Eliacorum*, places them among the **Seres** people <note>The "Seres" was the ancient Greek and Roman name for the inhabitants of northern China, known for silk.</note> and the island of **Seria**, where the custom of making silk from worms exists. **Claudian**, in his poem *On the Old Man of Verona* and in his *Panegyric to Stilicho*, calls these same Easterners "Black Indians." Likewise does **Tibullus** in his fourth book, *In Praise of Sulpicia*. **Pomponius Mela** calls them the "Black Races" <note>original: "Atras Gentes"</note>. According to **Strabo**, the "Aetherian" Ethiopians are the furthest peoples within **Carthage**, reaching the "Cinnamon-bearing Region." 

Herodotus, in his third book, mentions the "Long-lived Ethiopians" <note>original: "Æthiopes Macrobios"</note> who inhabit Africa toward the Southern Sea. An old anonymous commentator on Ptolemy’s *Tetrabiblos* <note>original: "Quadripartitum"</note> calls part of Ethiopia "Great Asia." In the writings of **Saint Jerome**, specifically in the *Life of Saint Matthias*, I read this: "Ethiopia, where the incursion of the **Apsarus** and the **Port of Hyssus** is located." **Dorotheus** calls this "Interior Ethiopia." However, in place of *Apsarus*, he identifies the river **Phasis**. This Ethiopia—whether real or mythical—is therefore located around **Colchis** <note>A region on the coast of the Black Sea, in modern-day Georgia.</note>.

**Memnones** <note>Greek: "μέμνονες"</note>, a people of Ethiopia below Egypt according to Ptolemy, Pliny, and **Stephanus**. **Sidonius**, if I am not mistaken, in his work to **Priscus Valerianus**, calls these people the "Indian Memnones," describing them as "scorched by the civic torch of Aurora" <note>A poetic way of saying they are darkened by the rising sun/the East.</note>.

**Rhizophagi** <note>Greek: "Ριζοφαγοι", literally "Root-eaters"</note>, a people of Ethiopia dwelling near the **Astaboras** and **Astapus** rivers, according to **Diodorus Siculus**. They are also called *Elii* <note>Greek: "ελειοι"</note> by Strabo in his sixteenth book. These Rhizophagi are placed among the Indians at the **Estaboras River** (as translated by **P. Gyllius**) by **Aelian** in his seventeenth book on animals. In the Greek edition of **Gesner’s** code, the word is printed as *ezamenon* <note>Greek: "εζαμενον"</note>, but it is clear from Pliny, Mela, Strabo, and Ptolemy that it should be read as *Astaboras* <note>Greek: "άϛάβορας"</note>, for they describe these Rhizophagi near this river, which is a branch of the **Nile**. From this passage in Aelian (and others, such as book 16, chapter 33, where he says **Libya** is near the Indians), it is understood that the Ethiopians who live by the Nile are also called "Indians." Thus **Virgil**, in the fourth book of the *Georgics*, was following ancient authority when he also called these people "Indians" (though "colored" to distinguish them from others). **Procopius** agrees with this in his work *On Buildings*.
