# History of the Origin of [the Ethiopians]

...where it says the Nile flows out from the mountains of the Indians. Therefore he calls Ethiopia "India." **Hyginus** also describes **Thebes of the Hundred Gates** as being in India; and in the *Book of Boundaries* <note>original Latin: "lib. Limitium"</note> he writes that Indians inhabit the region from **Egypt** all the way to the **Ocean** toward the **Equator** <note>original Latin: "Aequinoctialem"</note>.

We find in the records of the Greeks that the land of Egypt was sometimes named by them *Melambolos* <note>original Greek: "μελάμβωλος" — meaning black soil</note>, *Hephaistia* <note>original Greek: "ἡφαιστία" — land of fire or Hephaestus</note>, *Potamia* <note>original Greek: "ποταμία" — river-land</note>, *Ogygia* <note>original Greek: "ὠγυγία" — ancient/primordial</note>, and *Aetia*, or *Ethiopia* under *Aithyos* <note>original Greek: "Αἰτία, αἰθιοπία ὑπὸ αἴθυος"</note>. According to **Tzetzes** <note>A 12th-century Byzantine grammarian.</note> they were called *Cepheidas*; while **Pliny** (Book 5, Chapter 8 and Book 6, Chapters 29 and 30 of his *Natural History*) and **Solinus** in his *Polyhistor* (Chapter 33) report that it was formerly called **Aetheria**. However, according to **Strabo** (Book 2), there was only a certain part of it that bore this name, which was the final portion toward **Libya** and the region called **Cinnamomum** <note>The "Cinnamon-bearing" region, likely the Horn of Africa.</note>. 

This country was first named **Atlantia**, after the giant **Atlas** who is said to have reigned in **Africa**; and a son of **Vulcan** named **Ethiops**, arriving there, gave it his name, **Ethiopia**. Others say that this word "Ethiopia" comes from the Greek word *aitho* <note>original Greek: "αἴθω"</note>, which means "burnt," and *opsis* <note>original Greek: "ὄψις"</note>, "face," because the Ethiopian country is situated beneath the **Torrid Zone**. Some others maintain that this country took its name neither from the Greek words above, nor from Ethiops the son of Vulcan, but rather from a certain Eastern nation called the **Ethopeans**, which formerly lived along the **Indus River**. 

Beyond the above, I will report that the Ethiopians were formerly called *Auases* by the Egyptians, according to **Strabo** (Book 2), due to the variety of colors of the earth in their country, and that the people themselves were distinguished by this variety. Because of this, the name has remained with them even to the present, there being a region called **Gazacie** (from **Girava** in Geography), called by the good ancient authors *Abas*, *Hhabas*, and *Alhabas*. The Arabic article "Al" is added as a graceful ornament. From *Abas* or *Abassie*, the Ethiopians of today are called **Abyssinians** by all the nations of the earth; and by this word they are known and understood throughout all the **Orient**, according to the report of **Marco Polo** <note>original: "Marc Paule"</note> (Book 3, Chapter 43 of his *Travels*). 

Properly, the true Abyssinians are those who live in Africa toward the North, who neighbor the deserts that separate Egypt from Ethiopia. Their faces are marked, according to the custom of the country, with a hot and glowing iron, which has caused many to believe they used this branding in place of **Baptism**—a thing which is entirely far from their intention. Those of this nation are also named **Nubians**, from the province of **Nubia**, which at present is somewhat under the subjection and sovereignty of the great Emperor or Christian King **Prester John** <note>original: "Prestegiani Chrestié" — a legendary Christian monarch of the Middle Ages, often identified with the Emperor of Ethiopia.</note>, of whom we will speak at length hereafter. 

The **Hebrews** have written that *Chus* (a Hebrew word) signifies in English **Ethiopia**, or "black." This was the name of one of the sons of **Ham**, son of **Noah**, from which *Chus* the Ethiopians descended and proceeded, who are named in the Hebrew language <insert>כושים</insert> *Chussim*, as confirmed by **Josephus** (Book 1, Chapter 12 of *Antiquities of the Jews*), **Eusebius** (Book 9, Chapter 4 of his *Preparation for the Gospel*), and **Saint Augustine** (Book 16, Chapter 11 of *The City of God*). In fact, these Hebrews call Ethiopia *Chus* in their language; the **Portuguese** <note>original: "Lusitaniens"</note> call it *Cussia*; the Greeks call it *Aithiopian* <note>original Greek: "Αἰθιοπίαν"</note>; and the Latins call it **India**. 

As the author who interprets our Hebrew, Chaldean, and Greek names of the Old and New Testaments says: "Ethiopia in Hebrew is called *Chus*, and it is interpreted as 'black' or 'blackness'; for *Aithiopia* in Greek signifies 'heat' or 'burning.' The region of the Ethiopians, rising from the **Indus River**, adjacent to Egypt..."

### On the black color of the complexion of the Ethiopians, Negroes, Blacks, or Moors of Africa.

<image-desc>Decorative initial Q featuring floral and scrollwork patterns.</image-desc>
**Q**uite a few ancient Greek and Latin authors have written that the Black color of the complexion of the Ethiopians was made and caused by the vehement and insupportable heat and ardor of the **Sun's Rays**, which struck directly down upon their region located in Africa under the **Torrid Zone** <note>The region of the Earth between the Tropics of Cancer and Capricorn.</note>. This is what **Herodotus** in his third book and **Strabo** in the 15th book of his *Geography* denied for several reasons, attributing this entirely to the seed of their black and curly-haired fathers who, by their nature, engendered them.

The **Hebrews** have asserted in their writings that **Ham** <note>original: Chã</note>, one of the sons of the Patriarch **Noah**, having been deprived of his father's blessing, caused no small wound to his posterity. This was so that his descendants would be a perpetual testimony of the ire and indignation of God toward his father. Because of this, the children of **Mitzraim** <note>original: Mitzraim</note> his son, who are none other than the **Egyptians**, were born with a black color, rendered deformed in this way from other men, as is confirmed by **Rabbi Solomon** <note>original: R. Selo, referring to the commentator Rashi</note> on Genesis 12. The **Gætulians**, besides being black, have such foul-smelling mouths that they are constrained to always keep salt in them, according to the report of **Guillaume Postel** <note>original: G. Postel</note> in his *Compendium of Cosmography*. The children of **Phut**, the third of his sons, who are none other than the **Libyans** or **Moors**, were likewise born black in color, flat-nosed <term>camus</term>, thick-lipped <term>lippus</term>, and very hideous and frightful. The children of **Cush** <note>original: Chus</note>, the first of his sons, who are the **Ethiopians**, were also born of a very black color—not because of their Province and Region being situated under the violent heat of the Sun’s rays, as most of the ancient Greek and Latin authors have written, but rather because of their origin.

And this is all the more certain because under the **Equator** and the **Torrid Zone** <note>The regions of the Earth surrounding the Equator, once thought too hot for habitation.</note>, and places closest to one or the other **Tropic**, among the very black peoples who inhabit those areas today, one finds many others who are of white and chestnut colors. These people are the offspring and descendants of the blood of **Abraham**, **Solomon**, and other **Jews**, whose ancestors came to live among these **Negro** or black peoples. Likewise, those who live in **India** under the same climate—even the same parallel—would be of the same and identical color as them if they did not proceed from a different origin than the other peoples mentioned above. This is further proven in the **West Indies**, where the **Indians** are for the most part of an olive or "Indian" color—that is, a dark ashen color—except for a few who live in a single place not far from the others, for which reason they are held and reputed as enemies by their neighbors. In contrast, the true **Negro** or black **Ethiopians** take great pleasure and glory in their black color. Furthermore, as far as 35 degrees of latitude in **Africa** beyond the Equator, the peoples there are very black in color, unlike those who live on this side of the said equator, among whom are the **Spanish**, **Sardinians**, **Syrians**, **Arabs**, **Babylonians**, **Chaldeans**, **Persians**, **Susians**, **Turks**, **Tartars**, **Gedrosians**, and other peoples situated 35 degrees on this side of the Equator at a similar latitude. Among these, no **Ethiopian**, Negro, or black peoples are currently found. This leads us to believe entirely in the opinion of the aforementioned **Hebrews**, who have assured that **Cush**, named above and descended from **Ham** (who was of white color just like his brothers **Japhet** and **Shem**), fathered and begot these **Ethiopians**, Negroes, and blacks as a perpetual testimony to the fault and guilt he committed against his own father; as is confirmed by **Gilbert Génébrard** <note>original: G. Genebrard</note> in Book 1 of his *Chronography*, following **Berosus** in Book 3 of his *Antiquities*.

Regarding what is mentioned above, we shall report the following words of a very learned modern personage: "The Latins called the wicked and the impious 'black'..." <note>original Latin: "Latini improbos & impios, nigros dicebant," likely continuing onto the next page</note>

<margin>cc</margin>“Now it is enough for us that the middle of the East and West be placed in **America**, because 그 region is divided from the **Indies** and **Africa** by infinite spaces. The middle of the North and South, however, is the **Equator**, as far as the whole world is concerned: but for this hemisphere which is on this side of the Equator, it is the 45th degree of latitude: so that whatever lies between there and the Pole is attributed to the North, and the rest to the South. And since the ancients (except for **Posidonius** and **Avicenna**) defined the habitations of men by the tropical and polar circles, thinking there was no place for safety or living beyond them, this error must be removed. For it has been discovered by frequent voyages that the region of the Equator is most healthy; whereas under the **Tropics**, the regions burn with incredible heat, and the reason is readily apparent. For the **Sun** rises higher at the Equator, and is carried much more swiftly because of the magnitude of the circle than at the tropics. Indeed, **Alvarez** <note>Francisco Álvares, a Portuguese explorer</note> writes that the waters there freeze with frost in the month of June, provided the South wind blows. Add to this the great force of the rains, the incredible height of the mountains, and the abundance of forests; finally, the color and face of the men is not at all black, but like that of olives. On the contrary, under the Tropics there is vehement heat, no rain, no forests, few rivers, and a perpetual plain of sands—except in **Arabia Felix** and certain places in **India**, due to the nature of the East and the mountainous region. Finally, the skin of the inhabitants is black, not only of the **Ethiopians**, but also of the **Indians**, as **Ctesias** long ago and our own men have discovered. For I can hardly be persuaded by what a certain learned man teaches, that men became black from the curse of **Cush**; and long ago the opinion of **Herodotus** was ridiculed, who thought the semen of Ethiopians was black. For it would be necessary for Ethiopians born in **Scythia** <note>Central Eurasia</note> to be black, and Scythians born in **Ethiopia** to be white, whereas all peoples have long since been mixed by the multitude and frequency of colonies. But we see that men, just like plants, degenerate gradually when the soil is changed, and the reason is the same why fire and the sun—as **Aristotle** teaches—stain men with a black color. Indeed, **Pliny** writes that lions in Ethiopia are black, as the poet **Oppian** testifies he had seen in his book on hunting.” This same author, continuing his discourse, says finally, “And since under the tropics and both Poles...”

Therefore, what **Hippocrates** <note>The famous Greek "Father of Medicine"</note> says—that men to the North are deformed by paleness and thinness—would be absurd, unless we refer to the extreme reaches of the North; for the same ancient writers say that those in the closer northern regions are robust and tall.

# Peoples of this World
<note>original French: "Langues de ceft Vniuers"—in this context, "langues" refers to "nations" or "peoples" rather than just spoken languages.</note>

...the heat of the Sun, they abound in coldness and humidity, in which there is much nourishment that is not drawn out by heat itself. Therefore, the men there are of a white color, with long hair, great stature, and well-proportioned; but of a cold nature, and of cruel manners due to the vehemence of the cold being in those places. Read more in **L. le Roy**, book 1, leaf 23, *On the Vicissitude of Things*; see also **J. Bodin**, *Method of History*, chapter 5.

The **Maurusians**, who are none other than **Moors**, presently inhabit **Mauritania** in Africa, so named from the Greek word *mauros* <note>original Greek: μανρὸς—meaning dark, dim, or black</note>, which signifies black according to some authors, because this people is colored with this tint. On this point, I do not wish to cast doubt, although it seems to me that the entire stretch of the country named Mauritania does not have black people, and that rather the **Nigrites** <note>A term used by ancient geographers for the peoples of the Niger River region in Sub-Saharan Africa</note> deserve such a name; but let us pass over this and grant to the ancients what is neither honest nor fitting to deny them by contradiction, since the word is of such significance that it carries not only blackness, but an obscure and shadowy color. Thus, it must not be taken as a rule that if there are white people in Mauritania, it contradicts the name, since we know there are several kinds of Moors. Modern navigators and travelers who have particularly described the **Cape of Good Hope** and the countries in **Ethiopia** toward the Indian Sea, have written the following concerning the doubt so much debated by many regarding the color of these Moors or Negroes. There are those who hold that the burning heat of the Sun is the cause of this blackness, whereas **Strabo** in book 15 seems to be of the contrary opinion when he says that heat is not the cause of the blackened color. This is because those who are in their mothers' wombs, even though the Sun has not spread its rays upon them, are nevertheless born black and swarthy; he then adds that they become such by the force of the seed of their fathers, whom they are made to resemble.

Those who attribute the cause to the Sun, such as **Alexander of Aphrodisias** <note>A Greek commentator on Aristotle</note> in book 1 of *Problems*, inquiring why the Sun blackens a man, whitens linen, softens wax, and hardens mud, responds that the aptitude of the affected matter is the cause. For, he says, the materials of our body—except for <term>phlegm|original: "pituite," one of the four traditional humors</term>—whenever they are too greatly heated, cause the hide and skin to blacken. With this author agrees **Albert the Great** in his book *On the Nature of Places*, when he says that Southern men, and those who stay in hot and meridional parts—and above all the **Ethiopians**—are black as much for the heat of the Sun in the places where they reside as for the heated disposition of their bodies. This is because, in the first place, the seed of generation in them is hot, and the <term>matrix|womb</term> of the women who receive this seed is also very hot and very dry. From this it happens that once the seed of the man is conceived, being digested by a violent <term>concoction|the "cooking" or ripening of humors through heat</term>, the blood of the formed fruit becomes <term>adust|original: "aduste"—meaning scorched or parched by heat</term> and burnt. The more subtle moisture being driven out by the humor of the place, that which is gross and earthy—which is also burnt—remains, and causes the blackness in the body and the skin of the men. In these people, the more earthy parts are also very strong, and the bones are very white, as can be seen in the teeth of Moors; whereas their flesh, stained by the burnt blood, is blackish and swarthy. All these reasons are very good and drawn from nature itself, but for my part, I cannot [conclude]...

# History of the Origin of the
<note>original French: "Hiſtoire de l'Origine des"—likely "History of the Origin of the Nations" or "Peoples," continuing the previous page's focus.</note>

...attribute to the power of the Sun what I attribute to the seed, to which the latter gives the most strength, even though the Sun is designated as the primary cause by common saying. And it is true that in **Ethiopia**, white men produce children who resemble them, and in these parts, black men coupled with white women have children who reflect their color: which is a very apparent argument for the vigor of the seed, unless one wished to add the power of the imagination <note>A common Renaissance belief that a mother’s thoughts or sights during conception or pregnancy could physically alter the appearance of the child.</note>, which has influence in some things, but not always. Therefore, we are content, so as not to stray from the reasoning of the ancients, to believe that the already disposed seed can do much, and that the thing thus begun receives its final impressions from the vehemence of the Sun, since we see that those who spend a long time in the sun's glare also feel a very great alteration of their color. Furthermore, all the aforementioned peoples, according to whether they are closer to or farther from these burning heats and the perpendicular strikes of the Sun's rays, are also more black and have frizzy hair, which is a very apparent sign of great heat.

There is yet another consideration, which concerns the opinion of the ancients and many moderns, who estimate the lands located under the **Equinoctial line**, or **Torrid Zone**, to be entirely deserted, sterile, dry, and without any fruit or seed whatsoever. People have clung to this opinion all the more because they have seen the most learned and scholarly men stumble against this stone and stop at such an ill-advised division of the celestial Zones; for if that were the case, most of the earth would be uninhabitable. For out of five Zones, they maintain that three are without habitation, and they take **Aristotle** as their guarantor, whom it seems would be a heresy in terms of Philosophy to contradict. Following his custom of reasoning subtly and with some foundation, he says in the 3rd [book] of *Meteorology* <note>original: "Meteores"</note>, chapter 2, that the middle Zone, which is that of the **Equator**, is uninhabitable because of the violence of the heat, and the two extremities as well, because the cold there is unbearable. 

But **Ptolemy**, through his descriptions, shows quite the contrary, and several other good authors show that the Equator is not so violent that men cannot live there, nor so dry and burnt that the trees and plants do not stay green in all seasons. Likewise, the **Poles** are not so assaulted by cold that there are not infinite thousands of men who inhabit our **Arctic**, as **Olaus the Great** and **John** <note>Olaus Magnus and Joannes Magnus, Swedish brothers and prominent 16th-century geographers/historians</note> have described at length in their descriptions of the northernmost regions of the earth. And as for the **Antarctic Pole**, those who have described the voyages of **Magellan** have no doubt that the country there is inhabited, and that the land being populated, nature has also provided for the nourishment of the inhabitants under that line. 

Regarding the Equator, **Albert the Great**, whom we alleged above, says in the treatise *On the Nature of Places* <note>original: "De natura locorum"</note>, chapter 6, and treatise 1, chapter 19 of the 3rd book of *Meteorology*, that in that region which the ancients called "burnt," under the Equator, the dwelling is milder and more temperate than elsewhere under the Tropics—not that it is always so, but according to the presence of the Sun. For when the Sun occupies the **Winter Solstice**, namely the **Tropic of Capricorn**, it is without lie that the season is milder and more temperate at the **Tropic of Cancer** than under the Equator; and on the contrary, when the Sun occupies the summer tropic, everything is temperate toward the southern parts, from which it follows that all this...

consideration relates to the presence or distance of the Sun. The Sun, when positioned at the Parallel of the **Equator**, is actually more bearable to those who live beneath it, even though twice a year it is directly perpendicular to them and turns back upon itself; not that it stays fixed in the same place, for its circle is wide, and in almost a straight course it departs from the **Equinox**, toward which it does not return without passing through a barrier of four of the lesser signs <note>This refers to the movement of the sun through the constellations of the Zodiac.</note>. This is the reason why the heat and its vehemence do not remain in one place and do not easily burn it, considering the span of time—that is, the heat of the rising Sun and that which it creates while moving retrograde—and it happens that one heat does not meet the other. Consequently, it is impossible for the heat there to be as vehement and increased as was formerly estimated. 

Thus, men of good wit recognize how much those people err who, basing their ideas on the reflection and the striking of perpendicular rays upon the inhabitants of those lands under the **Equator**, estimate that they are burned by it; they consequently infer that this part of the world is uninhabitable. However, the equality of the days and nights <note>At the Equator, days and nights are always roughly 12 hours each.</note> is the cause for this violent heat being tempered, just as it is also corrected by the Sun's deep descent below the **Horizon**. Thus, the heat increased during the twelve-hour daily course is tempered by the equal length of the night, which makes the volatility and speed of the sun's rays less vehement. 

Now, if one argues that this solar course passing through the **Equinoctial line** is not as temperate as we say, one can draw proof from the fact that while the Sun is there, it performs its course very quickly, whereas it is slower when passing through the lesser signs of the **Zodiac**. One cannot accept the opinion that says nothing is temperate between two very hot things, especially since we cannot agree—without failing miserably—that both **Tropics** are very hot at the same time, seeing as it is impossible for them to enjoy the presence of the Sun in the same season. It is known by experience that when the Sun moves away from any part of the earth, it causes cooling because the lower elements <note>The "lower elements" here refer to water and earth, which were thought to be naturally cold compared to the "fire" of the sun.</note> gain the upper hand.

And to avoid entering into too long a discourse, since reason shows that the regions under the **Equator** are indeed temperate, it would be folly to call them uninhabitable—especially since the discoveries made in our own time have shown us the contrary. We know by the true accounts of those who have traveled both this side and that of the line dividing the **Hemispheres**, that between the two **Tropics of Cancer and Capricorn**, one does not feel a continual alteration of heat except in the manner we have described: namely, when the Sun is perpendicular. At that time, in the area where it passes, for one month before and one month after, the air is cloudy and hot. This has been confirmed by the aforementioned navigators and travelers in their voyages, saying unanimously that the inhabitants are much troubled by this heat, and hardly a day passes without it raining for two or three hours. They say the water of this rain, or rather this "stew," is hot, salty, and of bad taste, which is probable given the attractions of the Sun. These rains are hardly less unhealthy than those of a summer storm, when, due to the vehemence of corrupt vapors, we see it rain toads and frogs <note>A common folklore belief that sudden summer storms could transport or "generate" small animals like frogs.</note>. ## History of the Origin of the

...as we have said, is the winter of the equatorial lands: but as the Sun moves further away, the season there is mild and temperate, without one seeing any sign of drought, nor scorching, nor lack of fruits, grasses, and greenery, just as the ancients wished to prove with arguments lacking any fairness <note>The author is refuting the classical Greek theory that the "Torrid Zone" was a scorched, uninhabitable wasteland.</note>. Furthermore, we find in the navigations and travels of the aforementioned modern navigators and travelers that the inhabitants of Kilwa <note>original: "Quilao", an island state off the coast of present-day Tanzania.</note>, a country of the Indies, are diverse in color (which goes against those who attribute the blackness of the complexion to the heat of the country), for they are ordinarily of an olive color, neither white nor black; others there are white like those of Barbary <note>North Africa</note>, and others black like the blackest of Ethiopia. On the Island of Saint Thomas <note>São Tomé</note>, located directly under the Equator, or Equinoctial line, the children of Europeans are white there as in Europe, unless, their white wives having died, they marry the daughters of Ethiopians who have become Christians and live according to our fashion; for the children who come from them are no longer white, but rather blackish: which is evident proof that the Sun is not at all the cause of men being black in Ethiopia and other places, but that this comes from the disposition of the seeds <note>A 16th-century term for heredity or genetics.</note>.

&emsp;&emsp;To conclude this matter, we shall advise readers that according to the accounts of moderns who speak of the Negroes, Blacks, or Moors of Africa, after one has passed the land of the Bazanez people, currently called Azanaghes <note>The Sanhaja, a Berber tribal confederation of the Sahara.</note>, who are of a tawny color and dwell on this side of the river Niger or Senegal, one comes to the land of those Negroes, Blacks, or Moors living beyond the aforementioned river Niger or Senegal. The separation of the said Bazanez and the said Negroes, Blacks, or Moors is made by the said river Niger, otherwise called the Senegal, the source of which is held to come from the same place as that of the Nile, having the same ebb and flow as the Egyptian river, watering and fattening the lands through which it passes in the same way, and nourishing Crocodiles and other aquatic Beasts or Monsters that are ordinarily seen in the Nile. Because of this river, the whole country is named Senegal, looking toward the West at the great Ocean sea, to the south the kingdom of Gambia, and toward the North is this great River which separates (as has been said) the aforementioned Bazanez from the said Negroes, Blacks, or Moors, and gives a beginning to the country named in this time Lower Ethiopia <note>A historical geographical term used by Europeans to describe the sub-Saharan regions of West and Central Africa.</note>. These Negroes, Blacks, or Moors of Senegal are at present Mahometans <note>Muslims</note>, but not of the most refined or firm in their superstition as the white Moors, especially since they have no persons to instruct them, and they do not take much account of it, particularly since Christians have frequented them. These black people go all naked, except for some covers of goat skin or cotton to cover their private parts. In this country, although outside the power and jurisdiction of the King of Senegal, are the Barbarins and Seretes, black like the others. Having passed this country, one goes to the kingdom of Gambia where the inhabitants are also black, partly Idolaters and partly Mahometans. Following this coast, grazing Africa and doubling the Cape of Palms, you enter the kingdom of Guinea, in which are Malagueta <note>original: "Molegete", referring to the Grain Coast, named for Malagueta pepper.</note>, Benin, and Manicongo <note>The Kingdom of Kongo</note>, where there are also many black people, partly Idolaters—who change their god every day from the morning—and partly Mahometans, as Jean <note>This likely refers to Joannes Leo Africanus, a primary source for African geography in the 16th century.</note> describes at length.

## Of the Kingdom of Ethiopia.

<note>Ornamental drop cap 'N' with intricate floral patterns.</note>We read nothing in all of Holy Scripture, and even less in the secular histories of the ancients, that provides any certain memory of the race, succession, and lineage of the Kings of Ethiopia. It is true, however, that we find written in ancient histories that Cush <note>original: "Chus"; in biblical tradition, the son of Ham and grandson of Noah</note> was the first to found the kingdom of Ethiopia, which endures even to this day, as Marino Sanuto <note>original: "Marin Romain"</note> recounts in his history of the Ethiopians, based on the reports of the histories of the Abyssinians <note>A historical name for Ethiopia</note>; this seems to be what the poet Homer intended to denote when speaking of the great antiquity of this kingdom. These histories of the Abyssinians or Ethiopians contain that after this Cush, the first King of Ethiopia, died, six other Kings, his successors, reigned after him. There is no memory of their names in the histories, and it is certain that one cannot truly remark how long they reigned, nor in which city or town of Ethiopia their principal residence was located, until after these six Kings, the seventh retired to the city of Aksum <note>original: "Caxumo"</note>. In this city was established the principal royal seat of the Ethiopian Kings until the time of Jesus Christ, as the aforementioned Marino Sanuto recounts. He says that the greatest certainty we have regarding the lineage of the aforementioned Kings is that Makeda, otherwise known as Nicaula <note>The Queen of Sheba</note>, Queen of Ethiopia and Egypt—as Josephus writes in Book 8 of the *Antiquities of the Jews*—coming from Sheba <note>Saba</note>, an island of the Nile later called Meroë by Cambyses, to visit the great King Solomon in the eleventh year of his reign, had intimacy with this great King and had by him a son first named Melich, then David. He was the first to firmly establish the kingdom of Ethiopia. It is certain, according to the histories of the said Ethiopians, that the preceding Ethiopian Kings had no stability or security in their kingdom until Arue, who first established the seat of his kingdom at Aksum for 400 years. Then Agabo his brother for 200; then Ghedur, otherwise called Sabannit, for 100 years, having conquered all of Ethiopia; then Makeda his daughter for 80 years, who was the mother of the said Melich, who reigned 29 years; Audede his son for one year; Auda his brother for 11 years; Gegafio for 3 years; Zangua for 44 years; Gafio for 1; Antet for 61; Bafara for 9; Cauada for 2; Chauze for 10; Endur for 9; Guaza for 1; Eudrach for 1; Chaales for 1; Setija for 17; Aglaba for 3; Aufcua for 1; Breguas for 17; Beseclugna for 17; and Baazena for 27, under whose reign our Lord Jesus Christ was born. However, this is not too certain or assured, as Gilbert Genebrard demonstrates in his *Cosmography*.

The histories of these Ethiopians recount that this Queen Candace, who is spoken of in the Acts of the Apostles under the title of Queen of Ethiopia, was named Judith in her own right. In fact, those Ethiopians did not understand the Syriac language in his time, and even less the Greek, but they did understand Hebrew, which they learned from their childhood in their schools, just as they still do today—much like we learn the Greek and Latin languages. In this way, we must interpret the words of Chapter 8 of the *Acts of the Apostles*, speaking of the Eunuch of the Queen of Ethiopia, who, while sitting in his chariot, was reading the Prophet Isaiah. The priests there marry so as to leave a lineage, but the monks do not; however, if the priests' wives die, it is not permitted for them to enter into a second marriage. There is a great diversity of religious orders who take vows and profession of chastity, obedience, and poverty, living in community and performing great and admirable abstinences under the Rule of Saint Anthony and Saint Macarius, though they have other saintly Abbots and Monks who have caused many of their monasteries to be built. Of our Saints, they recognize only the glorious Virgin Mary Mother of God, Saint Michael, the Apostles, and notably Saint Thomas and Saint Matthew—the latter having converted the inhabitants of Meroë, and the former having traveled from Ethiopia to the Indies to win over the Indians. Among the Martyrs, they greatly revere St. Stephen and St. George; and among the Confessors, the hermits St. Anthony and St. Macarius. Whoever unhappily blasphemes against these is burned alive in the public square. They have a number of their own particular Saints from among those who lived saintly lives in their country. All of these report to one great and sovereign leader to whom they all refer; this leader usually stays at the Court and depends on the Patriarch of Grand Cairo (who formerly resided in Alexandria, Egypt). In our time, they have acknowledged by letters and actions the Holy Apostolic See of Rome—not as the one who appoints or has the power to establish their Bishops, but only as the head of the Churches and the mother of the flock for the foundation of doctrine, just as Christians have always testified regarding this holy see and the universal Bishop who presides there. 

The histories of these Ethiopians recite that this Queen Candace—of whom mention is made in the *Acts of the Apostles* under the title Queen of Ethiopia—was named Judith in her own right. She was born two miles from Aksum <note>original: "Caxumo." Aksum was the capital of the ancient Aksumite Empire.</note>, a city in the Kingdom of Angote in Ethiopia, and she was the first to plant the faith of Jesus Christ our Lord in Ethiopia. She also built the first Church there, which is still standing, very beautiful and magnificent, bearing the title of Saint Mary of Zion. This is because the sacred Table and Stone of the altar was brought from Mount Zion in Jerusalem; for the Ethiopians are accustomed to naming their churches after stones <note>This refers to the "tabot," a consecrated tablet representing the Ark of the Covenant, which is the most sacred element of an Ethiopian Orthodox church.</note>. This Queen was converted to the Christian faith by her agent, Philip the Eunuch, whom the Deacon Saint Philip (one of the seventy-two disciples) instructed in the Gospel doctrine, as is contained in the 8th chapter of the *Acts of the Apostles*. This is confirmed by L. Carretus in his *Epistle to the Jews*, citing Psalm 72: "The kings of Sheba and Ethiopia shall offer gifts" <note>original: "Reges Sabæ, & Æthiopiæ, munera offerent"</note>, and Psalm 68: "and furthermore the Ethiopian shall clap his hands" <note>original: "et præterea Æthyops plaudet manibus suis"</note>. It is also confirmed by Father Francisco Álvares <note>A Portuguese missionary and explorer who wrote "A True Relation of the Lands of Prester John" (1540).</note> in chapters 38 and 84 of his account of his voyage to Ethiopia, where he reports the letter from the Ethiopian King David <note>Emperor Lebna Dengel, who took the throne name Dawit II.</note> sent to Pope Clement VII in the year of Salvation 1524 via the same Álvares. It is true, however, that F. Brocard, in his description of the Holy Land, maintains that these Ethiopians were taught the Christian religion by Saint Matthew.

He took this idea from Simeon Metaphrastes <note>A 10th-century Byzantine author famous for compiling the lives of saints.</note>, a Greek author who says that the tradition of the Fathers holds that Saint Matthew was the only one among all the Evangelists who wrote his Gospel in the Hebrew language, and not in the Syriac language (as some have claimed), nor in the Greek language (as John Calvin wrote). He argues this first because all the ancient Fathers of the Church held this view, and secondly because all the fragments that Saint Jerome cites from this Gospel are pure Hebrew. The strongest reason is that Saint Matthew did not write only for the Jews and Syrians, but for all the peoples of the East. These latter peoples used this language as the most learned and grammatical; even now, they use it when celebrating their Masses <note>The author is likely confusing Hebrew with Ge'ez, the ancient liturgical language of Ethiopia, which is a Semitic language like Hebrew.</note>. For this reason, Saint Bartholomew seems to have brought the Gospel of Saint Matthew with him to those countries above all other Evangelists. A copy of which Pantæ-

The priests there marry, but the monks do not, so that they may leave a lineage <note>The author implies priests marry to ensure a line of succession, a common practice in many Eastern traditions where the priesthood was often hereditary.</note>; however, if their wives die, it is not permitted for them to enter into a second marriage. Anyone who wickedly blasphemes against these saints is burned alive in the public square. They also have many of their own local Saints who lived holy lives in their country. They do not confer baptism on anyone until they are forty days old if it is a male, and sixty [days if it is a female]...

if it is a female child, these people say that the faith of the parents is sufficient, and especially that of the mother; they believe that the holy communion she received while pregnant has sanctified the child in her womb. This child is carried to the Church just as is done here, and baptized at its door rather than at the baptismal fonts. The water there is blessed, and the child is sprinkled with this water using the same words that we use. They also use anointing, just as in the Roman Church, on both the forehead and the shoulders of the child being baptized. A godfather is present who holds the child under the armpits, and the Priest, holding a ewer <note>A large jug or pitcher used for carrying water for washing.</note> of water in one hand, performs the pouring with the other, saying: *I baptize you in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit.* In short, they use the same ceremonies as those of our Catholic Church. It is true that they only baptize on Saturdays and Sundays, because those are the only days they celebrate the Holy Mass, and without it, they do not confer the grace of baptism, because they give the sacred communion to the newly regenerated child. Besides this holy Sacrament of baptism, all these Ethiopians also observe an annual Baptism at the same time that we celebrate the feast of the Epiphany <note>The "Apparition of our Lord," or Epiphany, commemorates the visit of the Magi and the baptism of Jesus in the Jordan River.</note>. During this solemnity, everyone comes to a certain lake, and after some prayers are made by a Bishop, they all go down naked into the water and bathe there. They hold the opinion that this washing serves to purge those who, having been Christians, had become Moors <note>In this 16th-century context, "Moors" usually refers to Muslims.</note> and then returned to the Church through repentance. Now, throughout all Ethiopia, there are soldiers and officers chosen from all parts who are in the King’s pay, and who are lightly marked on the skin with a cross using a hot iron; this has caused some to believe that in Ethiopia, this sign alone served as Baptism. Furthermore, according to the account of Leo Africanus <note>Joannes Leo Africanus (c. 1494–1554), a famous traveler and diplomat whose "Description of Africa" was a primary source for Europeans.</note> in Book 4 of the *Description of Africa*, the inhabitants of the city of Bresch <note>Modern-day Cherchell, Algeria.</note> in Africa have the custom of painting a black cross on their cheek and another on their hand—specifically in the palm of the hand, under the fingers. This practice is also observed by the mountain people of Algiers and Buggie <note>Béjaïa, a port city in Algeria.</note> because, according to African historians, the Goths <note>A Germanic people who established kingdoms in Spain and North Africa in the early Middle Ages.</note> took possession of many countries and infinite mountains. By this means, a great number of people were converted to the Christian faith, and the Gothic Kings ordered their officers to levy no tribute from them. But because at the time of payment everyone claimed to be a Christian, without there being any easy way to notice or recognize those who were or were not, it was ordained that Christians should be designated and recognized by this cross. Since the time that sovereignty was taken out of their hands, all the people returned to the Mohametan law <note>The Islamic faith.</note>. Nevertheless, this manner of marking remained successively from time to time, without many being found who can explain the reason for it. The lords of Mauritania <note>A region in North Africa, roughly modern Morocco and Western Algeria.</note> still observe this same custom as well as the nobles, who make a cross on their cheek with a hot iron, and one sees enough of them in Europe marked in this way. As for the holy communion, they receive it with very great reverence and honor the bread before it is consecrated in honor of what it is to become, firmly believing in the real presence of the substance of the body of our Lord sacramentally in the Eucharist. those Ethiopians [hold] that it is a sin to do otherwise, and that it shows little respect for such a high and divine mystery; furthermore, there must be more than one Priest present when the Mass is said, and all those attending must receive communion, having performed great fasts—especially the Monks, who fast for more than half the year. During this time, they only say and celebrate Mass at night, and everyone receives communion, then they go to take their meal. As for which days are designated for these fasts, Francisco Álvares in his history of Ethiopia, chapter 3, and Joseph Scaliger in his *Commentary on the Calendar of the Abyssins*, Book 7 of *On the Correction of Times* <note>original: "de la Correctiō des temps," referring to Scaliger's influential work on chronology, *De emendatione temporum*.</note>, describe them at length. The order of the Estates is such that the Clergy hold the highest place after the King, then come the *Ienquates* and *Bassamates*—that is to say, doctors <note>In this context, "doctors" refers to learned scholars or theologians.</note> and those who make a profession of teaching letters and judging—and after them, the Nobility are respected, and finally the soldiers. When someone comes to die, they incense the body and wash it, and afterwards they shroud it and sew it inside a linen cloth. When the Priests come to carry it to the earth, they say several very short prayers, then lift the body and carry it to the Church, the cross always marching in front with the censer and the holy water; and being near the Church, they do not carry the body inside it, but rather put it immediately into its pit, having incensed it and thrown holy water inside, without saying funeral rites or vigils, except for some chapters of the Gospel of Saint John. They do not sing any Masses for the deceased, just as they celebrate none for the particular devotion of any living person, since they sing only one each day in each Church. They mourn their dead for the space of forty days, which is how long their mourning lasts, being dressed during this time in entirely black clothes, which they leave off after this time to resume their ordinary and previous clothing. In short, all the Christian Ethiopians are uniform in their Religion, without there being among them any schisms, heresies, or divisions on the matter of their doctrine, because only the Clergy involve themselves in treating and discoursing upon the Holy Scripture. Marriage ceremonies are commonly performed there in the same form and manner as in the Catholic, Apostolic, and Roman Church. These Ethiopians, under the authority of Zara Yaqob <note>Zerah Iacob (reigned 1434–1468), a powerful Emperor of Ethiopia who sought to centralize the church and state.</note> their Emperor, first pledged obedience to Pope Eugene the third <note>The text says "third," but historically this refers to Pope Eugene IV (1431–1447) during the Council of Florence.</note> residing in Rome, who thereafter sent them a certain book, quite thick, to serve as instruction for their ceremonies; which book is still held, according to the voyages of Modern authors, to be found in Ethiopia today, as reported in the letter inserted at the end of the voyages of Álvares, and as confirmed by Damiano de Góis in his book *On the Faith, Religion, and Customs of the Ethiopians*. See what is written at length concerning the customs and Religion of these people by Andrea Corsali in his Letter and voyages addressed to Duke Lorenzo de' Medici; Dom Francisco Álvares in his voyages to Ethiopia; Jerónimo Osório in Book 9 of the *Deeds of Alphonse* and Book 17 of his *History of Portugal*, chapters 20, 21, 22, 23, and 24; Duarte Barbosa in his books of voyages; the Author of the *Summary of the Kingdoms, Cities, and Peoples of the East*; Sabellicus in his *Rhapsodies* or *Ennead* 10, Book 8; André Thevet in Book 2, chapter 14 of his *Cosmography*; and François de Belleforest in volume 2.

### Of the Ethiopian, Indian, or Nubian language.

Raphael Volaterran <note>Raffaele Maffei, a humanist scholar</note>, as reported by Theodore Bibliander in his commentary on the common reasoning of all languages and letters, wrote that the Ethiopians use and employ, up to the present day, the letters and characters of the Babylonians. This author had learned this from those ignorant of the truth of this matter, who, through a common and vulgar belief, held that these Ethiopians had learned and received their language, religion, and origin from Abraham the Chaldean. This is not true, seeing as it is a most certain thing (as we have clearly verified above) that these Ethiopians are descended from no other than Cush, son of Ham, and not from any of the children of Shem <note>The author is navigating 16th-century racial and linguistic theories based on the Table of Nations in Genesis</note>. And even though the form and order of writing the letters and characters of the Ethiopian language—which are written from the left hand toward the right—is entirely different from those of the Hebrew language, nevertheless the power of the said letters and characters, the origin of their words, and the ways of declining and conjugating their nouns and verbs approach very closely those of the said Hebrew language. Regarding this, we shall recite the authority of that great and learned personage Guillaume Postel, who, in his treatise on the *Alphabet of Twelve Languages*, in the chapter on the Indian or Ethiopian language, said the following:

Johann Potken, administrator of the Church of Cologne, was the first who, having had the Psalms of David and the Song of Songs printed here in our Europe some years ago in the Ethiopian, Indian, and Nubian language and its characters, dared—through an ignorance of the Hebrew, Chaldean, and Syriac languages—to assert along with the common crowd (though without much reason) that this language was the same as, or similar to, Chaldean. # Languages of this Universe.

[Our Lord] Jesus Christ spoke a language that was common and vernacular throughout all Syria, which is apparent from several places and passages of Holy Scripture previously cited by me in the chapter on the Syriac language. The <term>Targum</term> <note>An Aramaic translation or paraphrase of the Hebrew Bible</note>, whether the Assyrian or Babylonian version, is written and composed in that Assyrian or Babylonian language; the other <term>Targum</term>, the Jerusalem or Syriac paraphrase, is written and composed in that Syriac language. The reason that induced the aforementioned <term>Potken</term> <note>Johannes Potken, a 16th-century German scholar who published the first printed book in Ge'ez (Ethiopian)</note> to hold, along with the common and vulgar opinion, what we have deduced above, is that he had heard it said, or had read in the books of antiquity, that the Chaldean language was immediately the first and most ancient in the world after the Hebrew language, and consequently that this Ethiopian, Indian, or Nubian language was one and the same.

But we must, with the authority of <term>Teseo Ambrogio</term> <note>A 16th-century Italian linguist</note> in his introduction to the Chaldean, Syriac, and Armenian languages, and the aforementioned <term>Theodor Bibliander</term> <note>A Swiss reformer and polyglot</note> in his *Commentary on the Common Reason of All Languages and Letters*, hold as most certain that this language is in no way Chaldean, but rather another entirely diverse and dissimilar from it. However, it is no less ancient than the other, because <term>Ham</term>, the third son of the Patriarch Noah—to whom and to whose descendants fell the lot of Africa and interior Ethiopia for their habitation and dwelling—transplanted the shoots of Hebraism or Chaldaism into these regions. These remain even to the present day among the Ethiopian, Indian, or Nubian Christians in the southern region of Sabachta, from which part the Queen of Sheba departed to visit King Solomon in the city of Jerusalem. 

These Ethiopians, Indians, or Nubians assert that they have prayed to and adored our Lord Jesus Christ in this language ever since they were taught and indoctrinated in the Christian religion by a Philip, the Eunuch of their Queen named Candace, who was the wife or daughter of one of their kings named Alexander—a name common and familiar to Ethiopian kings even before the time of Alexander the Great. These Ethiopians, Indians, or Nubians became more specifically known to Christendom from the time of Pope Eugene III, and they presently converse ordinarily in the cities of Jerusalem and Rome, as well as in the ports and harbors of Africa, with Jews, Greeks, Italians, Spaniards, Portuguese, and others.

The poet Virgil, in the fourth book of his *Georgics*, called them colored Indians <note>original: "Indos Coloratos"</note>, mentioning "the Nile flowing down from the Indians" <note>original: "Nilum ab Indis deuexum"</note>, and stating that "the Indian color is common to both Ethiopians and Asian Indians" <note>original: "color Indus Æthyopibus & Indis asiaticis communis"</note>. He asserts they are called "Indians," a word common to all Oriental languages, some calling them *Hindi*, others *Hundy* or *Hundiet*, and some *Hundistam*. This word, according to the Ethiopian, Indian, or Nubian priests who presently live in both Constantinople and Venice, is common to Indians and Oriental Christians, as well as to the greater and more sensible part of the other Indians <term>ἀϐαϯϐο͂ν</term> <note>original: "abatibon"</note>, which is to say, those who adore the Devil.

# Of Prester John, Prest-Ian, Prestian, or Prestegian, Great Emperor or King of the Ethiopians, Indians, Nubians, and Abyssinians.

## CHAP. LII.

<image-desc>Decorative drop cap 'G' with floral and foliate motifs within a square frame.</image-desc>

Génébrard <note>Gilbert Génébrard (1535–1597), a French Benedictine exegete and orientalist.</note> in the second book of his *Chronography*, making mention of the three Kings who came to adore our Lord Jesus Christ, has reported these words worthy of great consideration and remark.

> In the 35th year of Herod, the Magi <note>original: "Magi"</note>—who were to worship Christ—came from Persia, which is in the East of the land of Israel (Epiphanius, *Against Heresies*, 51). Two years later, Herod died of a horrific disease. Joseph died at age 71 (Book 2 of the *Kings of Israel*). Herod was buried at Herodium, a city which was a journey of two and a half days from Jerusalem (ibid).

More probable is the view of Ammonius of Alexandria: that on the thirteenth day after the birth of Christ, the Magi arrived in Jerusalem guided by a new star, proclaiming that the King of the Jews was born (*In the Harmony*). This is why the Church celebrates the Epiphany on that day. They likely came from Persia or another eastern place, which we will discuss soon, in the 33rd year of his reign; the star appeared to the Kings four years before his death, according to the words of Saint Cyprian at the very beginning of his *Sermon on Baptism*. For the ancient tradition of the Church is that the Magi were Kings and local rulers <term>Toparchs: governors of a specific district or petty kings</term> (Tertullian, *Against the Jews* and book 3 *Against Marcion*; Jerome on Psalm 71; Augustine, book 3 *On the Wonders of Scripture*, chapter 4, and *Sermon 43 to the Brothers in the Wilderness*; Hilary, book 4 *On the Trinity*; Idacius Clarius to Varimund the Arian). To say nothing of the Greeks: Athanasius, in the second question of his *Diverse Questions to Prince Antiochus*—which Reuchlin <note>Johann Reuchlin (1455–1522), a German humanist and scholar of Greek and Hebrew.</note> translated differently than those commonly found in his volumes—says, "We call the feast of the Epiphany the day of the Three Kings" (Cantacuzenus, *Apology 1*, etc.).

And indeed, they were not only Kings, but they also laid the foundation for that vast Christian Kingdom in India—for they had come from its province which was called Tarshish <note>original: "Tarsis"</note>, and today is Tarfestan (Hayto)—which he who held it for twelve hundred years was called Prester John <note>original: "Presbyter Ioannes"</note>. He possessed both ecclesiastical and secular authority until, around the year 1200, he succumbed to the weapons of the Tartars <note>The Mongol Empire.</note>. From there arose the Islamic empire of the Great Khan (Marco Polo the Venetian in his *Travels*). The title of Prester John was then transferred to that great Christian Emperor of the Abyssinians or Ethiopians (Jerónimo Osorio <note>A Portuguese bishop and historian (1506–1580).</note> in his history of the deeds of Emmanuel, King of Portugal). Nor is it necessary that they were "Great Kings," as God often chooses the weaker things of the world to shame the stronger. However, they were all called "Kings" according to the custom of the East, being those who were entitled to use the scepter and diadem by virtue of their dignity, whether they ruled by their own will or were subject to the law of another. Thus they were distinguished from dukes, as Kimhi <note>David Kimhi (1160–1235), a medieval Jewish biblical commentator and grammarian.</note> often notes. This practice is still observed today by the Tartars, Persians, Ethiopians, and other Easterners; for they are not so anxious and careful in distinguishing between a "King" and a "Prince." Thus Catherine of Alexandria was the daughter of King Costus—that is, a Prince—and thus in the Gospel, of a certain...

...just as the Lord heals the son of a certain petty king, so in the Old Testament, Joshua killed 30 kings of the land of Canaan in a single battle—a land which is otherwise very small and does not constitute a full kingdom. <note>original Latin: "dam reguli filium sanat Dominus, sic in veteri Testamento 30. Reges terræ Chanaam, quæ alioquin est perexigua, nec iustum Regnum conficit vna acie peremit Iosue."</note>

The same Génébrard <note>Gilbert Génébrard (1535–1597), a French scholar</note> in book 4 of his said *Chronography* [writes]: *In India there was a certain great Christian King; the Land of Caghat, from whence the three Kings came to Bethlehem, was still entirely Christian, but under the lordship of the Khan*, in the year of Salvation 1253. *The Constable of Armenia, to the King of Cyprus, cited in Vincent of Beauvais, book 31, chapter 92.* The voyages and navigations of the Portuguese and Spanish report that Pêro da Covilhã and Afonso de Paiva <note>original: "Pierre Couillane, & Alphonse Pauia"</note> were the first European ambassadors who were sent on behalf of Emmanuel, King of Portugal, to Ethiopia toward this great Emperor around the year 1496 or 1497.

Dom Francisco Álvares, Portuguese by nation, in his travels in Ethiopia writes that the Ethiopian Annals—composed in the Ethiopian, Indian, Nubian, and Abyssinian languages, formerly taken from Hebrew and Chaldean <note>In this period, "Chaldean" often referred to Syriac or Ge'ez (Ethiopic)</note>, and seen by him in Axum <note>original: "Caxumo"</note>, the principal city of Ethiopia—record that the Queen of Sheba <note>original: "Saba"</note>, who came from Meroë to see this great King Solomon in the city of Jerusalem, was named in her own name Makeda, though others call her Nicaula. They say she had a son by the said Solomon named Melic <note>Menelik I</note>, and later David, whom she made and established as her heir of Ethiopia, from whom is descended the lineage of the Kings of the great Ethiopian Empire. This is confirmed by Marinus Victorinus in his discourse on the Kings of Ethiopia, Andrea Corsali in his letter to Duke Lorenzo de' Medici, and Guillaume Postel in his *Alphabet of the Twelve Languages* and in his work on the distinguished nations who took their names and titles from Noah and his children. For this reason, all Ethiopian Kings have held the memory of Solomon in very great reverence, sending offerings every year to the temple in Jerusalem, as children of the house of David and instructed in the Law of Moses. They take this from the New Testament, speaking of the Eunuch <note>The Ethiopian Eunuch from Acts 8:26-40</note> sent to Judea in the time of the Apostles, who was baptized by Philip, one of the seven deacons, and first planted the Christian religion in Ethiopia.

As for this word "Prester John," "Prestian," "Prestan," or "Prestegia"—a common and familiar name for all Kings of Ethiopia—Paolo Giovio, in the first book of his *Elogies*, maintains that it is corrupted among us, and that the true name of the Kings of this province is *Belulgiam*, which was common to all the kings of this country, meaning "Pearl of great price and incomparable excellence." This is confirmed by Guy Le Fèvre de La Boderie in his preface to the Syriac New Testament, noting that the Ethiopians call this King and Lord *Ian Belul*, or *Ian Encoe* in the Chaldean language, which means "Precious" or "High"; or as Jean Bodin writes in his *Method for the Easy Comprehension of History*, chapter 5, *Iochan Belul*, meaning "most precious stone." Some modern authors maintain that Saint Thomas the Apostle, according to what is written in the Acts of the Apostles, went to preach in Greater India, where he died and left behind such a great multitude of people converted to the faith of Jesus Christ that, having elected a Lord to govern them, they gave him this name of "Prester John"—both because all the Lords were clerics <term>clergymen: implying they held both religious and secular authority</term> and because they had this name "John" in common since the first one who was elected, who was so named. This is confirmed by André Thevet in Book 11, Chapter 28 of his *Cosmography*.

Several other details worthy of remark and consideration are treated regarding this great Emperor or King *Prester John* <note>original: "Prestegian"</note> in *John Mandeville* in his travels, the chapter on *Prester John* and his state; *Alvise Cadamosto* in part 2 of his navigations, chapter 60; *Marco Polo the Venetian* in Book 3, chapter 38 of his travels; *Francisco Álvares* in his travels in Ethiopia; *Damião de Góis*, a Portuguese, in his treatise on the faith, religion, and customs of the Ethiopians under the Empire of this *Prester John*; *André Thevet* in Book 2, chapters 13 and 14 of his *Cosmography*; *Joseph Scaliger* in Book 7 of *The Improvement of Time*, in the chapter of annotations on the Ethiopian Calendar; *Antoine du Verdier* in Book 2, chapter 1 of his *Diverse Lessons*; *Juan de Torquemada*, a Spaniard, on the second day of his *Hexameron*; *François de Belleforest* in Book 1, chapter 4 of his *Universal History*, and Book 6, chapters 22 and 23 of volume 2 of his *Cosmography*; *Abraham Ortelius* in tables 4 and 47 of his *Theatre of the World*; *Louis Le Roy* in Book 9 of the *Vicissitude of Things*; the author of the *Political Treasury*, Book 2, in the chapter on the great King of Ethiopia; and *Blaise de Vigenère* in his treatise on ciphers.

The dominion of this great Emperor or King extends in Africa from one Tropic to the other, reaching a span of 50 or 52 degrees of latitude, which makes more than a thousand leagues of travel. Its length is from the east to the west: namely, from the Red Sea, at the place where Suakin and Massawa are located, unto the Atlantic Ocean. That is to say, Egypt lies to his north and the northern regions, and neighbors him toward Nubia—so named in the Hebrew language *Nubiah*, meaning "Sprout of God" <note>original: "Germe de Dieu"</note>, because the faith was germinated in the body of the Ethiopian Eunuch, and later through Candace, Queen of Ethiopia, according to *Guy Lefèvre de la Boderie* <note>A French poet and Orientalist</note> on folio 24. To the east of him is the Red Sea and part of the Indian Ocean, and the gulf named the *Barbarian Gulf*, reaching to the lands of *Malindi* and *Benamate* <note>likely referring to the Mutapa Empire</note>, which were unknown to ancient authors. To the south, it faces the Mountains of the Moon, which serve as a fence and wall on that side, or rather the Cape of Good Hope. To the west, it has for its borders and limits the River Niger (or Senegal) and the kingdoms of Nubia and *Manicongo* <note>The Kingdom of Kongo</note>, as confirmed by *Abraham Ortelius* in table 4 of his *Theatre of the Universe*.

Of the kingdoms and provinces that are under the said domination of this great Emperor or King, the titles and headings of his letters patent sent to Popes *Leo* the Tenth and *Clement* the Seventh, and to the King of Portugal—included in the travels of *Álvares* mentioned above, and translated into Latin by *Damião de Góis*, a Portuguese knight, in his discourse on the faith, religion, and customs of the Ethiopians—give ample proof and demonstration. They state that this Emperor or King is:

Emperor of Great and Upper *Ethiopia*, and of very great kingdoms, jurisdictions, and lands; King of *Goa*, *Cafates*, *Fatagar*, *Angote*, *Baru*, *Balignanzar*, *Adée*, *Vanga*, *Gojam* (where the sources and fountains of the *Nile* are located), *Amhara*, *Begemder*, *Ambée*, *Vangussi*, *Tigray* <note>original: "Tigremahon"</note>, *Sabaim*, *Saba*, *Bahr Negash* <note>original: "Barnagas"</note>, and Lord as far as *Nubia*, which extends to the land of *Egypt*.

Joachim the Abbot <note>Joachim of Fiore, c. 1135–1202, a mystic and theologian known for his apocalyptic theories</note>, in his *Appendix on Christian Nations*, wrote the following regarding Christians:

The nations of Christians are divided into ten nations, namely: the Latins, Greeks, Indians, Jacobites, Nestorians, Maronites, Armenians, Georgians, Syrians, and Mozarabs <note>Iberian Christians who lived under Muslim rule</note>.

The first nation is that of the Latins, who have the Emperor of Germany and many Kings, namely: the Kings of Castile, Aragon, Spain, Portugal, Navarre, etc. In the French nation, there is one King of the Franks, and many Dukes, Counts, and Barons. In the nation of Italy, however, there is the Pope, the King of Sicily and Naples, many Dukes, Counts, Marquises, and great communities <note>original: "comunitates magnæ," referring to the independent City-States or Republics</note>, namely: Venice, Lucca, Siena, and others. In the German nation, besides the Emperor, who must be Christian, there are many Kings, namely: the King of England, Scotland, Hungary, Bohemia, Poland, Denmark <note>original: "Daciæ," a common medieval Latin term for Denmark</note>, Frisia, Sweden, Norway, Dalmatia, and many Marquises, Landgraves, Dukes, and Counts; likewise the King of Cyprus, and the inhabitants of the island of Malta <note>original: "Meltidis"</note> and other islands obedient to the Roman Church.

The second nation is that of the Greeks, who formerly had the Patriarch of Constantinople, Archbishops, Bishops, Abbots, etc., in spiritual matters, but in temporal matters an Emperor, Dukes, and Counts, etc. They are now few in number, however, because the Saracens <note>original: "Agareni," literally "descendants of Hagar"</note> and Turks have occupied and invaded the greatest part of Greece. These do not obey the Roman Church and hold many errors which are condemned by the Church, because they say that the Holy Spirit does not proceed from the Son, but from the Father alone <note>The "Filioque" controversy, a primary cause of the Great Schism between East and West</note>; they also say there is no Purgatory.

The third nation is that of the Indians, whose Prince is Prester John <note>original: "Preste-Ian"</note>, whose power exceeds all Christians: for he has under him seventy-two Kings, and when the said King and Lord Prester John rides, he always has a wooden cross carried before him. When he goes to war, he has twelve crosses made of gold and precious stones carried as banners. In his land is the body of the blessed Apostle Thomas, held in greatest veneration; others say, on the contrary, that the body of this saint is in the East Indies.

The fourth nation is that of the Jacobites <note>A Monophysite Christian sect, today primarily the Syriac Orthodox Church</note>; so named after Jacob the Heretic <note>Jacob Baradaeus</note>, a disciple of the Patriarch of Alexandria. These occupy a large part of Asia in the East, the land of Mambrae which is near Egypt, and the land of Ethiopia, encompassing more than forty kingdoms. These are circumcised and baptized with a hot iron, branding the mark of the cross on their foreheads and other parts of the body, such as the chest or arms. These confess to God alone and not to the priests <note>The text mentions "Indæorum," likely a typo for "Iudæorum" (Jews) or "Indorum" (Indians)</note> or Saracens, and they say there is only a divine nature in Christ <note>This refers to the Monophysite belief that Christ has one nature, rather than being both fully human and fully divine</note>. Some of them speak the Chaldaic language <note>Syriac or Aramaic</note>, some the Arabic language, and others indeed speak other languages according to the diversity...

# History of the Origin of Nations

nations, and these were condemned in the Council of Chalcedon <note>original: "Cedensi." The Council of Chalcedon (451 AD) condemned the Miaphysite doctrine often associated with the Jacobite or Coptic churches mentioned on the previous page.</note>.

The **fifth nation** is that of the **Nestorians**, named after the heretic Nestorius <note>original: "Nestorino"</note> who was the Bishop of Constantinople. These alone posit two persons in Christ: one divine, and the other human. They deny that the Blessed Virgin Mary is the Mother of God, but claim she is only the mother of the man Jesus. They use the Chaldean <note>referring to Syriac or Aramaic</note> language in their scriptures and consecrate the body of Christ using leavened bread. They inhabit Tartary <note>Central and North Asia</note> and Greater India, and they are many in number. Their land is as vast as Germany and Italy combined. These are the heretics who were condemned in the third Synod of Ephesus; they were divided from the Roman Church and have remained in their stubbornness.

The **sixth nation** is that of the **Maronites**. The Maronites are named after a certain heretic called Maron; they posit only one intellect and one will in Christ <note>the heresy of Monothelitism</note>. They live near Libya in the province of Phoenicia <note>modern-day Lebanon</note> in great numbers. They are warrior men, well-taught and experienced in battle, especially skilled in the use of bows and arrows. Following the custom of the Latins, they use bells, and their Bishops use rings, mitres, and pastoral staves. In their scriptures, they use the Chaldean script, but in common speech, they use the Arabic language. At one time, they were under the obedience of the Roman Church, for their Patriarch took part in the General Lateran Council held in Rome under Innocent III; but afterward, they withdrew from the Roman Church. They were first condemned in the Synod of Constantinople, and later they came into obedience with the Roman Church, but then they returned again to their own opinion, in which they persevere to this day.

The **seventh nation** is that of the **Armenians**, who live in the kingdom of Armenia near Antioch. They have their own idiom and a language common to all; they sing the Holy Scriptures and the office of the Church in the vernacular language so that they may be understood by all laypeople, both men and women. They have their own Primate whom they call the **Catholicos**, whom they obey with great devotion and reverence, just as we obey the Pope. They fast during Lent with great devotion, during which they do not eat fish nor drink wine. However, on Fridays, they eat meat.

The **eighth nation** is that of the **Georgians**, named after Saint George, whom they hold as their Patron in battles. They live in eastern parts and are a beautiful, strong, and refined people. They are greatly feared by the Medes, Persians, and Syrians, on whose borders they dwell. They use the Greek language and perform the sacraments after the manner of the Greeks. The clerics have round tonsures <note>original: "coronas," the shaved circle on a priest's head</note> on their heads, while the laymen have square ones. When they come to the Holy Sepulchre, they do not pay tribute to the Saracens <note>medieval term for Muslims</note>, and they enter Jerusalem with banners held high because the Saracens fear them. Their women use arms just like the men; they even have beards and hair like the men <note>a medieval trope regarding the "Amazon-like" fierceness of Caucasian women</note> and wear high hats on their heads, a cubit in height. When they write to the Sultan, whatever they ask for is immediately granted to them.

The **ninth nation** is that of the **Syrians** <note>original: "Surianorũ"</note>, so called after the city of Tyre <note>original: "Sur"</note>, which is the most eminent city in Syria or Assyria. In common speech, they use the Saracen <note>Arabic</note> language, but in divine scriptures and the offices of the Mass, they use the Greek language. They have Bishops and observe the customs of the Greeks, obeying them in all things; they consecrate with leavened bread and hold the opinions of the Greeks against the Latins. They are followed by certain Christians who are called Samaritans in the Holy Land, who were first converted in the time of the Apostles, but they are not well-versed in the Catholic faith.

### Languages of this World

The **tenth nation** is that of the **Mozarabs**. Formerly, these Mozarabs were many in parts of Africa and Spain, but now they are few. They are called Mozarabs because they maintained many of the customs <note>original: "modos"</note> of the Christians from Arabia. In their divine services, they use the Latin language and obey the Roman Church and Latin prelates. They consecrate the host using unleavened bread <term>unleavened bread: bread made without yeast, as used in the Latin Rite</term> like the Latins do, yet they differ from the Latins in many ways. For although the natural day is divided into twenty-four hours of day and night, they have as many daily offices—including specific hours, psalms, hymns, and certain prayers—which are exceedingly long and are not recited in the Latin manner. For what the Latins say at the beginning, they say at the end or in the middle. Some divide the Sacrament of the Eucharist into seven parts, others into ten. This is a very devout nation; in marriage, they join only with persons of their own people or nation. Among them, if a woman loses her first husband, she never marries another but remains in perpetual chastity. The causes for such great diversity or division among Christians were, firstly, that from ancient times, Christians were restricted from celebrating general councils; thus, when heretics arose in various parts of the world, there was no one to apply a remedy. The second cause was the negligence of the Supreme Pontiffs, because they did not take care to send messengers to Christians living in error; had they done so, they might have led many or all back to the one faith and obedience of the Roman Church.

Barthélemy de Chasseneuz <note>a famous 16th-century French jurist known for his work "Catalogus Gloriae Mundi"</note>, in the 12th part of his catalog, *The Glory of the World*, consideration 22, writes the following: Regarding the Christian sects, there are thirteen nations holding that faith, and there are four which are categorized under the Latins, for principally all Latins are Christians. Within the Latin nation, there are four other specific nations: namely, the **French**, **German**, **Italian**, and **Spanish** nations. But there is one that has held and holds the faith without "monsters" <note>referring here to theological aberrations or heresies</note> or any error, and without deviation because it has never withdrawn from the faith or strayed in any point; this is the **French nation**, which has always lacked such monsters and has always defended, helped, protected, and increased the Catholic faith, fighting for it with all its strength against almost all other nations. In this first nation, the French, the King of France is the principal figure, who is called the **Most Christian King** <note>original: "Christianissimus"</note> among all the kings of the world. Under him are many dukes, counts, marquises, and barons obedient to him, as well as the King of Navarre and the King of Yvetot <note>a small, ancient sovereign principality in Normandy</note>, although some say the kingdom of Navarre falls under the Spanish nation. 

The **second nation** is the **Italian**, in which resides the principal head of all Christendom, who is the Pope. He holds primacy and leadership over the entire Church and the Christian sect, and all obey him, or are bound to obey. In that nation are the King of Sicily, the King of Naples, the Duchy of Venice, the Dukes of Milan, Ferrara, and Urbino, and the Marquises of Mantua and Montferrat, and many other counts, principalities, and dominions such as those of Florence, Siena, and Genoa. 

The **third nation** is the **Spanish**, in which are the Kings of Castile, León, Granada, Aragon, and Portugal, along with many dukes and counts; the principal kingdom is called Castile and Spain, whose king is called the **Catholic King** <note>original: "Rex Catholicus"</note>. 

The **fourth nation** is that of the **Germans**, or the **Germanic nation**, in which is the Emperor. There are many kings, such as the King of England, Scotland, Hungary, Bohemia, Poland, Denmark <note>original: "Dacia," a common Latin term for Denmark in the Middle Ages</note>, Frisia, Sweden, Norway, Dalmatia, and Croatia, along with many landgraves, dukes, and counts. Likewise, the King of Cyprus on the island of Cyprus. All the aforementioned are obedient to the Roman Church, although many...
